1.39.s: yaḥ prāṇināṃ jīvayan khāni sevate śivo bhūtvā mātariśvā rasāgrabhuk | dhvajo 'ntarikṣasya sa sarvabhūtabhṛd vāyur devaḥ svātinā no 'bhirakṣatu ||
1.39.d: यः प्राणिनां जीवयन् खानि सेवते शिवो भूत्वा मातरिश्वा रसाग्रभुक् । ध्वजो ऽन्तरिक्षस्य स सर्वभूतभृद् वायुर् देवः स्वातिना नो ऽभिरक्षतु ॥
1.39.m: He who, animating the bodily apertures of living beings, attends [upon them], having become auspicious, Mātariśvan who enjoys the best of essences, / the banner of the atmosphere, sustaining all beings—may that god Vāyu protect us with Svāti.

1.39.s: yāv īḍitāv ātmavidbhir maṇīṣibhiḥ sahitau yau trīṇi savanāni sāmagau | indrāgnī varadau namaskṛtau viśākhayoḥ kurvatām āyuṣe śrīḥ ||
1.39.d: याव् ईडिताव् आत्मविद्भिर् मणीषिभिः सहितौ यौ त्रीणि सवनानि सामगौ । इन्द्राग्नी वरदौ नमस्कृतौ विशाखयोः कुर्वताम् आयुषे श्रीः ॥
1.39.m: The two praised by sages knowing the self, together chanting the Sāmans at the three pressings, / may Indra and Agni, granters of boons, venerated, bring forth fortune for long life under the two Viśākhās.

1.39.s: viśve devā yam ṛṣim āhur mitraṃ bharadvājam ṛṣitaḥ prasāmavit | taṃ jagatyā gāthayā staumy ugraiḥ sa mām anūrādhābhir bhṛtakaṇvo 'bhirakṣatu ||
1.39.d: विश्वे देवा यम् ऋषिम् आहुर् मित्रं भरद्वाजम् ऋषितः प्रसामवित् । तं जगत्या गाथया स्तौम्य् उग्रैः स माम् अनूराधाभिर् भृतकण्वो ऽभिरक्षतु ॥
1.39.m: The sage whom the All-gods call Mitra, from Bharadvāja the sage, knower of melodies: / him I praise with a song in the jagatī [metre] by fierce [chants]; may he protect me with the Anurādhās.

1.40.s: śatakratur yo nijaghāna śambaraṃ vṛtraṃ ca hatvā saritaḥ prasarjataḥ | sa naḥ stutaḥ prītamanāḥ puraṃdaro marutsakhā jyeṣṭhayā no 'bhirakṣatu ||
1.40.d: शतक्रतुर् यो निजघान शम्बरं वृत्रं च हत्वा सरितः प्रसर्जतः । स नः स्तुतः प्रीतमनाः पुरंदरो मरुत्सखा ज्येष्ठया नो ऽभिरक्षतु ॥
1.40.m: He of a hundred rites who struck down Śambara, and having slain Vṛtra released the rivers, / may he, praised, pleased in mind, the breaker of strongholds, friend of the Maruts, protect us with Jyeṣṭhā.

1.40.s: yā dhārayaty ojasātidevapadaṃ mātā pṛthivī ca sā sarvabhūtabhṛt | sā naḥ stutā kṛṇutāṃ karmasiddhaye mūlaṃ devī nirṛtiḥ sarvakarmasu ||
1.40.d: या धारयत्य् ओजसातिदेवपदं माता पृथिवी च सा सर्वभूतभृत् । सा नः स्तुता कृणुतां कर्मसिद्धये मूलं देवी निरृतिः सर्वकर्मसु ॥
1.40.m: She who by her might upholds the station surpassing the gods, and she, Mother Earth, sustainer of all beings: / may that praised goddess Nirṛti make Mūla [favourable] for us in all rites, for the accomplishment of our rite.

1.40.s: parjanyasṛṣṭās tisṛṇībhir āvṛtaṃ yās tarpayanty abhitaḥ pravṛddhaye | tāḥ staumy āpo vāruṇīḥ … pūrvā āṣāḍhā svadhayāstu yojane ||
1.40.d: पर्जन्यसृष्टास् तिसृणीभिर् आवृतं यास् तर्पयन्त्य् अभितः प्रवृद्धये । ताः स्तौम्य् आपो वारुणीः … पूर्वा आषाढा स्वधयास्तु योजने ॥
1.40.m: Sent forth by Parjanya, which satisfy [the earth] all around with streams for growth, / those waters belonging to Varuṇa I praise [...]; may Pūrvā Aṣāḍhā be [joined] with svadhā in conjunction.

1.40.s: yās triṃśataṃ trīṃś ca madanti devā devanāmno nirmitāṃś ca bhūyasaḥ | tā no 'ṣāḍhā uttarā vaso viśve śivāḥ kriyāḥ kṛṇutāṃ suramatāḥ ||
1.40.d: यास् त्रिंशतं त्रींश् च मदन्ति देवा देवनाम्नो निर्मितांश् च भूयसः । ता नो ऽषाढा उत्तरा वसो विश्वे शिवाः क्रियाः कृणुतां सुरमताः ॥
1.40.m: In whom the three and thirty gods rejoice, and many beings fashioned bearing the names of gods: / may those Uttarā Aṣāḍhās, O Vasus, All[-gods], approved by the gods, make our rites auspicious.

1.40.s: yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvakṛt sarvabhūtabhṛd yasmād anyan na paraṃ kiṃ canāsti | anirmitaḥ satyajitaḥ puruṣṭutaḥ sa no brahmābhijitā no 'bhirakṣatu ||
1.40.d: यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वकृत् सर्वभूतभृद् यस्माद् अन्यन् न परं किं चनास्ति । अनिर्मितः सत्यजितः पुरुष्टुतः स नो ब्रह्माभिजिता नो ऽभिरक्षतु ॥
1.40.m: He who is all-knowing, all-making, sustaining all beings, beyond whom there is nothing else higher, / unfashioned, victorious in truth, much-praised: may that Brahmā protect us with Abhijit.

1.41.s: sthānācyute sthānam indrāya pātave devebhyaś ca ya īrayaṃs trir vicakrame | taṃ svid dhi svargaṃ nākapṛṣṭhaṃ viśvaṃ viṣṇur devaḥ śravaṇenābhirakṣatu ||
1.41.d: स्थानाच्युते स्थानम् इन्द्राय पातवे देवेभ्यश् च य ईरयंस् त्रिर् विचक्रमे । तं स्विद् धि स्वर्गं नाकपृष्ठं विश्वं विष्णुर् देवः श्रवणेनाभिरक्षतु ॥
1.41.m: He who strode [three times], sending forth a place for Indra and the gods to rule, without falling from his place, / indeed to that heaven, the vault of the sky, the universe—may the god Viṣṇu protect [us] with Śravaṇa.

1.41.s: aṣṭau śatāni śvetaketūnāṃ yāni tvaṃ ca sa tvaṃ nijaghāna bhūyasaḥ | anādeśenobhayataś ca vīḍitāḥ śraviṣṭhābhir no 'bhirakṣantu vājinaḥ ||
1.41.d: अष्टौ शतानि श्वेतकेतूनां यानि त्वं च स त्वं निजघान भूयसः । अनादेशेनोभयतश् च वीडिताः श्रविष्ठाभिर् नो ऽभिरक्षन्तु वाजिनः ॥
1.41.m: The eight hundred white comets, which you, even you, struck down in great numbers, / strengthened on both sides without command: may the horses protect us with the Śraviṣṭhās.

1.41.s: vājā devī devamṛṇānikākubhāv ubhāv ājasya natakarmaṇā śivā | tava vrājaṃ staumasi devabhojanau pratyagbhiṣak śatabhiṣak śivau naḥ ||
1.41.d: वाजा देवी देवमृणानिकाकुभाव् उभाव् आजस्य नतकर्मणा शिवा । तव व्राजं स्तौमसि देवभोजनौ प्रत्यग्भिषक् शतभिषक् शिवौ नः ॥
1.41.m: The divine Vājas, the summits of the divine debt, both auspicious through the humble deed of goat-milk; / we praise your pen, you two who feast the gods, the inward healer: may Śatabhiṣaj be auspicious to us.

1.41.s: śunāsīrau naḥ pramumūtu jihmasau tautau pitṛbhyo dadatuḥ stanau śubhau | tau pūrvajau kṛṇutām ekapād ajaḥ pratiṣṭhānau sarvakāmābhayāya ca ||
1.41.d: शुनासीरौ नः प्रमुमूतु जिह्मसौ तौतौ पितृभ्यो ददतुः स्तनौ शुभौ । तौ पूर्वजौ कृणुताम् एकपाद् अजः प्रतिष्ठानौ सर्वकामाभयाय च ॥
1.41.m: May Śunā and Sīra loosen for us what is crooked; may those two grant their two fair breasts to the ancestors; / may those firstborn two, Aja Ekapād, make the two foundations for all desires and freedom from fear.

1.41.s: sarvārthāya kṛṇomi karmasiddhaye gaviṣṭutāyānekakāriṇe namaḥ | so 'hir budhnyaḥ kṛṇutām uttarau śivau pratiṣṭhānau sarvakāmābhayāya ca ||
1.41.d: सर्वार्थाय कृणोमि कर्मसिद्धये गविष्टुतायानेककारिणे नमः । सो ऽहिर् बुध्न्यः कृणुताम् उत्तरौ शिवौ प्रतिष्ठानौ सर्वकामाभयाय च ॥

1.41.s: yaṃ mahāhemam ṛṣitaḥ prasāmavid bharadvājaś candramasau divākaram | sajuṣṭānām aśvayujau bhayāya ca sa naḥ pūṣā kṛṇutāṃ revatīṃ śivām ||
1.41.d: यं महाहेमम् ऋषितः प्रसामविद् भरद्वाजश् चन्द्रमसौ दिवाकरम् । सजुष्टानाम् अश्वयुजौ भयाय च स नः पूषा कृणुतां रेवतीं शिवाम् ॥
1.41.m: Whom from Bharadvāja the sage, knowing melodies, the great golden one, the moon, the sun / of those united; and for fear of the two Aśvayuj; may that Pūṣan make Revatī auspicious for us.

1.41.s: jīrṇaṃ santaṃ yau yuvānaṃ hi cakratur ṛṣiṃ dhiyā cyavanaṃ somapau kṛtau | tau naś cittibhir bhiṣajām asya satkarau … prajām aśvinyām aśvinau śivau ||
1.41.d: जीर्णं सन्तं यौ युवानं हि चक्रतुर् ऋषिं धिया च्यवनं सोमपौ कृतौ । तौ नश् चित्तिभिर् भिषजाम् अस्य सत्करौ … प्रजाम् अश्विन्याम् अश्विनौ शिवौ ॥
1.41.m: The two who made the sage Cyavana young when he was aged, by wisdom, and were made soma-drinkers: / may those two auspicious Aśvins, healers who honour this [worshipper], [...] offspring under Aśvinī with insights.

1.41.s: yasya śyāmaśabalau rakṣataḥ svadhā duṣkṛt sukṛd vividhā carṣaṇīdhṛtau | tau savitryā ca savitur dharmacāribhir yamo rājā bharaṇībhir no 'bhirakṣatu ||
1.41.d: यस्य श्यामशबलौ रक्षतः स्वधा दुष्कृत् सुकृद् विविधा चर्षणीधृतौ । तौ सवित्र्या च सवितुर् धर्मचारिभिर् यमो राजा भरणीभिर् नो ऽभिरक्षतु ॥
1.41.m: Whose two dogs, dark and spotted, guard the svadhā, the evil-doer and the good-doer, diverse, sustaining people: / may King Yama, with Sāvitrī and the followers of Savitṛ's law, protect us with the Bharaṇīs.

1.42.s: atha nakṣatrasnānānāṃ vidhiṃ vakṣyāmi sāṃpadam | grahadaivatapūjāṃ ca yeṣu yatra yathāvidhi ||
1.42.d: अथ नक्षत्रस्नानानां विधिं वक्ष्यामि सांपदम् । ग्रहदैवतपूजां च येषु यत्र यथाविधि ॥
1.42.m: Now I shall declare the rite of lunar-mansion baths that brings prosperity, / and the worship of the planets and deities, during which, where, and according to rule.

1.42.s: nakṣatrayogakālajñaḥ kṛtvā tantraṃ yathāvidhi | yajed grahān haviṣyeṇa yathoktena ca devatāḥ ||
1.42.d: नक्षत्रयोगकालज्ञः कृत्वा तन्त्रं यथाविधि । यजेद् ग्रहान् हविष्येण यथोक्तेन च देवताः ॥
1.42.m: Knowing the times of conjunction of the lunar mansions, having performed the procedure according to rule, / one should worship the planets with sacrificial food and the deities as prescribed.

1.42.s: praśastalakṣaṇaṃ kumbhaṃ sasaṃbhārajalaṃ budhaḥ | saṃpātābhihitaṃ kṛtvā mantrair vidhim anusmaran ||
1.42.d: प्रशस्तलक्षणं कुम्भं ससंभारजलं बुधः । संपाताभिहितं कृत्वा मन्त्रैर् विधिम् अनुस्मरन् ॥
1.42.m: The wise man, having prepared a jar of auspicious marks, containing water and ritual accessories, / consecrated by the remnants of the oblation, with mantras, mindful of the rule,

1.42.s: sāvitryā śāntisūktaiś ca mahāvyāhṛtibhis tathā | apāṃ stotraiḥ pavitraiś ca nakṣatrastutibhis tathā ||
1.42.d: सावित्र्या शान्तिसूक्तैश् च महाव्याहृतिभिस् तथा । अपां स्तोत्रैः पवित्रैश् च नक्षत्रस्तुतिभिस् तथा ॥
1.42.m: with the Sāvitrī, with the peace-hymns, and with the great mystical utterances, / with hymns to the waters, purifying hymns, and praises of the lunar mansions,

1.42.s: nakṣatradaivatān mantrān pratinakṣatram āvapet | kāmyāṃś caivāvapen mantrān karmaliṅgavidhānavit ||
1.42.d: नक्षत्रदैवतान् मन्त्रान् प्रतिनक्षत्रम् आवपेत् । काम्यांश् चैवावपेन् मन्त्रान् कर्मलिङ्गविधानवित् ॥
1.42.m: should insert the mantras belonging to the deities of the lunar mansions, lunar mansion by lunar mansion, / and he who knows the rules on the characteristic marks of rites should also insert desire-prompted mantras.

1.42.s: saṃpātyāthābhimantrya vā nakṣatrasnānakovidaḥ | snāpayed arthinaṃ vāgbhiḥ puṇyābhir abhimantritam ||
1.42.d: संपात्याथाभिमन्त्र्य वा नक्षत्रस्नानकोविदः । स्नापयेद् अर्थिनं वाग्भिः पुण्याभिर् अभिमन्त्रितम् ॥
1.42.m: Having poured remnants of the oblation or having consecrated [the jar], he who is skilled in lunar-mansion baths / should bathe the petitioner, consecrated with auspicious words.

1.42.s: eṣa eva vidhir dṛṣṭaḥ sadasyebhyaś ca dakṣiṇā | pūrvam āpyāyayed dehaṃ paścād dadyāt tu dakṣiṇām ||
1.42.d: एष एव विधिर् दृष्टः सदस्येभ्यश् च दक्षिणा । पूर्वम् आप्याययेद् देहं पश्चाद् दद्यात् तु दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.42.m: Just this is the observed rule, and a sacrificial fee to the members of the assembly: / first one should refresh the body, and afterwards give the sacrificial fee.

1.42.s: anena vidhinā snātvā dadyāc caivātra dakṣiṇām | prāpnoty anunayaṃ puṃsaḥ sa vedaphalam aśnute ||
1.42.d: अनेन विधिना स्नात्वा दद्याच् चैवात्र दक्षिणाम् । प्राप्नोत्य् अनुनयं पुंसः स वेदफलम् अश्नुते ॥
1.42.m: Having bathed according to this rule, one should give a sacrificial fee here; / he attains the favour of the man, and he enjoys the fruit of the Veda.

1.42.s: ātmānaṃ nirmalīkṛtya devān iṣṭvā grahāṃs tathā | vidvadbhyo dakṣiṇā deyā dvijān annena tarpayet ||
1.42.d: आत्मानं निर्मलीकृत्य देवान् इष्ट्वा ग्रहांस् तथा । विद्वद्भ्यो दक्षिणा देया द्विजान् अन्नेन तर्पयेत् ॥
1.42.m: Having purified oneself, and having worshipped the gods and likewise the planets, / a sacrificial fee should be given to the learned, and one should satisfy the twice-born with food.

1.43.s: kṛttikābhiḥ śirīṣasya aśvatthasya vaṭasya ca | snāpayet pattrabhaṅgena ya icched rājapūjitam ||
1.43.d: कृत्तिकाभिः शिरीषस्य अश्वत्थस्य वटस्य च । स्नापयेत् पत्त्रभङ्गेन य इच्छेद् राजपूजितम् ॥
1.43.m: Under Kṛttikā, he who desires to be honoured by the king / should bathe with crushed leaves of the śirīṣa, the aśvattha, and the banyan.

1.43.s: rohiṇyāṃ snāpayed vaiśyaṃ sarvabījair alaṃkṛtam | akṣatān antaraṃ kṛtvā tathā saubhāgyam arhati ||
1.43.d: रोहिण्यां स्नापयेद् वैश्यं सर्वबीजैर् अलंकृतम् । अक्षतान् अन्तरं कृत्वा तथा सौभाग्यम् अर्हति ॥
1.43.m: Under Rohiṇī, one should bathe a vaiśya adorned with all seeds, / putting unbroken grains in between; thus he attains good fortune.

1.43.s: yadā mṛgaśiro yujyet tadā snānaṃ vidhīyate | muktāmaṇisuvarṇena dhanārthī tena snāpayet ||
1.43.d: यदा मृगशिरो युज्येत् तदा स्नानं विधीयते । मुक्तामणिसुवर्णेन धनार्थी तेन स्नापयेत् ॥
1.43.m: When Mṛgaśiras is in conjunction, then a bath is prescribed; / one desiring wealth should bathe with pearls, gems, and gold.

1.43.s: śrīveṣṭakasarjarasatagarośīrapattrakaiḥ | ārdrāyāṃ vaṇijaḥ snātāḥ sulābhāṃs tu labhanti te ||
1.43.d: श्रीवेष्टकसर्जरसतगरोशीरपत्त्रकैः । आर्द्रायां वणिजः स्नाताः सुलाभांस् तु लभन्ति ते ॥
1.43.m: Merchants bathed under Ārdrā with turpentine, resin, tagara, uśīra, and pattraka / indeed obtain good profits.

1.43.s: punarvasubhyāṃ gomārgād āhared agramṛttikām | gopīṭhe snāpayed go 'rthī kṣipraṃ gomān bhaviṣyati ||
1.43.d: पुनर्वसुभ्यां गोमार्गाद् आहरेद् अग्रमृत्तिकाम् । गोपीठे स्नापयेद् गो ऽर्थी क्षिप्रं गोमान् भविष्यति ॥
1.43.m: Under the two Punarvasus, one should fetch top-soil from a cattle-path; / one desiring cattle should bathe on a cow-seat; he will quickly become possessed of cattle.

1.43.s: raktaśālisahasreṇa tāvadbhir gaurasarṣapaiḥ | sahasravīryānantyā ca madayantīpriyaṅgubhiḥ | trīn puṣyān brāhmaṇaḥ snātaḥ pārthivaṃ labhate yaśaḥ ||
1.43.d: रक्तशालिसहस्रेण तावद्भिर् गौरसर्षपैः । सहस्रवीर्यानन्त्या च मदयन्तीप्रियङ्गुभिः । त्रीन् पुष्यान् ब्राह्मणः स्नातः पार्थिवं लभते यशः ॥
1.43.m: With a thousand grains of red rice, as many white mustard seeds, / and sahasravīryā, anantā, madayantī, and priyaṅgu: / a brāhmaṇa bathed under three Puṣyas attains royal glory.

1.43.s: aśleṣāsv āhārayed ubhayataḥ kūlamṛttikāḥ | aśvārohaṃ snāpayet tena kṣipravāhī bhaviṣyati ||
1.43.d: अश्लेषास्व् आहारयेद् उभयतः कूलमृत्तिकाः । अश्वारोहं स्नापयेत् तेन क्षिप्रवाही भविष्यति ॥
1.43.m: Under Āśleṣā, one should procure soil from both banks [of a river]; / one should bathe a horseman with it; he will quickly become a good rider.

1.43.s: maghābhis tu tilaiḥ snāyād utpalaiḥ kamalais tathā | tasmiṃs tu māse sā kanyā kṣipraṃ ca labhate patim ||
1.43.d: मघाभिस् तु तिलैः स्नायाद् उत्पलैः कमलैस् तथा । तस्मिंस् तु मासे सा कन्या क्षिप्रं च लभते पतिम् ॥
1.43.m: Under the Maghās, one should bathe with sesame, with blue lotuses, and with red lotuses; / in that very month that maiden quickly obtains a husband.

1.43.s: atha pūrvayoḥ phalgunyoḥ śatapuṣpā priyaṅgavaḥ | madhv eva ca tṛtīyaṃ syāt saubhāgyaṃ bhogavardhanam ||
1.43.d: अथ पूर्वयोः फल्गुन्योः शतपुष्पा प्रियङ्गवः । मध्व् एव च तृतीयं स्यात् सौभाग्यं भोगवर्धनम् ॥
1.43.m: Now under the prior two Phalgunīs [there should be] dill, priyaṅgu mustard seeds, / and honey should be the third; it brings good fortune and increases enjoyment.

1.43.s: athottarayoḥ phalgunyor akṣatā gaurasarṣapāḥ | etat snānaṃ prayuñjīta prajāsthāpanam uttamam ||
1.43.d: अथोत्तरयोः फल्गुन्योर् अक्षता गौरसर्षपाः । एतत् स्नानं प्रयुञ्जीत प्रजास्थापनम् उत्तमम् ॥
1.43.m: Now under the latter two Phalgunīs [there should be] unbroken grains and white mustard seeds; / one should employ this bath, the supreme establisher of offspring.

1.44.s: hastena sarvakārūṇāṃ caurāṇāṃ cāpi nityaśaḥ | nadīgiritaṭākeṣu mṛttikāsnānam uttamam ||
1.44.d: हस्तेन सर्वकारूणां चौराणां चापि नित्यशः । नदीगिरितटाकेषु मृत्तिकास्नानम् उत्तमम् ॥
1.44.m: Under Hasta, for all artisans and also for thieves, / a mud-bath in rivers, mountains, and ponds is constantly best.

1.44.s: citrāyāṃ citramālyais tu sarvagandhair alaṃkṛtam | yoṣārthī snāpayet tena kṣipraṃ sa labhate priyām ||
1.44.d: चित्रायां चित्रमाल्यैस् तु सर्वगन्धैर् अलंकृतम् । योषार्थी स्नापयेत् तेन क्षिप्रं स लभते प्रियाम् ॥
1.44.m: Under Citrā, one desiring a woman should bathe [himself] adorned with varied garlands / and all perfumes; through this he quickly obtains a beloved [woman].

1.44.s: svātinā tu gandhaiḥ snāyād utpalaiḥ kumudais tathā | tasmiṃs tu māse sā kanyā kṣipraṃ nirvyūhyate tataḥ ||
1.44.d: स्वातिना तु गन्धैः स्नायाद् उत्पलैः कुमुदैस् तथा । तस्मिंस् तु मासे सा कन्या क्षिप्रं निर्व्यूह्यते ततः ॥
1.44.m: Under Svāti, however, she should bathe with perfumes, blue lotuses, and white water lilies; / then in that month that girl is quickly led away [in marriage].

1.44.s: khaḍgasya ca viṣāṇena gajasya ṛṣabhasya vā | viśākhābhyām abhiṣikto rājā pṛthivīm abhiśāsayet ||
1.44.d: खड्गस्य च विषाणेन गजस्य ऋषभस्य वा । विशाखाभ्याम् अभिषिक्तो राजा पृथिवीम् अभिशासयेत् ॥
1.44.m: With the horn of a rhinoceros, of an elephant, or of a bull, / a king consecrated under the two Viśākhās shall rule over the earth.

1.44.s: anūrādhāsv āhārayed valmīkaśatamṛttikāḥ | karṣaṇaṃ snāpayet tena dhanadhānyena vardhate ||
1.44.d: अनूराधास्व् आहारयेद् वल्मीकशतमृत्तिकाः । कर्षणं स्नापयेत् तेन धनधान्येन वर्धते ॥
1.44.m: Under the Anurādhās, one should fetch soil from a hundred anthills; / one should bathe a farmer with it; he increases in wealth and grain.

1.44.s: jyeṣṭhāyāṃ jyaiṣṭhyakāmaṃ tu abhiṣiñcet purohitam | rasaiś ca miśradhānyaiś cābhiṣiktaḥ prāśayed rasān ||
1.44.d: ज्येष्ठायां ज्यैष्ठ्यकामं तु अभिषिञ्चेत् पुरोहितम् । रसैश् च मिश्रधान्यैश् चाभिषिक्तः प्राशयेद् रसान् ॥
1.44.m: Under Jyeṣṭhā, however, one should consecrate a domestic priest who desires preeminence; / and consecrated with fluids and mixed grains, he should ingest the fluids.

1.44.s: mūlena sarvatobhadram upaviṣṭā varavarṇinī | śamīpattrasahasreṇa snānāt putraṃ prasūyate ||
1.44.d: मूलेन सर्वतोभद्रम् उपविष्टा वरवर्णिनी । शमीपत्त्रसहस्रेण स्नानात् पुत्रं प्रसूयते ॥
1.44.m: Under Mūla, a woman of fair complexion, seated upon a sarvatobhadra diagram, / gives birth to a son from a bath with a thousand śamī leaves.

1.44.s: atha pūrvāsv aṣāḍhāsu yā snāyād ahate paṭe | jātarūpeṇa kalyāṇī bhogaṃ bhuṅkte patipriyā ||
1.44.d: अथ पूर्वास्व् अषाढासु या स्नायाद् अहते पटे । जातरूपेण कल्याणी भोगं भुङ्क्ते पतिप्रिया ॥
1.44.m: Now, under the prior Aṣāḍhās, the auspicious woman, beloved of her husband, who bathes / wearing an unwashed garment with gold, enjoys pleasure.

1.44.s: athottarāsv aṣāḍhāsu yaḥ snāyāc ced upoṣitaḥ | mahāhrada uśīreṇa dāsīdāsena vardhate ||
1.44.d: अथोत्तरास्व् अषाढासु यः स्नायाच् चेद् उपोषितः । महाह्रद उशीरेण दासीदासेन वर्धते ॥
1.44.m: Now, under the latter Aṣāḍhās, if one who has fasted bathes / in a great pool with uśīra, he increases in female and male slaves.

1.44.s: vacayotpalakuṣṭhaiś ca brāhmī siddhārthakais tathā | abhijid brāhmaṇaḥ snātaḥ pārthivaṃ labhate yaśaḥ ||
1.44.d: वचयोत्पलकुष्ठैश् च ब्राह्मी सिद्धार्थकैस् तथा । अभिजिद् ब्राह्मणः स्नातः पार्थिवं लभते यशः ॥
1.44.m: With sweet flag, blue lotuses, and kuṣṭha, and likewise brāhmī and white mustard seeds: / a brāhmaṇa bathed under Abhijit attains royal renown.

1.45.s: śravaṇena sravantīnāṃ yaḥ snāyāt saṃgameṣu ca | sa saṃgacchati svarṇena hiraṇyena dhanena vā ||
1.45.d: श्रवणेन स्रवन्तीनां यः स्नायात् संगमेषु च । स संगच्छति स्वर्णेन हिरण्येन धनेन वा ॥
1.45.m: Under Śravaṇa, he who bathes at the confluences of streams / is united with gold, precious metal, or wealth.

1.45.s: śraviṣṭhābhir dhanakāmaṃ tu snāpayed yatra candanaiḥ | etat snānaṃ prayuñjāno dhanadhānyena vardhate ||
1.45.d: श्रविष्ठाभिर् धनकामं तु स्नापयेद् यत्र चन्दनैः । एतत् स्नानं प्रयुञ्जानो धनधान्येन वर्धते ॥
1.45.m: Under the Śraviṣṭhās, one should bathe one who desires wealth with sandalwood pastes; / employing this bath, he increases in wealth and grain.

1.45.s: śatabhiṣag bhiṣakkāmo 'bhiṣiñcec chāntikarmasu | so 'bhiṣikto hatapāpmā sarvarogaiḥ pramucyate ||
1.45.d: शतभिषग् भिषक्कामो ऽभिषिञ्चेच् छान्तिकर्मसु । सो ऽभिषिक्तो हतपाप्मा सर्वरोगैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
1.45.m: Under Śatabhiṣaj, one desiring to be a physician should consecrate [himself] in propitiatory rites; / consecrated, his evil destroyed, he is released from all diseases.

1.45.s: atha pūrvayoḥ proṣṭhapadayo rocanayāñjanena ca | snātā gajaviṣāṇena rājānaṃ janayet sutam ||
1.45.d: अथ पूर्वयोः प्रोष्ठपदयो रोचनयाञ्जनेन च । स्नाता गजविषाणेन राजानं जनयेत् सुतम् ॥
1.45.m: Now, under the prior two Proṣṭhapadās, [a woman] bathed with yellow orpiment, collyrium, / and [water from] an elephant's tusk shall give birth to a king as a son.

1.45.s: athottarayoḥ proṣṭhapadayoḥ prasannāpadmakaṃ madhu | gandharvaṃ snāpayet tena rājavāhī bhaviṣyati ||
1.45.d: अथोत्तरयोः प्रोष्ठपदयोः प्रसन्नापद्मकं मधु । गन्धर्वं स्नापयेत् तेन राजवाही भविष्यति ॥
1.45.m: Now, under the latter two Proṣṭhapadās, [there should be] clear liquor, padmaka wood, and honey; / one should bathe an equestrian with it; he will become a bearer of kings.

1.45.s: khaḍgasya ca viṣāṇena jalena madhusarpiṣā | revatyāṃ kṣatriyaḥ snāto rājā pṛthivīm abhiśāsate ||
1.45.d: खड्गस्य च विषाणेन जलेन मधुसर्पिषा । रेवत्यां क्षत्रियः स्नातो राजा पृथिवीम् अभिशासते ॥
1.45.m: With the horn of a rhinoceros, with water, honey, and clarified butter, / a kṣatriya king bathed under Revatī rules over the earth.

1.45.s: aśvinyāṃ svastikaṃ mālyaṃ madayantīpriyaṅgubhiḥ | rūpājīvāyās tat snānaṃ saubhāgyaṃ bhogavardhanam ||
1.45.d: अश्विन्यां स्वस्तिकं माल्यं मदयन्तीप्रियङ्गुभिः । रूपाजीवायास् तत् स्नानं सौभाग्यं भोगवर्धनम् ॥
1.45.m: Under Aśvinī, a garland shaped like a svastika, with henna and priyaṅgu: / that bath brings good fortune and increases enjoyment for a courtesan.

1.45.s: bharaṇībhir bhadramustais tv elāsiddharthakais tathā | snātā patikulaṃ gacched asapatnam akaṇṭakam ||
1.45.d: भरणीभिर् भद्रमुस्तैस् त्व् एलासिद्धर्थकैस् तथा । स्नाता पतिकुलं गच्छेद् असपत्नम् अकण्टकम् ॥
1.45.m: Under the Bharaṇīs, having bathed with nut grass, cardamom, and white mustard seeds, / she goes to her husband's family, free of rivals and free of obstacles.

1.46.s: sarvajñaḥ sarvaga śaṃsa nārada prajñānam anyasmād anūnaprajñāt svargasya lokasya dehādyairyāt pathibhir upapanno manuṣyaḥ ||
1.46.d: सर्वज्ञः सर्वग शंस नारद प्रज्ञानम् अन्यस्माद् अनूनप्रज्ञात् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य देहाद्यैर्यात् पथिभिर् उपपन्नो मनुष्यः ॥
1.46.m: Omniscient, all-pervading Nārada, declare the wisdom from that other [sage] of non-deficient wisdom, / endowed with paths by which a mortal goes from the body to the heavenly world!

1.46.s: upoṣitaḥ śuciśīlaḥ puṇyagandho yadā bhavet | prāg astaṃgamanabhojanād yad enaṃ nityam atandritaḥ ||
1.46.d: उपोषितः शुचिशीलः पुण्यगन्धो यदा भवेत् । प्राग् अस्तंगमनभोजनाद् यद् एनं नित्यम् अतन्द्रितः ॥
1.46.m: When, having fasted, pure in conduct, with a sacred scent, / before eating at sunset, he constantly and unweariedly [serves] this [path]:

1.46.s: samayācārapūrvābhiḥ karmasiddhiḥ praśasyate | taṃ kāmadughaṃ svargakāmaḥ paretya pratipadyate ||
1.46.d: समयाचारपूर्वाभिः कर्मसिद्धिः प्रशस्यते । तं कामदुघं स्वर्गकामः परेत्य प्रतिपद्यते ॥
1.46.m: Accomplishment of deeds is praised through [actions] preceded by conventional conduct; / desiring heaven, when deceased, he attains that wish-granting cow.

1.47.s: kṛttikābhiḥ pāyasaṃ sarpiṣā saha bhojayet | taṃ kāmadughaṃ svargakāmaḥ paretya pratipadyate ||
1.47.d: कृत्तिकाभिः पायसं सर्पिषा सह भोजयेत् । तं कामदुघं स्वर्गकामः परेत्य प्रतिपद्यते ॥
1.47.m: Under the Kṛttikās, one should feed [priests] rice cooked in milk along with clarified butter; / desiring heaven, when deceased, he attains that wish-granting cow.

1.48.s: rohiṇyām akṣatair māṣaiḥ sarpirmiśraṃ sahaudanam | dugdhānnapānaṃ maṃheta so 'kṣato yamasādane ||
1.48.d: रोहिण्याम् अक्षतैर् माषैः सर्पिर्मिश्रं सहौदनम् । दुग्धान्नपानं मंहेत सो ऽक्षतो यमसादने ॥
1.48.m: Under Rohiṇī, one should offer unbroken black lentils mixed with clarified butter along with boiled rice, / [and] food and drink made with milk; he remains uninjured in Yama's abode.

1.48.s: mṛgaśirasi maṃheta ajāṃ dhenuṃ payasvinīm | sāsmai sarvān kāmān dugdhvā eti pūrvā payasvinī ||
1.48.d: मृगशिरसि मंहेत अजां धेनुं पयस्विनीम् । सास्मै सर्वान् कामान् दुग्ध्वा एति पूर्वा पयस्विनी ॥
1.48.m: Under Mṛgaśiras, one should offer a female goat, a milch cow yielding abundant milk; / having milked all wishes for him, she, yielding milk, goes before [him].

1.48.s: ārdrāyāṃ kṛsaraṃ dadyāt tailamiśram upoṣitaḥ | punarvasubhyāṃ maṃheta madhvapūpāṃs tv anuttamān ||
1.48.d: आर्द्रायां कृसरं दद्यात् तैलमिश्रम् उपोषितः । पुनर्वसुभ्यां मंहेत मध्वपूपांस् त्व् अनुत्तमान् ॥
1.48.m: Under Ārdrā, having fasted, one should give a mixture of rice and sesame mixed with sesame oil; / under the two Punarvasus, one should offer unsurpassed cakes with honey.

1.48.s: rukmaṃ puṣyeṇa maṃheta so 'kṣato yamasādane | aśleṣā rajataṃ dadyāt saurabheyeṇa preṣitaḥ ||
1.48.d: रुक्मं पुष्येण मंहेत सो ऽक्षतो यमसादने । अश्लेषा रजतं दद्यात् सौरभेयेण प्रेषितः ॥
1.48.m: Under Puṣya, one should offer gold; he remains uninjured in Yama's abode; / under Āśleṣā, he should give silver, [and] sent by an ox,

1.48.s: sarpān nirhanti pretasya paripanthi sukhād bhayāt | maghābhis tu tilān dadyān madhumiśrān smaran pitṝn ||
1.48.d: सर्पान् निर्हन्ति प्रेतस्य परिपन्थि सुखाद् भयात् । मघाभिस् तु तिलान् दद्यान् मधुमिश्रान् स्मरन् पितॄन् ॥
1.48.m: he slays the serpent highwaymen of the deceased through ease and fear. / Under the Maghās, one should give sesame seeds mixed with honey, remembering the ancestors.

1.48.s: kāmais tatropatiṣṭhanti amī ye somayājinaḥ | phāṇiteneṣṭakā miśrā dadyāt pūrvayoḥ phalgunyor madhunottarayoḥ ||
1.48.d: कामैस् तत्रोपतिष्ठन्ति अमी ये सोमयाजिनः । फाणितेनेष्टका मिश्रा दद्यात् पूर्वयोः फल्गुन्योर् मधुनोत्तरयोः ॥
1.48.m: Those Soma-sacrificers attend upon him there with [fulfillment of] desires. / Under the prior two Phalgunīs one should give bricks mixed with treacle, and under the latter two with honey.
Under the prior and latter Phalgunīs, [cows] yield honey and treacle.

1.49.s: bṛhaddhastirathaṃ yuktaṃ hastena tu dadan naraḥ | savituḥ sthānam āpnoti divyāṃ kāmajavāṃ sabhām ||
1.49.d: बृहद्धस्तिरथं युक्तं हस्तेन तु ददन् नरः । सवितुः स्थानम् आप्नोति दिव्यां कामजवां सभाम् ॥
1.49.m: A man who gives a great elephant-drawn chariot under Hasta / attains the realm of Savitṛ, the divine hall moving at will.

1.49.s: citrāyāṃ vṛṣalīṃ dadyāt sarvapuṣpair alaṃkṛtām | gandhaiḥ śuśrūṣamāṇas tu dhruve sthāne sugandhiḥ prapadyate ||
1.49.d: चित्रायां वृषलीं दद्यात् सर्वपुष्पैर् अलंकृताम् । गन्धैः शुश्रूषमाणस् तु ध्रुवे स्थाने सुगन्धिः प्रपद्यते ॥
1.49.m: Under Citrā, one should give a Śūdra woman adorned with all flowers; / serving with perfumes, fragrant, he reaches a firm station.

1.49.s: svātāv ekadhanaṃ dadyād yadyad asya priyaṃ gṛhe | asajjamāno gaccheta aśarīro yathā manaḥ ||
1.49.d: स्वाताव् एकधनं दद्याद् यद्यद् अस्य प्रियं गृहे । असज्जमानो गच्छेत अशरीरो यथा मनः ॥
1.49.m: Under Svāti, one should give a single treasure, whatever in his house is dear [to him]; / unattached, he travels bodiless like the mind.

1.49.s: dhenuṃ tu rūpasaṃpannām anaḍvāhau tu vā vahau | viśākhābhyāṃ madhumanthaṃ prāpayet sthānam uttamam ||
1.49.d: धेनुं तु रूपसंपन्नाम् अनड्वाहौ तु वा वहौ । विशाखाभ्यां मधुमन्थं प्रापयेत् स्थानम् उत्तमम् ॥
1.49.m: Under the two Viśākhās, [giving] a milch cow endowed with good form, or two draft oxen, / [and] a gruel mixed with honey, leads to the highest abode.

1.49.s: anūrādhāsu prāvaraṇam annaṃ tu śuci jyeṣṭhāyāṃ ca | dadyāc cānnaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo bhakṣair uccāvacaiḥ saha ||
1.49.d: अनूराधासु प्रावरणम् अन्नं तु शुचि ज्येष्ठायां च । दद्याच् चान्नं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो भक्षैर् उच्चावचैः सह ॥
1.49.m: Under the Anurādhās, an outer garment, but pure food under Jyeṣṭhā; / and one should give food to brāhmaṇas along with varied delicacies.

1.49.s: surāṃ mūlena maṃhetābrāhmaṇībhya upoṣitaḥ | mātus tenānṛṇo bhavati saṃkarāc ca vimucyate ||
1.49.d: सुरां मूलेन मंहेताब्राह्मणीभ्य उपोषितः । मातुस् तेनानृणो भवति संकराच् च विमुच्यते ॥
1.49.m: Having fasted, one should offer liquor to non-brāhmaṇa women under Mūla; / through this he becomes free of debt to his mother and is released from confusion of caste.
Under the prior Aṣāḍhās [one should give] a gruel of flour in water; under the latter, with honey.

1.49.s: abhijid duhitaraṃ dadyān madhuparkapurogamām | uttame brahmaṇaḥ sthāne sarvakāmaiḥ pramodate ||
1.49.d: अभिजिद् दुहितरं दद्यान् मधुपर्कपुरोगमाम् । उत्तमे ब्रह्मणः स्थाने सर्वकामैः प्रमोदते ॥
1.49.m: Under Abhijit, one should give a daughter preceded by the honey-mixture; / he rejoices in the highest station of Brahmā with all desires.

1.50.s: kambalaṃ śravaṇe dadyād vastrāntaram upoṣitaḥ | śraviṣṭhābhir vastrayugaṃ gandhān śatabhiṣag bhavet ||
1.50.d: कम्बलं श्रवणे दद्याद् वस्त्रान्तरम् उपोषितः । श्रविष्ठाभिर् वस्त्रयुगं गन्धान् शतभिषग् भवेत् ॥
1.50.m: Having fasted, one should give a woolen blanket under Śravaṇa, [and] a second garment; / under the Śraviṣṭhās a pair of garments; under Śatabhiṣaj there should be perfumes.

1.50.s: ajaṃ saṃpacyodanaṃ dadyāt pūrvayoḥ proṣṭhapadayor aurabhreṇa sahottarayoḥ ||
1.50.d: अजं संपच्योदनं दद्यात् पूर्वयोः प्रोष्ठपदयोर् औरभ्रेण सहोत्तरयोः ॥
1.50.m: Having cooked a goat, one should give boiled rice under the prior two Proṣṭhapadās; / under the latter two, along with a ram.

1.50.s: dhenuṃ ca rūpasaṃpannāṃ gaur gṛṣṭiḥ pūrṇadohanīm | revatyāṃ trivatsāṃ dadyāc chubhakāṃsyopadohinīm ||
1.50.d: धेनुं च रूपसंपन्नां गौर् गृष्टिः पूर्णदोहनीम् । रेवत्यां त्रिवत्सां दद्याच् छुभकांस्योपदोहिनीम् ॥
1.50.m: And under Revatī, one should give a milch cow endowed with good form, a cow that has calved once, filling the milk pail, / having had three calves, being milked into an auspicious bell-metal vessel.

1.50.s: vastreṇānaḍvāhau saṃbaddhvā dadyād aśvayujo r naraḥ | daśa varṣasahasrāṇi lomnilomni mahīyate ||
1.50.d: वस्त्रेणानड्वाहौ संबद्ध्वा दद्याद् अश्वयुजो र् नरः । दश वर्षसहस्राणि लोम्निलोम्नि महीयते ॥
1.50.m: Under the two Aśvayujas, a man who gives two draft oxen bound together with a cloth / is honored for ten thousand years for every hair [on their bodies].

1.50.s: aṣṭau varṣasahasrāṇi ajadhenvā payo 'śnute | daśa varṣasahasrāṇi godhenvā payo 'śnute ||
1.50.d: अष्टौ वर्षसहस्राणि अजधेन्वा पयो ऽश्नुते । दश वर्षसहस्राणि गोधेन्वा पयो ऽश्नुते ॥
1.50.m: For eight thousand years he enjoys milk from a milch goat; / for ten thousand years he enjoys milk from a milch cow.

1.50.s: anaḍvāhaṃ tu yo dadyāt suhṛdaṃ sādhuvāhinam | vīraṃ prajānāṃ bhartāraṃ prāpnoti daśadhenudam ||
1.50.d: अनड्वाहं तु यो दद्यात् सुहृदं साधुवाहिनम् । वीरं प्रजानां भर्तारं प्राप्नोति दशधेनुदम् ॥
1.50.m: He who gives a draft ox that is friendly and carries well, / a vigorous bearer of subjects, obtains [the reward of] one who gives ten milch cows.

1.50.s: yadā vatsasya pādau dvau śiras cāpi pradṛśyate | tadā gauḥ pṛthivī jñeyā yāvad garbhaṃ na muñcati ||
1.50.d: यदा वत्सस्य पादौ द्वौ शिरस् चापि प्रदृश्यते । तदा गौः पृथिवी ज्ञेया यावद् गर्भं न मुञ्चति ॥
1.50.m: When the two front feet and the head of the calf are seen, / the cow is to be known as the earth, as long as she has not dropped the fetus.

1.50.s: bharaṇībhiḥ kṛṣṇatilāṃ dadyāt tiladhenuṃ payasvinīm | tayā durgāṇi tarati kṣuradhārāṃś ca parvatān ||
1.50.d: भरणीभिः कृष्णतिलां दद्यात् तिलधेनुं पयस्विनीम् । तया दुर्गाणि तरति क्षुरधारांश् च पर्वतान् ॥
1.50.m: Under the Bharaṇīs, one should give an effigy of a cow made of sesame [seeds] with black sesame, abounding in milk; / by means of it he crosses over difficult passages and mountains with razor-sharp edges.

1.50.s: nakṣatrāṇāṃ yathā somo jyotiṣām iva bhāskaraḥ | bhāti divyaṃ divaṃ jyotiḥ pāvakaḥ śucir uttamaḥ ||
1.50.d: नक्षत्राणां यथा सोमो ज्योतिषाम् इव भास्करः । भाति दिव्यं दिवं ज्योतिः पावकः शुचिर् उत्तमः ॥
1.50.m: Just as Soma [shines] among the lunar mansions, as the sun among heavenly lights, / [so] the purifier, pure and supreme, shines as divine light in heaven.

1.50.s: evam uktāṃ nakṣatradakṣiṇāṃ yo dadātīha jīvaloke | apahatya tamaḥ sarvaṃ brahmaloke mahīyate | yathā yaṣṭus tathādhyetur eṣā brāhmī pratiśrutir eṣā brāhmī pratiśrutir iti || kṛttikārohiṇīmadhye paippalādā mantrāḥ ||
1.50.d: एवम् उक्तां नक्षत्रदक्षिणां यो ददातीह जीवलोके । अपहत्य तमः सर्वं ब्रह्मलोके महीयते । यथा यष्टुस् तथाध्येतुर् एषा ब्राह्मी प्रतिश्रुतिर् एषा ब्राह्मी प्रतिश्रुतिर् इति ॥ कृत्तिकारोहिणीमध्ये पैप्पलादा मन्त्राः ॥
1.50.m:
He who gives the sacrificial fee for the lunar mansions in this living world as described, / having destroyed all darkness, is exalted in the world of Brahmā. / As for the sacrificer, so for the reciter: this is the Vedic promise, this is the Vedic promise.

(Pariśiṣṭa 1b. [Paippalāda Mantras between Kṛttikā and Rohiṇī])

The Paippalāda mantras between Kṛttikā and Rohiṇī [are concluded].

2.1.s: om | brahmaṇe brahmavedāya rudrāya parameṣṭhine | namaskṛtya pravakṣyāmi śeṣam ātharvaṇaṃ vidhim ||
2.1.d: ओम् । ब्रह्मणे ब्रह्मवेदाय रुद्राय परमेष्ठिने । नमस्कृत्य प्रवक्ष्यामि शेषम् आथर्वणं विधिम् ॥
2.1.m: Om. Having bowed to Brahmā, the Brahmaveda, and Rudra Parameṣṭhin, / I shall proclaim the remainder of the Atharvan rule.

2.1.s: daivaṃ prabhavate śreṣṭhaṃ hetumātraṃ tu pauruṣam | daivena tu suguptena śakto jetuṃ vasuṃdharām ||
2.1.d: दैवं प्रभवते श्रेष्ठं हेतुमात्रं तु पौरुषम् । दैवेन तु सुगुप्तेन शक्तो जेतुं वसुंधराम् ॥
2.1.m: Fate is sovereign and paramount, whereas human effort is merely an instrumental cause; / but supported well by fate, one is able to conquer the earth.

2.1.s: daivāt puruṣakārāc ca daivam eva viśiṣyate | tasmād daivaṃ viśeṣeṇa pūjayet tu mahīpatiḥ ||
2.1.d: दैवात् पुरुषकाराच् च दैवम् एव विशिष्यते । तस्माद् दैवं विशेषेण पूजयेत् तु महीपतिः ॥
2.1.m: Between fate and human effort, fate indeed is superior; / therefore the ruler of the earth should especially venerate fate.

2.1.s: daivakarmavidau tasmāt sāṃvatsarapurohitau | gṛhṇīyāt satataṃ rājā dānasaṃmānarañjanaiḥ ||
2.1.d: दैवकर्मविदौ तस्मात् सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ । गृह्णीयात् सततं राजा दानसंमानरञ्जनैः ॥
2.1.m: Therefore, the king should constantly maintain the astrologer and the royal priest, who know rites concerning fate, / through gifts, honors, and pleasing words.

2.1.s: apitā tu yathā bālas tathāsāṃvatsaro nṛpaḥ | amātṛko yathā bālas tathātharvavivarjitaḥ || arimadhye yathaikākī tathā vaidyavivarjitaḥ ||
2.1.d: अपिता तु यथा बालस् तथासांवत्सरो नृपः । अमातृको यथा बालस् तथाथर्वविवर्जितः ॥ अरिमध्ये यथैकाकी तथा वैद्यविवर्जितः ॥
2.1.m: Just as a child is fatherless, so is a king without an astrologer; / just as a child is motherless, so is one destitute of an Atharvan; / just as one is alone in the midst of enemies, so is one destitute of a physician.

2.1.s: dharmeṇa pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ vijayiṣyan mahīpatiḥ | vidyālakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ bhārgavaṃ varayed gurum ||
2.1.d: धर्मेण पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां विजयिष्यन् महीपतिः । विद्यालक्षणसंपन्नं भार्गवं वरयेद् गुरुम् ॥
2.1.m: A ruler of the earth who desires to conquer the entire earth in accordance with dharma / should choose as spiritual guide a descendant of Bhṛgu endowed with learning and bodily signs.

2.1.s: caturvidhasya karmaṇo vedatattvena niścayam | prajāpatir athaiko hi na vedatrayam īkṣate ||
2.1.d: चतुर्विधस्य कर्मणो वेदतत्त्वेन निश्चयम् । प्रजापतिर् अथैको हि न वेदत्रयम् ईक्षते ॥
2.1.m: The determination of fourfold ritual action is made according to the reality of the Veda; / for Prajāpati alone does not look upon the triad of Vedas [apart from the fourth].

2.2.s: atharvabhinnaṃ yac chāntaṃ tac chāntaṃ netarais tribhiḥ | vijñānaṃ triṣu lokeṣu jāyate brahmavedataḥ ||
2.2.d: अथर्वभिन्नं यच् छान्तं तच् छान्तं नेतरैस् त्रिभिः । विज्ञानं त्रिषु लोकेषु जायते ब्रह्मवेदतः ॥
2.2.m: What is pacified by that which belongs to the Atharvan is pacified; it is not pacified by the other three; / supreme knowledge in the three worlds arises from the Brahmaveda.

2.2.s: atharvā sṛjate ghoram adbhutaṃ śamayet tathā | atharvā rakṣate yajñaṃ yajñasya patir aṅgirāḥ ||
2.2.d: अथर्वा सृजते घोरम् अद्भुतं शमयेत् तथा । अथर्वा रक्षते यज्ञं यज्ञस्य पतिर् अङ्गिराः ॥
2.2.m: The Atharvan releases the terrible, and likewise he pacifies portents; / the Atharvan protects the sacrifice; the Aṅgiras is the lord of the sacrifice.

2.2.s: divyāntarikṣabhaumānām utpātānām anekadhā | śamayitā brahmavedajñas tasmād rakṣitā bhṛguḥ ||
2.2.d: दिव्यान्तरिक्षभौमानाम् उत्पातानाम् अनेकधा । शमयिता ब्रह्मवेदज्ञस् तस्माद् रक्षिता भृगुः ॥
2.2.m: The knower of the Brahmaveda is the pacifier of portents of the sky, the intermediate space, and the earth in diverse ways; / therefore the descendant of Bhṛgu is the protector.

2.2.s: brahmā śamayen nādhvaryur na chandogo na bahvṛcaḥ | rakṣāṃsi rakṣati brahmā brahmā tasmād atharvavit ||
2.2.d: ब्रह्मा शमयेन् नाध्वर्युर् न छन्दोगो न बह्वृचः । रक्षांसि रक्षति ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मा तस्माद् अथर्ववित् ॥
2.2.m: The Brahman priest can pacify, not the Adhvaryu, not the Chandoga, not the Bahvṛca; / the Brahman priest guards against the demons; therefore the Brahman priest must be a knower of the Atharvan.

2.2.s: senāyā rakṣaṇe tasmāt svarāṣṭraparivṛddhaye | śāntyarthaṃ ca mahīpālo vṛṇuyād bhārgavaṃ gurum ||
2.2.d: सेनाया रक्षणे तस्मात् स्वराष्ट्रपरिवृद्धये । शान्त्यर्थं च महीपालो वृणुयाद् भार्गवं गुरुम् ॥
2.2.m: Therefore, for the protection of the army, for the increase of his own realm, / and for the sake of propitiation, the ruler of the earth should choose a descendant of Bhṛgu as spiritual guide.

2.3.s: gurave pārthivo dadyāt kotiṃ varaṇadakṣiṇām | ardhamardhaṃ mahībhāgaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu tribhāgataḥ ||
2.3.d: गुरवे पार्थिवो दद्यात् कोतिं वरणदक्षिणाम् । अर्धमर्धं महीभागं तृतीयं तु त्रिभागतः ॥
2.3.m: The earthly ruler should give to the spiritual guide ten million [coins] as the choice-fee, / or half of a territory of the earth, or a third from a threefold division.

2.3.s: evaṃ bhūmipramāṇena koṭibhāgaṃ vinirdiśet | yena vā parituṣyeta gurus tat pārthivaś caret ||
2.3.d: एवं भूमिप्रमाणेन कोटिभागं विनिर्दिशेत् । येन वा परितुष्येत गुरुस् तत् पार्थिवश् चरेत् ॥
2.3.m: Thus according to the extent of the land he should assign a crore or a portion; / or the ruler of the earth should do that by which the spiritual guide may be completely satisfied.

2.3.s: ghnanti daivopasargāś ca na ca devo 'bhivarṣati | vīrās tatra na sūyante yad rāṣṭram apurohitam ||
2.3.d: घ्नन्ति दैवोपसर्गाश् च न च देवो ऽभिवर्षति । वीरास् तत्र न सूयन्ते यद् राष्ट्रम् अपुरोहितम् ॥
2.3.m: Ominous afflictions from fate destroy it, and the god does not send rain, / [and] heroes are not born in that realm which has no royal priest.

2.3.s: na haviḥ pratigṛhṇanti devatāḥ pitaro dvijāḥ | tasya bhūmipater yasya gṛhe nātharvavid guruḥ ||
2.3.d: न हविः प्रतिगृह्णन्ति देवताः पितरो द्विजाः । तस्य भूमिपतेर् यस्य गृहे नाथर्वविद् गुरुः ॥
2.3.m: The deities, the ancestors, and the twice-born do not accept an oblation / from that ruler of the earth in whose house there is no spiritual guide who knows the Atharvan.

2.3.s: samāhitāṅgapratyaṅgaṃ vidyācāraguṇānvitam | paippalādaṃ guruṃ kuryāc chrīrāṣṭrārogyavardhanam ||
2.3.d: समाहिताङ्गप्रत्यङ्गं विद्याचारगुणान्वितम् । पैप्पलादं गुरुं कुर्याच् छ्रीराष्ट्रारोग्यवर्धनम् ॥
2.3.m: One should appoint as spiritual guide a follower of the Pippalāda school, whose major and minor limbs are well proportioned, / who is endowed with learning, proper conduct, and virtue, who increases fortune, the realm, and health;

2.4.s: tathā śaunakinaṃ vāpi vedamantravipaścitam | rāṣṭrasya vṛddhikartāraṃ dhanadhānyādibhiḥ sadā ||
2.4.d: तथा शौनकिनं वापि वेदमन्त्रविपश्चितम् । राष्ट्रस्य वृद्धिकर्तारं धनधान्यादिभिः सदा ॥
2.4.m: or likewise a follower of the Śaunaka school, learned in the Vedic mantras, / who continually brings about the increase of the realm through wealth, grain, and the like.

2.4.s: ātharvaṇād ṛte nānyo niyojyo 'tharvavid guruḥ | nṛpeṇa jayakāmena nirmito 'gnir ivādhvare ||
2.4.d: आथर्वणाद् ऋते नान्यो नियोज्यो ऽथर्वविद् गुरुः । नृपेण जयकामेन निर्मितो ऽग्निर् इवाध्वरे ॥
2.4.m: Except for an Atharvan, no other should be appointed as spiritual guide who knows the Atharvan / by a king desiring victory, just as fire is prepared at a sacrificial session.

2.4.s: bahvṛco hanti vai rāṣṭram adhvaryur nāśayet sutān | chandogo dhananāśāya tasmād ātharvaṇo guruḥ ||
2.4.d: बह्वृचो हन्ति वै राष्ट्रम् अध्वर्युर् नाशयेत् सुतान् । छन्दोगो धननाशाय तस्माद् आथर्वणो गुरुः ॥
2.4.m: A Bahvṛca destroys the realm; an Adhvaryu ruins sons; / a Chandoga leads to the destruction of wealth; therefore, the spiritual guide must be an Atharvan.

2.4.s: ajñānād vā pramādād vā yasya syād bahvṛco guruḥ | deśarāṣṭrapurāmātyanāśas tasya na saṃśayaḥ ||
2.4.d: अज्ञानाद् वा प्रमादाद् वा यस्य स्याद् बह्वृचो गुरुः । देशराष्ट्रपुरामात्यनाशस् तस्य न संशयः ॥
2.4.m: He whose spiritual guide is a Bahvṛca through ignorance or through negligence / will suffer the destruction of his country, realm, city, and ministers: of this there is no doubt.

2.4.s: yadi vādhvaryavaṃ rājā niyunakti purohitam | śastreṇa vadhyate kṣipraṃ parikṣīṇārthavāhanaḥ ||
2.4.d: यदि वाध्वर्यवं राजा नियुनक्ति पुरोहितम् । शस्त्रेण वध्यते क्षिप्रं परिक्षीणार्थवाहनः ॥
2.4.m: If a king appoints an Adhvaryu priest as his royal priest, / he is swiftly slain by a weapon, his wealth and conveyances having wasted away.

2.5.s: yathaiva paṅgur adhvānam apakṣī cāṇḍajo nabhaḥ | evaṃ chandogaguruṇā rājā vṛddhiṃ na gacchati ||
2.5.d: यथैव पङ्गुर् अध्वानम् अपक्षी चाण्डजो नभः । एवं छन्दोगगुरुणा राजा वृद्धिं न गच्छति ॥
2.5.m: Just as a lame man cannot travel the path, and a wingless bird cannot traverse the sky, / even so a king does not attain prosperity through a Chandoga spiritual guide.

2.5.s: purodhā jalado yasya maudo vā syāt kadā cana | abdād daśabhyo māsebhyo rāṣṭrabhraṃśaṃ sa gacchati ||
2.5.d: पुरोधा जलदो यस्य मौदो वा स्यात् कदा चन । अब्दाद् दशभ्यो मासेभ्यो राष्ट्रभ्रंशं स गच्छति ॥
2.5.m: He whose royal priest should ever be a Jalada or a Mauda / suffers the loss of his realm within a year or ten months.

2.5.s: palālakam idaṃ sarvam ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃsthitam | sāraṃ sāraparaṃ dhānyam atharvāṅgiraso viduḥ ||
2.5.d: पलालकम् इदं सर्वम् ऋग्यजुःसामसंस्थितम् । सारं सारपरं धान्यम् अथर्वाङ्गिरसो विदुः ॥
2.5.m: All this that is contained in the Ṛg-, Yajur-, and Sāmaveda is mere chaff; / the knowers of Atharvan and Aṅgiras know the grain that is the essential, supreme essence.

2.5.s: trayo lokās trayo devās trayo vedās trayo 'gnayaḥ | ardhamātre layaṃ yānti vedaś cātharvaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
2.5.d: त्रयो लोकास् त्रयो देवास् त्रयो वेदास् त्रयो ऽग्नयः । अर्धमात्रे लयं यान्ति वेदश् चाथर्वणः स्मृतः ॥
2.5.m: The three worlds, the three gods, the three Vedas, and the three fires / merge into the half-mora, and that is traditionally known as the Atharvaveda.

2.5.s: na tithir na ca nakṣatraṃ na graho na ca candramāḥ | atharvamantrasaṃprāptyā sarvasiddhir bhaviṣyati ||
2.5.d: न तिथिर् न च नक्षत्रं न ग्रहो न च चन्द्रमाः । अथर्वमन्त्रसंप्राप्त्या सर्वसिद्धिर् भविष्यति ॥
2.5.m: Neither lunar day nor lunar mansion, neither planet nor moon [can impede]: / through the acquisition of the Atharvan mantra, all success will come to pass.

2.6.s: guruṇā paippalādena vedamantravipaścitā | vardhate dhanadhānyena rāṣṭram evaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
2.6.d: गुरुणा पैप्पलादेन वेदमन्त्रविपश्चिता । वर्धते धनधान्येन राष्ट्रम् एवं न संशयः ॥
2.6.m: With a spiritual guide belonging to the Pippalāda school, learned in the Vedic mantras, / the realm increases in wealth and grain in this manner, without a doubt.

2.6.s: stabdhaṃ nṛśaṃsaṃ pramattaṃ śraddhāhīnam aśāstragam | bhūmikāmo na yāceta dātāram api pārthivam ||
2.6.d: स्तब्धं नृशंसं प्रमत्तं श्रद्धाहीनम् अशास्त्रगम् । भूमिकामो न याचेत दातारम् अपि पार्थिवम् ॥
2.6.m: One desiring land should not ask of an arrogant, cruel, negligent king / who lacks faith and does not follow the śāstras, even though he is a giver.

2.6.s: sahasrāṇāṃ śataṃ japtvā gāyatryāyājyayājakaḥ | pūyate bhrūṇahāpy evaṃ cāṇḍālānnāda eva ca ||
2.6.d: सहस्राणां शतं जप्त्वा गायत्र्यायाज्ययाजकः । पूयते भ्रूणहाप्य् एवं चाण्डालान्नाद एव च ॥
2.6.m: Having muttered the Gāyatrī a hundred thousand times, one who sacrifices for those unfit to sacrifice / is purified, as is even a killer of an embryo or an eater of a Caṇḍāla's food.

2.6.s: sarvadravyaparityāgāc chuddhir anyair udāhṛtā | anyaiś caturṇāṃ vedānām adhītyādyottamā ṛcaḥ ||
2.6.d: सर्वद्रव्यपरित्यागाच् छुद्धिर् अन्यैर् उदाहृता । अन्यैश् चतुर्णां वेदानाम् अधीत्याद्योत्तमा ऋचः ॥
2.6.m: Purification through the abandonment of all possessions has been declared by others; / and by others, through having recited the beginning and concluding verses of the four Vedas.

2.6.s: yajanād abhicārād vā kva cid vā mantrakarmaṇi | pūtān eva dvijān prāhur agnikāñcanavarcasa iti || iti rāṣṭrasaṃvargaḥ samāptaḥ ||
2.6.d: यजनाद् अभिचाराद् वा क्व चिद् वा मन्त्रकर्मणि । पूतान् एव द्विजान् प्राहुर् अग्निकाञ्चनवर्चस इति ॥ इति राष्ट्रसंवर्गः समाप्तः ॥
2.6.m:
Whether from sacrificing, from sorcery, or anywhere in ritual involving mantras, / they declare the twice-born to be purified indeed, having the radiance of fire and gold.

Thus ends the Preservation of the Realm.

3.1.s: ācāryapurohitavajramukhata ity āha durmatiḥ sa bhāradvājo
3.1.d: आचार्यपुरोहितवज्रमुखत इत्य् आह दुर्मतिः स भारद्वाजो

3.1.s: na hy agner ivopayuktasyopayogo vidyata iti parāśaro
3.1.d: न ह्य् अग्नेर् इवोपयुक्तस्योपयोगो विद्यत इति पराशरो

3.1.s: yasyānyakulopayuktaḥ purodhāḥ śāntikapauṣṭikaprāyaścittīyābhicārikanaimittikordhvadehikāny atharvavihitāni karmāṇi kuryāt sa tasya pratyaṅgiro bhūtvā hastyaśvarathapadātikaṃ prakṛtimukhebhyo …
3.1.d: यस्यान्यकुलोपयुक्तः पुरोधाः शान्तिकपौष्टिकप्रायश्चित्तीयाभिचारिकनैमित्तिकोर्ध्वदेहिकान्य् अथर्वविहितानि कर्माणि कुर्यात् स तस्य प्रत्यङ्गिरो भूत्वा हस्त्यश्वरथपदातिकं प्रकृतिमुखेभ्यो …

3.1.s: variṣyan na punaḥ kuryād anyaṃ rājā purohitam | nirmālyam iva taṃ rājā nānyo bhūyaḥ samācaret ||
3.1.d: वरिष्यन् न पुनः कुर्याद् अन्यं राजा पुरोहितम् । निर्माल्यम् इव तं राजा नान्यो भूयः समाचरेत् ॥

3.1.s: svajasraṃ hy agnau hetur bhagavato vyādhitapatitonmattābhiśastaprahīṇapradhvastasaṃprasāraṇam ṛtvik ||
3.1.d: स्वजस्रं ह्य् अग्नौ हेतुर् भगवतो व्याधितपतितोन्मत्ताभिशस्तप्रहीणप्रध्वस्तसंप्रसारणम् ऋत्विक् ॥

3.1.s: tasmāt kulīnaṃ śrotriyaṃ bhṛgvaṅgirovidaṃ vinayākṛtiśaucācārayuktam alolupaṃ vrataniyamacāritravṛttalakṣanaguṇasaṃpannaṃ saṃdhivigrahacintakaṃ māhendrajālaprabhṛtikarmādiṣv abhividakaṃ jitasthānāsanaṃ himātapavarṣasahaṃ hrīdhṛtikam ārjavaṃ śamadamadayādānaśaktisaṃpannaṃ bṛhaspatyuśanasoḥ sthānākṛtipramāṇaṃ varṇāśrutavapuṣā cānumeyaṃ tejasvinaṃ gambhīraṃ sattvayuktaṃ guruṃ vṛṇīyād bhūpatir iti ||
3.1.d: तस्मात् कुलीनं श्रोत्रियं भृग्वङ्गिरोविदं विनयाकृतिशौचाचारयुक्तम् अलोलुपं व्रतनियमचारित्रवृत्तलक्षनगुणसंपन्नं संधिविग्रहचिन्तकं माहेन्द्रजालप्रभृतिकर्मादिष्व् अभिविदकं जितस्थानासनं हिमातपवर्षसहं ह्रीधृतिकम् आर्जवं शमदमदयादानशक्तिसंपन्नं बृहस्पत्युशनसोः स्थानाकृतिप्रमाणं वर्णाश्रुतवपुषा चानुमेयं तेजस्विनं गम्भीरं सत्त्वयुक्तं गुरुं वृणीयाद् भूपतिर् इति ॥

3.1.s: madhuparkādyena vidhinā yathārthaṃ saṃpādya dakṣiṇāṃ dadyāt
3.1.d: मधुपर्काद्येन विधिना यथार्थं संपाद्य दक्षिणां दद्यात्

3.1.s: hastyaśvaṃ narayānaṃ divyam ābharaṇam ātapatraṃ hiraṇyaṃ kṣitigodhanadhānyaratnādikaṃ ca gurave dadyād
3.1.d: हस्त्यश्वं नरयानं दिव्यम् आभरणम् आतपत्रं हिरण्यं क्षितिगोधनधान्यरत्नादिकं च गुरवे दद्याद्

3.2.s: hastyaśvaṃ gurave dadyān narayānaṃ tathaiva ca | divyam ābharaṇaṃ caiva ātapatrādim eva ca ||
3.2.d: हस्त्यश्वं गुरवे दद्यान् नरयानं तथैव च । दिव्यम् आभरणं चैव आतपत्रादिम् एव च ॥

3.2.s: ucchiṣṭārthaṃ na gṛhṇīyān maṅgalārthaṃ mahīpatiḥ | mantrauṣadhyo na sidhyanti rājā tatra vinaśyati ||
3.2.d: उच्छिष्टार्थं न गृह्णीयान् मङ्गलार्थं महीपतिः । मन्त्रौषध्यो न सिध्यन्ति राजा तत्र विनश्यति ॥

3.2.s: nātidīrghaṃ nātihrasvaṃ nātisthūlaṃ kṛśaṃ tathā | na ca hīnātiriktāṅgaṃ kva cit kuryāt purohitam ||
3.2.d: नातिदीर्घं नातिह्रस्वं नातिस्थूलं कृशं तथा । न च हीनातिरिक्ताङ्गं क्व चित् कुर्यात् पुरोहितम् ॥

3.2.s: hīnādhikāṅgaṃ patitaṃ vivarṇaṃ stenaṃ jaḍaṃ klībam aśaktiyuktam | bhinnasvaraṃ kāṇaṃ virūpanetraṃ dveṣyaṃ ca rājā guruṃ naiva kuryāt ||
3.2.d: हीनाधिकाङ्गं पतितं विवर्णं स्तेनं जडं क्लीबम् अशक्तियुक्तम् । भिन्नस्वरं काणं विरूपनेत्रं द्वेष्यं च राजा गुरुं नैव कुर्यात् ॥

3.2.s: hīnādhikāṅge purarāṣṭrahāniḥ kāṇe jaḍe vāhanakośanāśaḥ | stene tv aśakte ca samastadoṣāḥ klībe vivarṇe nṛpatir vinaśyet ||
3.2.d: हीनाधिकाङ्गे पुरराष्ट्रहानिः काणे जडे वाहनकोशनाशः । स्तेने त्व् अशक्ते च समस्तदोषाः क्लीबे विवर्णे नृपतिर् विनश्येत् ॥

3.3.s: bhinnasvare jāyate gātrabhedo dveṣye gurau vipratipattim āhuḥ | vivarṇanetre patite tu putrān adhvaryuṇā ca nihanti pautrān ||
3.3.d: भिन्नस्वरे जायते गात्रभेदो द्वेष्ये गुरौ विप्रतिपत्तिम् आहुः । विवर्णनेत्रे पतिते तु पुत्रान् अध्वर्युणा च निहन्ति पौत्रान् ॥

3.3.s: kṛṣṇe kośakṣayaṃ vidyād rakte vāhanasaṃkṣayaḥ | piṅgalaḥ pārthivaṃ hanyād rāṣṭraṃ hanyāt tu kekaraḥ ||
3.3.d: कृष्णे कोशक्षयं विद्याद् रक्ते वाहनसंक्षयः । पिङ्गलः पार्थिवं हन्याद् राष्ट्रं हन्यात् तु केकरः ॥

3.3.s: bahvṛcaṃ hi niyuñjyād yaḥ paurohitye tu pārthivaḥ | sa tārapaṅke hastīva saha tenaiva majjati ||
3.3.d: बह्वृचं हि नियुञ्ज्याद् यः पौरोहित्ये तु पार्थिवः । स तारपङ्के हस्तीव सह तेनैव मज्जति ॥

3.3.s: adhvaryuṃ hi niyuñjyād yaḥ paurohitye tu pārthivaḥ | uttitīrṣur ivāśmānam ādatte svavadhāya saḥ ||
3.3.d: अध्वर्युं हि नियुञ्ज्याद् यः पौरोहित्ये तु पार्थिवः । उत्तितीर्षुर् इवाश्मानम् आदत्ते स्ववधाय सः ॥

3.3.s: vadhabandhaparikleśaṃ kośavāhanasaṃkṣayaḥ | karoty etānvaye 'vasthās tapoyukto 'pi sāmagaḥ ||
3.3.d: वधबन्धपरिक्लेशं कोशवाहनसंक्षयः । करोत्य् एतान्वये ऽवस्थास् तपोयुक्तो ऽपि सामगः ॥

3.3.s: anvayākṛtisaṃpannaṃ tasmād bhṛgvaṅgirovidam | gotrāṅgirasavāsiṣṭhaṃ rājā kuryāt purohitam ||
3.3.d: अन्वयाकृतिसंपन्नं तस्माद् भृग्वङ्गिरोविदम् । गोत्राङ्गिरसवासिष्ठं राजा कुर्यात् पुरोहितम् ॥

3.3.s: makheṣu rāṣṭreṣu pureṣu caiva senāsu rājñāṃ svaniveśaneṣu | ya utpātās trividhā ghorarūpās tān sarvān śamayed brahmavedavit ||
3.3.d: मखेषु राष्ट्रेषु पुरेषु चैव सेनासु राज्ञां स्वनिवेशनेषु । य उत्पातास् त्रिविधा घोररूपास् तान् सर्वान् शमयेद् ब्रह्मवेदवित् ॥

3.3.s: tasmād guruṃ vedarahasyayuktaṃ caturvidhe karmaṇi cāpramattam | śāntaṃ ca dāntaṃ ca jitendriyaṃ ca kuryān narendraḥ priyadarśanaṃ ca || priyadarśanaṃ ceti || iti rājaprathamābhiṣekaḥ samāptaḥ ||
3.3.d: तस्माद् गुरुं वेदरहस्ययुक्तं चतुर्विधे कर्मणि चाप्रमत्तम् । शान्तं च दान्तं च जितेन्द्रियं च कुर्यान् नरेन्द्रः प्रियदर्शनं च ॥ प्रियदर्शनं चेति ॥ इति राजप्रथमाभिषेकः समाप्तः ॥
3.3.m:
(Pariśiṣṭa 3. The King's First Consecration)

Thus ends the king's first consecration.

4.1.s: om atha purohitakarmāṇi || rājñaḥ prātar utthitasya kṛtasvastyayanasya
4.1.d: ओम् अथ पुरोहितकर्माणि ॥ राज्ञः प्रातर् उत्थितस्य कृतस्वस्त्ययनस्य
4.1.m: Om. Now, the duties of the royal domestic priest. For the king who has risen in the morning and performed his auspicious recitations,

4.1.s: atha purohitaḥ snātānuliptaḥ śuciḥ śuklavāsāḥ soṣṇīṣaḥ savitā prasavānām iti vyākhyātam ||
4.1.d: अथ पुरोहितः स्नातानुलिप्तः शुचिः शुक्लवासाः सोष्णीषः सविता प्रसवानाम् इति व्याख्यातम् ॥
4.1.m: now the royal domestic priest, having bathed, anointed himself, pure, wearing white garments and a turban—[the recitation beginning] "Savitṛ of impulses" has been explained.

4.1.s: imam indra vardhayety uktam ||
4.1.d: इमम् इन्द्र वर्धयेत्य् उक्तम् ॥
4.1.m: "Magnify this Indra" has been stated.

4.1.s: pari dhatteti dvābhyāṃ rājño vastram abhimantrya prayacchet ||
4.1.d: परि धत्तेति द्वाभ्यां राज्ञो वस्त्रम् अभिमन्त्र्य प्रयच्छेत् ॥
4.1.m: Consecrating the king's garment with the two verses beginning "Put on...", he should hand it to him.

4.1.s: yad ābadhnann ity alaṃkārān ||
4.1.d: यद् आबध्नन्न् इत्य् अलंकारान् ॥
4.1.m: The ornaments with "That which they bound..."

4.1.s: siṃhe vyāghra iti siṃhāsanam ||
4.1.d: सिंहे व्याघ्र इति सिंहासनम् ॥
4.1.m: The throne with "In the lion, in the tiger..."

4.1.s: yas te gandha iti gandhān ||
4.1.d: यस् ते गन्ध इति गन्धान् ॥
4.1.m: The perfumes with "The scent of yours which..."

4.1.s: ehi jīvaṃ trāyamāṇam ity akṣiṇī aṅkte ||
4.1.d: एहि जीवं त्रायमाणम् इत्य् अक्षिणी अङ्क्ते ॥
4.1.m: He anoints the two eyes with "Come, the living, the protecting..."

4.1.s: vātaraṃhā ity aśvam ||
4.1.d: वातरंहा इत्य् अश्वम् ॥

4.1.s: hastivarcasam iti hastinam ||
4.1.d: हस्तिवर्चसम् इति हस्तिनम् ॥
4.1.m: The elephant with "Elephant luster..."

4.1.s: yat te mātā yat te piteti narayānam ||
4.1.d: यत् ते माता यत् ते पितेति नरयानम् ॥
4.1.m: The palanquin with "What your mother, what your father..."

4.1.s: khaḍgaṃ cābhimantrayāmīti khaḍgam ||
4.1.d: खड्गं चाभिमन्त्रयामीति खड्गम् ॥
4.1.m: The sword with "And I consecrate the sword..."

4.1.s: khaḍgaṃ cābhimantrayāmi yaḥ śatrūn mardayiṣyati | marditāḥ śatravo 'nena vaśam āyāntu te sadeti ||
4.1.d: खड्गं चाभिमन्त्रयामि यः शत्रून् मर्दयिष्यति । मर्दिताः शत्रवो ऽनेन वशम् आयान्तु ते सदेति ॥
4.1.m: "And I consecrate the sword which will crush the enemies; / crushed by this, may enemies always come under your control."

4.1.s: paryaṅkam āsanaṃ khaḍgaṃ dhvajaṃ chattraṃ sacāmaram | ratham aśvagajaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dhanur varma śareṣudhim ||
4.1.d: पर्यङ्कम् आसनं खड्गं ध्वजं छत्त्रं सचामरम् । रथम् अश्वगजं श्रेष्ठं धनुर् वर्म शरेषुधिम् ॥
4.1.m: The couch, seat, sword, banner, umbrella with chowrie, / chariot, excellent horse and elephant, bow, armor, arrows, and quiver,

4.1.s: āñjanaṃ gandhamālyāni vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca | sarvān śāntyudakenaitān abhyukṣyec cābhimantrayet ||
4.1.d: आञ्जनं गन्धमाल्यानि वस्त्राण्य् आभरणानि च । सर्वान् शान्त्युदकेनैतान् अभ्युक्ष्येच् चाभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥
4.1.m: eye-salve, perfumes, garlands, garments, and ornaments— / having sprinkled all these with the pacifying water, he should consecrate them.

4.1.s: dūrvādīn mūrdhni nikṣipya svastyayanair abhimantrayet | abhayaṃ dyāvāpṛthivīty abhimantrito brāhmaṇān praṇipatya prāk ||
4.1.d: दूर्वादीन् मूर्ध्नि निक्षिप्य स्वस्त्ययनैर् अभिमन्त्रयेत् । अभयं द्यावापृथिवीत्य् अभिमन्त्रितो ब्राह्मणान् प्रणिपत्य प्राक् ॥
4.1.m: Having placed dūrvā grass and other things on his head, he should consecrate him with auspicious recitations. Consecrated with "Freedom from danger, O Heaven and Earth...", having first bowed down to the brahmins,

4.1.s: yuṣmatprasādāc chāntim adhigacchāmīti ||
4.1.d: युष्मत्प्रसादाच् छान्तिम् अधिगच्छामीति ॥
4.1.m: [the king says:] "By your favor, I obtain peace."

4.1.s: tathāstv ity ukto nirgacched iti ||
4.1.d: तथास्त्व् इत्य् उक्तो निर्गच्छेद् इति ॥
4.1.m: Addressed with "So be it!", he should go forth.

4.1.s: evaṃkṛtyasvastyayano yad evāvalokayati ta sidhyati ||
4.1.d: एवंकृत्यस्वस्त्ययनो यद् एवावलोकयति त सिध्यति ॥
4.1.m: Having thus performed the auspicious recitation, whatever he looks upon succeeds.

4.1.s: tad api ślokāḥ ||
4.1.d: तद् अपि श्लोकाः ॥

4.1.s: asuraiḥ pīḍyamānas tu purā śakro jagatprabhuḥ | kārayām āsa vidhivat purodhastve bṛhaspatim ||
4.1.d: असुरैः पीड्यमानस् तु पुरा शक्रो जगत्प्रभुः । कारयाम् आस विधिवत् पुरोधस्त्वे बृहस्पतिम् ॥
4.1.m: Afflicted by the Asuras in ancient times, Śakra, the lord of the world, / had Bṛhaspati installed according to rule in the office of royal domestic priest.

4.1.s: sa vṛto bhayabhītena śamanārthaṃ bubhūṣatā | maṅgalāni sasarjāṣṭāv abhayārthaṃ śatakratoḥ ||
4.1.d: स वृतो भयभीतेन शमनार्थं बुभूषता । मङ्गलानि ससर्जाष्टाव् अभयार्थं शतक्रतोः ॥
4.1.m: Chosen by him who was terrified by fear and desired pacification, / he emitted eight auspicious things for the safety of Śatakratu.

4.1.s: proktāni maṅgalāny aṣṭau brāhmaṇo gaur hutāśanaḥ | bhūmiḥ siddhārthakāḥ sarpiḥ śamī vrīhiyavau tathā ||
4.1.d: प्रोक्तानि मङ्गलान्य् अष्टौ ब्राह्मणो गौर् हुताशनः । भूमिः सिद्धार्थकाः सर्पिः शमी व्रीहियवौ तथा ॥
4.1.m: The eight auspicious things are declared: a brahmin, a cow, fire, / earth, white mustard seeds, clarified butter, the śamī tree, and rice and barley.

4.1.s: etāni satataṃ puṇyāni saṃpaśyann arcayann api | na prāpnoty āpadaṃ rājā śriyaṃ prāpnoty anuttamām ||
4.1.d: एतानि सततं पुण्यानि संपश्यन्न् अर्चयन्न् अपि । न प्राप्नोत्य् आपदं राजा श्रियं प्राप्नोत्य् अनुत्तमाम् ॥
4.1.m: Always looking upon and venerating these holy things, / the king does not meet with misfortune and attains unsurpassed prosperity.

4.2.m: Bathed at the Viśvāvasu muhūrta, consecrated with consecration mantras,
with garments, ornaments, and the like according to the previously stated rule,
taking a golden niṣka or a kṛṣṇala with his left hand,

4.2.s: yad duḥkṛtaṃ yac chabalaṃ sarvaṃ pāpmānaṃ dahatv ity
4.2.d: यद् दुःकृतं यच् छबलं सर्वं पाप्मानं दहत्व् इत्य्
4.2.m: saying: 'Whatever evil deed, whatever blemish [there is], let it burn away all evil,'

4.2.s: anena mantreṇa suvarṇaṃ śarīre nighṛṣya dakṣiṇena hastena viprāya dadyād
4.2.d: अनेन मन्त्रेण सुवर्णं शरीरे निघृष्य दक्षिणेन हस्तेन विप्राय दद्याद्
4.2.m: rubbing the gold on his body with this mantra, he should give it to a brāhmaṇa with his right hand,

4.2.s: aparimitaguṇān tilān sauvarṇamaye tāmramaye vā pātre sthāpayitvā yad ajñānād ity abhimantrya viprāya dadyāt ||
4.2.d: अपरिमितगुणान् तिलान् सौवर्णमये ताम्रमये वा पात्रे स्थापयित्वा यद् अज्ञानाद् इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य विप्राय दद्यात् ॥
4.2.m: Having placed an immeasurable quantity of sesame seeds in a vessel made of gold or copper, and having consecrated it with: 'Whatever out of ignorance...', he should give it to a brāhmaṇa.

4.2.s: yad ajñānāt tathā jñānād yan mayā śabalaṃ kṛtam | tat sarvaṃ tiladānena dahyatām iti hi prabho ||
4.2.d: यद् अज्ञानात् तथा ज्ञानाद् यन् मया शबलं कृतम् । तत् सर्वं तिलदानेन दह्यताम् इति हि प्रभो ॥
4.2.m: 'Whatever blemish was committed by me out of ignorance or out of knowledge, / let all that be burnt by the gift of sesame, O Lord!'

4.2.s: bhūmiś ca sasyasaṃpannā brāhmaṇe vedapārage | yathāśakti pradeyā hi bṛhaspativaco yathā ||
4.2.d: भूमिश् च सस्यसंपन्ना ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे । यथाशक्ति प्रदेया हि बृहस्पतिवचो यथा ॥
4.2.m: And land endowed with crops should indeed be given to a brāhmaṇa who has crossed to the end of the Veda, / according to one's ability, in accordance with the word of Bṛhaspati.

4.2.s: sa bhuktvā vividhān bhogān saptasāgaramekhalām | pṛthivīṃ prāpya modeta candravat pṛthivīpatiḥ ||
4.2.d: स भुक्त्वा विविधान् भोगान् सप्तसागरमेखलाम् । पृथिवीं प्राप्य मोदेत चन्द्रवत् पृथिवीपतिः ॥
4.2.m: Having enjoyed various pleasures, having obtained the earth / encircled by the seven oceans, that lord of the earth would rejoice like the moon.

4.2.s: annaṃ tu vividhaṃ nityaṃ pradadyāt dvijātaye | tūryaghoṣeṇa saṃyuktaḥ kṛtasvastyayanas tathā ||
4.2.d: अन्नं तु विविधं नित्यं प्रदद्यात् द्विजातये । तूर्यघोषेण संयुक्तः कृतस्वस्त्ययनस् तथा ॥
4.2.m: He should constantly present diverse foods to the twice-born, / accompanied by the sound of musical instruments, and having auspicious blessings performed.

4.2.s: gṛhadevāṃs tu saṃpūjya kāryaś cāpy utsavo gṛhe | chattrādīni ca yānāni pūjayed vidhivat svayam ||
4.2.d: गृहदेवांस् तु संपूज्य कार्यश् चाप्य् उत्सवो गृहे । छत्त्रादीनि च यानानि पूजयेद् विधिवत् स्वयम् ॥
4.2.m: And having worshipped the household deities, a festival should be held in the home; / and he himself should properly worship the parasol, other royal insignia, and conveyances.

4.2.s: puṣpaiś ca vividhaiḥ śubhraiḥ phalaiś cāpy arcayed budhaḥ tasmāt sarvāṇi satataṃ dānāni tu mahīpatiḥ | dattvā śraddhānvito viprair vṛto bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ ||
4.2.d: पुष्पैश् च विविधैः शुभ्रैः फलैश् चाप्य् अर्चयेद् बुधः तस्मात् सर्वाणि सततं दानानि तु महीपतिः । दत्त्वा श्रद्धान्वितो विप्रैर् वृतो भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥
4.2.m: [And the wise man should worship with various radiant flowers and fruits;] / therefore, the king, having continually made all gifts with faith, / surrounded by brāhmaṇas, should eat with restrained speech.

4.3.s: atha piṣṭamayīṃ rātriṃ caturbhir dīpakaiḥ saha | arcitāṃ gandhamālyena sthāpayet tasya cāgrataḥ ||
4.3.d: अथ पिष्टमयीं रात्रिं चतुर्भिर् दीपकैः सह । अर्चितां गन्धमाल्येन स्थापयेत् तस्य चाग्रतः ॥
4.3.m: Then he should set up before him [an effigy of] Night made of flour, together with four lamps, / worshipped with fragrant unguents and garlands.

4.3.s: namas kṛtvā tato rātrim arcayitvā yathāvidhi | dhūpena cānnapānena stotreṇa ca samarcayet ||
4.3.d: नमस् कृत्वा ततो रात्रिम् अर्चयित्वा यथाविधि । धूपेन चान्नपानेन स्तोत्रेण च समर्चयेत् ॥
4.3.m: Then, having bowed to Night and worshipped her according to rule, / he should venerate her with incense, food, drink, and a hymn of praise:

4.3.s: pāhi māṃ satataṃ devi sarāṣṭraṃ sasuhṛjjanam | uṣase naḥ prayacchasva śāntiṃ ca kṛṇu me sadā | ye tvāṃ prapadyante devi na teṣāṃ vidyate bhayam ||
4.3.d: पाहि मां सततं देवि सराष्ट्रं ससुहृज्जनम् । उषसे नः प्रयच्छस्व शान्तिं च कृणु मे सदा । ये त्वां प्रपद्यन्ते देवि न तेषां विद्यते भयम् ॥
4.3.m: 'Protect me always, O goddess, together with my realm and friends; / deliver us to the dawn, and always make peace for me; / for those who take refuge in you, O goddess, no fear exists.

4.3.s: rātriṃ prapadye jananīṃ sarvabhūtaniveśanīm | bhadrāṃ bhagavatīṃ kṛṣṇāṃ viśvasya jagato niśām ||
4.3.d: रात्रिं प्रपद्ये जननीं सर्वभूतनिवेशनीम् । भद्रां भगवतीं कृष्णां विश्वस्य जगतो निशाम् ॥
4.3.m: I take refuge in Night, the mother, who causes all beings to rest, / the auspicious, the divine, the dark, the night of the entire world.

4.3.s: saṃveśanīṃ saṃyamanīṃ grahanakṣatramālinīm | prapanno 'haṃ śivāṃ rātriṃ bhadre pāram aśīmahi ||
4.3.d: संवेशनीं संयमनीं ग्रहनक्षत्रमालिनीम् । प्रपन्नो ऽहं शिवां रात्रिं भद्रे पारम् अशीमहि ॥
4.3.m: Her who brings to rest, who restrains, garlanded with planets and lunar mansions, / in the auspicious Night I have taken refuge; O auspicious one, may we reach the other shore!

4.3.s: yāṃ sadā sarvabhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca | sāyaṃ prātar namasyanti sā māṃ rātry abhirakṣatv iti ||
4.3.d: यां सदा सर्वभूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च । सायं प्रातर् नमस्यन्ति सा मां रात्र्य् अभिरक्षत्व् इति ॥
4.3.m: Whom all beings, both motionless and moving, / constantly revere evening and morning, let that Night protect me!'

4.4.s: ā rātri pārthivam iṣirā yoṣā trāyamāna ity rātryāṇi ||
4.4.d: आ रात्रि पार्थिवम् इषिरा योषा त्रायमान इत्य् रात्र्याणि ॥
4.4.m: The Night-hymns are: 'Into the earthly space, O Night...', 'The active maiden...', and 'The saving...'

4.4.s: mamobhā mahyam āpa iti sūktābhyām anvālabhya japet ||
4.4.d: ममोभा मह्यम् आप इति सूक्ताभ्याम् अन्वालभ्य जपेत् ॥
4.4.m: Touching [the king], he should murmur the two hymns: 'Both mine...' and 'The waters to me...'

4.4.s: yo naḥ sva iti pañcabhiḥ sarṣapāñ juhuyāt ||
4.4.d: यो नः स्व इति पञ्चभिः सर्षपाञ् जुहुयात् ॥
4.4.m: With the five [stanzas beginning with] 'He who is our own...', he should offer mustard seeds into the fire.

4.4.s: yo 'smin yas tvā mātur iti dīpena nṛpasyopari triṣ parihṛtya praiṣakṛte prayacchet ||
4.4.d: यो ऽस्मिन् यस् त्वा मातुर् इति दीपेन नृपस्योपरि त्रिष् परिहृत्य प्रैषकृते प्रयच्छेत् ॥
4.4.m: Having circled [the lamp] three times over the king with the lamp to the accompaniment of 'He who in this...' and 'He who... from the mother', he should hand it to the messenger.

4.4.s: abhayam ity ṛcā catasraḥ śarkarāḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
4.4.d: अभयम् इत्य् ऋचा चतस्रः शर्कराः प्रदक्षिणं प्रतिदिशं क्षिपेत् ॥
4.4.m: With the verse 'Fearlessness...', he should cast four pebbles clockwise in every direction.

4.4.s: ehy aśmānam ā tiṣṭheti pañcamīm adhiṣṭhāpayet ||
4.4.d: एह्य् अश्मानम् आ तिष्ठेति पञ्चमीम् अधिष्ठापयेत् ॥
4.4.m: With 'Come, step upon the stone...', he should make him stand on the fifth [stone].

4.4.s: na taṃ yakṣmā aitu deva iti guggulukuṣṭhadūpaṃ dadyāt ||
4.4.d: न तं यक्ष्मा ऐतु देव इति गुग्गुलुकुष्ठदूपं दद्यात् ॥
4.4.m: With 'Let not consumption approach him, O god...', he should offer incense of bdellium and costus.

4.4.s: yas te gandhas tryāyuṣam iti bhūtiṃ prayacchet ||
4.4.d: यस् ते गन्धस् त्र्यायुषम् इति भूतिं प्रयच्छेत् ॥
4.4.m: With 'Whatever fragrance is yours...' and 'A triple lifetime...', he should apply sacred ashes.
Having fastened an amulet with 'You are an undoer of hexes...',

4.4.s: agnir mā pātu vasubhiḥ purastād iti śarkarān pradakṣiṇaṃ pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
4.4.d: अग्निर् मा पातु वसुभिः पुरस्ताद् इति शर्करान् प्रदक्षिणं प्रतिदिशं क्षिपेत् ॥
4.4.m: he should cast pebbles clockwise in every direction with 'May Agni protect me from the east with the Vasus...'

4.4.s: bahir niḥsṛtyottareṇa gatvā bāhyenopaniṣkramya suhṛde kuryāc chraddadhate kuryāt ||
4.4.d: बहिर् निःसृत्योत्तरेण गत्वा बाह्येनोपनिष्क्रम्य सुहृदे कुर्याच् छ्रद्दधते कुर्यात् ॥
4.4.m: Going outside, having gone north, having stepped outside, he should perform it for a friend, he should perform it for one who has faith.
The nightly rite of fearlessness [according to] Paiṭhīnasi, son of Mausalī.

4.5.m: Now next we shall explain the ritual procedure for the Night-hymns.
The royal priest, pure and clad in white,

4.5.s: pārthivasya paścimāṃ saṃdhyām upāsya darbhaiḥ pavitrapāṇī rājānam abhigamya
4.5.d: पार्थिवस्य पश्चिमां संध्याम् उपास्य दर्भैः पवित्रपाणी राजानम् अभिगम्य
4.5.m: having performed the king's evening twilight devotion, holding sacred darbha-grass in his hands, having approached the king,
having fashioned [an effigy of] Night made of flour,
having worshipped her with food, drink, incense, lamps, and garlands,
having worshipped her with four burning lamps,

4.5.s: ā rātri pārthivam iṣirā yoṣeti sūktadvayena rātrim upasthāya ||
4.5.d: आ रात्रि पार्थिवम् इषिरा योषेति सूक्तद्वयेन रात्रिम् उपस्थाय ॥
4.5.m: having attended upon Night with the two hymns 'Into the earthly space, O Night...' and 'The active maiden...',

4.5.s: trāyamāṇe viśvajite ahne ca tveti rājānaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ triḥ kṛtvā
4.5.d: त्रायमाणे विश्वजिते अह्ने च त्वेति राजानं प्रदक्षिणं त्रिः कृत्वा
4.5.m: having circumambulated the king three times with 'O saving, all-conquering one' and 'To the day and you',
having dismissed [the effigy] at the door of the royal palace,

4.5.s: na taṃ yakṣmā aitu deva iti guggulukuṣṭhadhūpaṃ dadyād
4.5.d: न तं यक्ष्मा ऐतु देव इति गुग्गुलुकुष्ठधूपं दद्याद्
4.5.m: he should offer incense of bdellium and costus with 'Let not consumption approach him, O god...'

4.5.s: yas te gandha iti bhūtim abhimantrya
4.5.d: यस् ते गन्ध इति भूतिम् अभिमन्त्र्य
4.5.m: Having consecrated sacred ashes with 'Whatever fragrance is yours...',
having made protection for the king with 'A triple lifetime...',

4.5.s: asapatnam iti śarkarām abhimantryāṅguṣṭhāt pradakṣiṇaṃ pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
4.5.d: असपत्नम् इति शर्कराम् अभिमन्त्र्याङ्गुष्ठात् प्रदक्षिणं प्रतिदिशं क्षिपेत् ॥
4.5.m: having consecrated a pebble with 'Rival-free...', he should throw it from his thumb clockwise in each direction.

4.5.s: śāntā dyaur iti japitvā rājānaṃ vāsagṛhaṃ nayet ||
4.5.d: शान्ता द्यौर् इति जपित्वा राजानं वासगृहं नयेत् ॥
4.5.m: Having murmured 'Peaceful is the sky...', he should lead the king to his bedchamber.
Having made protection with sacred ashes, having stepped outside,
he should perform it thus day after day.

4.6.s: yasya rājño janapade atharvā śāntipāragaḥ | nivasaty api tad rāṣṭraṃ vardhate nirupadravam ||
4.6.d: यस्य राज्ञो जनपदे अथर्वा शान्तिपारगः । निवसत्य् अपि तद् राष्ट्रं वर्धते निरुपद्रवम् ॥
4.6.m: In whose realm an Atharvan priest who has mastered propitiatory rites resides, / that king's realm flourishes free of calamities.

4.6.s: yasya rājño janapade sa nāsti vividhair bhayaiḥ | pīḍyate tasya tad rāṣṭraṃ paṅke gaur iva majjati ||
4.6.d: यस्य राज्ञो जनपदे स नास्ति विविधैर् भयैः । पीड्यते तस्य तद् राष्ट्रं पङ्के गौर् इव मज्जति ॥
4.6.m: In whose realm such a priest does not exist, that king's realm / is afflicted by various fears and sinks like a cow in the mud.

4.6.s: tasmād rājā viśeṣeṇa atharvāṇaṃ jitendriyam | dānasaṃmānasatkārair nityaṃ samabhipūjayet ||
4.6.d: तस्माद् राजा विशेषेण अथर्वाणं जितेन्द्रियम् । दानसंमानसत्कारैर् नित्यं समभिपूजयेत् ॥
4.6.m: Therefore, a king should constantly and especially honor / a self-controlled Atharvan priest with gifts, honor, and hospitality.

4.6.s: nityaṃ ca kārayec chāntiṃ grahaṛkṣāṇi pūjayet | bhūmidohān prakurvīta devatāyataneṣu ca ||
4.6.d: नित्यं च कारयेच् छान्तिं ग्रहऋक्षाणि पूजयेत् । भूमिदोहान् प्रकुर्वीत देवतायतनेषु च ॥
4.6.m: And he should constantly have propitiatory rites performed, worship the planets and lunar mansions, / and carry out milking-rites of the earth in the temples of deities.

4.6.s: catuspatheṣu goṣṭheṣu tīrtheṣv apsu ca kārayet | gotarpaṇaṃ ca vidhivat sarvadoṣavināśanam ||
4.6.d: चतुस्पथेषु गोष्ठेषु तीर्थेष्व् अप्सु च कारयेत् । गोतर्पणं च विधिवत् सर्वदोषविनाशनम् ॥
4.6.m: At crossroads, in cowpens, at bathing places, and at waters, he should have performed / the proper water libation for cows, which destroys all defects.

4.6.s: ya evaṃ kārayed rājā sarvakālaṃ jitendriyaḥ | anantaṃ sukham āpanoti kṛtsnāṃ bhuṅkte vasuṃdharām || iti purohitakarmāṇi samāptāni ||
4.6.d: य एवं कारयेद् राजा सर्वकालं जितेन्द्रियः । अनन्तं सुखम् आपनोति कृत्स्नां भुङ्क्ते वसुंधराम् ॥ इति पुरोहितकर्माणि समाप्तानि ॥
4.6.m:
A king who, having mastered his senses, has this performed at all times, / attains endless happiness and enjoys the entire earth.

Thus the duties of the royal priest are completed.

5.1.s: om atha puṣyābhiṣekasya vidhiṃ vakṣyāmi sāṃpadam | dharmārthakāmasaṃyuktaṃ rājā kuryāt purohitam ||
5.1.d: ओम् अथ पुष्याभिषेकस्य विधिं वक्ष्यामि सांपदम् । धर्मार्थकामसंयुक्तं राजा कुर्यात् पुरोहितम् ॥
5.1.m: Om. Now I shall declare the rite of consecration under Puṣya, which brings success; / the king should appoint a royal priest endowed with dharma, material gain, and desire.

5.1.s: sauvarṇarājatais tāmraiḥ kalaśaiḥ pārthivair api | sahasreṇa śatenātha toyagrahaṇam iṣyate ||
5.1.d: सौवर्णराजतैस् ताम्रैः कलशैः पार्थिवैर् अपि । सहस्रेण शतेनाथ तोयग्रहणम् इष्यते ॥
5.1.m: The gathering of water is desired with golden, silver, copper, / and earthenware jars, either by a thousand or by a hundred,

5.1.s: caturṇāṃ sāgarāṇāṃ tu nadīnāṃ ca śatasya tu | abhiṣekāya rājñas tu toyam āhṛtya yatnataḥ ||
5.1.d: चतुर्णां सागराणां तु नदीनां च शतस्य तु । अभिषेकाय राज्ञस् तु तोयम् आहृत्य यत्नतः ॥
5.1.m: having diligently brought water from the four oceans / and from a hundred rivers for the consecration of the king,

5.1.s: ekadvitricaturṇāṃ vā sāgarasya tu pañcamam | oṣadhīs teṣu sarveṣu kalaśeṣūpakalpayet ||
5.1.d: एकद्वित्रिचतुर्णां वा सागरस्य तु पञ्चमम् । ओषधीस् तेषु सर्वेषु कलशेषूपकल्पयेत् ॥
5.1.m: or from one, two, three, or four [rivers], and fifth from an ocean; / he should place medicinal herbs in all those jars.

5.1.s: sahā ca dahadevī ca balā cātibalā tathā | madayantī vacā śvetā vyāghradantī sumaṅgalā ||
5.1.d: सहा च दहदेवी च बला चातिबला तथा । मदयन्ती वचा श्वेता व्याघ्रदन्ती सुमङ्गला ॥
5.1.m: and sahā, dahadevī, balā, and atibalā, / madayantī, vacā, śvetā, vyāghradantī, sumaṅgalā,

5.2.s: śatāvarī jayantī ca śatapuṣpā sacandanā | priyaṅgū rocano aśīram amṛtā ca sasārikā ||
5.2.d: शतावरी जयन्ती च शतपुष्पा सचन्दना । प्रियङ्गू रोचनो अशीरम् अमृता च ससारिका ॥
5.2.m: śatāvarī, jayantī, śatapuṣpā along with candana, / priyaṅgu, rocana, uśīra, and amṛtā along with sārikā,

5.2.s: aśvatthaplakṣabilvānāṃ nyagrodhapanasasya ca | śirīṣāmrakapitthānāṃ pallavaiḥ samalaṃkṛtān ||
5.2.d: अश्वत्थप्लक्षबिल्वानां न्यग्रोधपनसस्य च । शिरीषाम्रकपित्थानां पल्लवैः समलंकृतान् ॥
5.2.m: adorned with sprouts of aśvattha, plakṣa, bilva, / nyagrodha, panasa, / śirīṣa, āmra, and kapittha,

5.2.s: hemaratnauṣadhībilvapuṣpagandhādhivāsitān | ācchāditān sitair vastrair abhimantrya purohitaḥ ||
5.2.d: हेमरत्नौषधीबिल्वपुष्पगन्धाधिवासितान् । आच्छादितान् सितैर् वस्त्रैर् अभिमन्त्र्य पुरोहितः ॥
5.2.m: scented with gold, jewels, herbs, bilva, flowers, and perfumes, / covered with white cloths—the purohita, having consecrated them with mantras,

5.2.s: sāvitry ubhayataḥ kuryāc chaṃ no devī tathaiva ca | hiraṇyavarṇāḥ sūktaṃ ca anuvākādyam eva ca ||
5.2.d: सावित्र्य् उभयतः कुर्याच् छं नो देवी तथैव च । हिरण्यवर्णाः सूक्तं च अनुवाकाद्यम् एव च ॥
5.2.m: should perform [the rite] with the Sāvitrī on both sides, and likewise the [hymn] "śaṃ no devīḥ", / the hymn "hiraṇyavarṇāḥ", and the first anuvāka.

5.2.s: dharaṇī pādapīṭhaṃ syād dūrvāmūlāṅkurān śubhān | tasyopari nyaset pīṭhaṃ haimaṃ raupyam athāpi vā ||
5.2.d: धरणी पादपीठं स्याद् दूर्वामूलाङ्कुरान् शुभान् । तस्योपरि न्यसेत् पीठं हैमं रौप्यम् अथापि वा ॥
5.2.m: The footstool should be [placed on] the earth, with auspicious dūrvā grass roots and sprouts; / upon it he should place a stool made of gold or silver.

5.3.s: anaḍudvyāghrasiṃhānāṃ mṛgasya ca yathākramam | catvāri carmāṇy etāni pūrvād ārabhya vinyaset ||
5.3.d: अनडुद्व्याघ्रसिंहानां मृगस्य च यथाक्रमम् । चत्वारि चर्माण्य् एतानि पूर्वाद् आरभ्य विन्यसेत् ॥
5.3.m: Of an ox, a tiger, a lion, / and a deer, respectively: / he should lay out these four skins beginning from the east.

5.3.s: cāturhotravidhānena juhuyāc ca purohitaḥ | caturdikṣu sthitair viprair vedavedāṅgapāragaiḥ ||
5.3.d: चातुर्होत्रविधानेन जुहुयाच् च पुरोहितः । चतुर्दिक्षु स्थितैर् विप्रैर् वेदवेदाङ्गपारगैः ॥
5.3.m: And according to the rules of the fourfold priesthood, the purohita should offer oblations, / with Brahmins situated in the four directions who have mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

5.3.s: bilvāhāraḥ phalāhāraḥ payasā vāpi vartayet | saptarātraṃ ghṛtāśī va tato homaṃ prayojayet ||
5.3.d: बिल्वाहारः फलाहारः पयसा वापि वर्तयेत् । सप्तरात्रं घृताशी व ततो होमं प्रयोजयेत् ॥
5.3.m: Subsisting on bilva, subsisting on fruits, or living on milk, / or eating ghee for seven nights, he should then perform the fire oblation.

5.3.s: gavyena payasā kuryāt sauvarṇena sruveṇa tu | vedānām ādibhir mantrair mahāvyāhṛtipūrvakaiḥ ||
5.3.d: गव्येन पयसा कुर्यात् सौवर्णेन स्रुवेण तु । वेदानाम् आदिभिर् मन्त्रैर् महाव्याहृतिपूर्वकैः ॥
5.3.m: He should perform it with cow's milk using a golden ladle, / with the beginning mantras of the Vedas preceded by the great utterances.

5.3.s: śarmavarmā gaṇaś caiva tathā syād aparājitaḥ | āyuṣyaś cābhayaś caiva tathā svastyayano gaṇaḥ ||
5.3.d: शर्मवर्मा गणश् चैव तथा स्याद् अपराजितः । आयुष्यश् चाभयश् चैव तथा स्वस्त्ययनो गणः ॥
5.3.m: The Śarmavarman hymn cycle, and likewise the Aparājita, / the Āyuṣya, the Abhaya, and likewise the Svastyayana hymn cycle—

5.4.s: etān pañca gaṇān hutvā vācayeta dvijottamān | hiraṇyenākṣatārgheṇa phalaiś ca madhusarpiṣā ||
5.4.d: एतान् पञ्च गणान् हुत्वा वाचयेत द्विजोत्तमान् । हिरण्येनाक्षतार्घेण फलैश् च मधुसर्पिषा ॥
5.4.m: having offered oblations with these five hymn cycles, he should have the best of the twice-born recite blessings, / with gold, unhusked barley water-reception gifts, fruits, and honey and ghee.

5.4.s: puṇyāhaṃ vācayitvāsya ārambhaṃ kārayed budhaḥ | tiṣyanakṣatrasaṃyukte mahūrte karaṇe śubhe ||
5.4.d: पुण्याहं वाचयित्वास्य आरम्भं कारयेद् बुधः । तिष्यनक्षत्रसंयुक्ते महूर्ते करणे शुभे ॥
5.4.m: Having had them recite the 'auspicious day' blessing, the wise [priest] should have him begin the rite / at a moment conjoined with the lunar mansion Puṣya, during an auspicious karaṇa.

5.4.s: uccairghoṣa iti tūryāṇy abhimantrya purohitaḥ | sarvatūryaninādena abhiṣikto hy alaṃkṛtaḥ ||
5.4.d: उच्चैर्घोष इति तूर्याण्य् अभिमन्त्र्य पुरोहितः । सर्वतूर्यनिनादेन अभिषिक्तो ह्य् अलंकृतः ॥
5.4.m: The purohita, having consecrated the musical instruments with the hymn "uccairghoṣa", / consecrated and adorned, to the sound of all musical instruments,

5.4.s: siṃhāsanaṃ samāruhya pīṭhikāṃ vā yathākramam | cāmarachattrasaṃyuktaṃ pratihāravibhūṣitam ||
5.4.d: सिंहासनं समारुह्य पीठिकां वा यथाक्रमम् । चामरछत्त्रसंयुक्तं प्रतिहारविभूषितम् ॥
5.4.m: having mounted the lion-throne or stool in due order, / furnished with chowrie and parasol, graced by the chamberlain—

5.4.s: mattadvipacatuṣkaṃ ca caturdikṣu prakalpayet | upaviṣṭas tato rājā prajānāṃ kārayed dhitam | akarā brāhmaṇā gāvaḥ strībālajaḍarogiṇaḥ ||
5.4.d: मत्तद्विपचतुष्कं च चतुर्दिक्षु प्रकल्पयेत् । उपविष्टस् ततो राजा प्रजानां कारयेद् धितम् । अकरा ब्राह्मणा गावः स्त्रीबालजडरोगिणः ॥
5.4.m: and he should place four rutting elephants in the four directions. / The king, seated then, should work for the welfare of his subjects: / tax-free Brahmins, cows, women, children, the simple, and the sick.

5.5.s: tatas tu darśanaṃ deyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ nṛpeṇa tu | śreṇīprakṛtimukhyānāṃ strījanaṃ ca namaskaret ||
5.5.d: ततस् तु दर्शनं देयं ब्राह्मणानां नृपेण तु । श्रेणीप्रकृतिमुख्यानां स्त्रीजनं च नमस्करेत् ॥
5.5.m: Then audience must be granted by the king to the Brahmins, / and to the chiefs of the guilds and subjects; and he should bow to the women.

5.5.s: āśiṣas te hi dāsyanti tuṣṭā janapadā bhuvi | evaṃ prajānurajyeta pṛthivī ca vaśā bhavet ||
5.5.d: आशिषस् ते हि दास्यन्ति तुष्टा जनपदा भुवि । एवं प्रजानुरज्येत पृथिवी च वशा भवेत् ॥
5.5.m: For they, the pleased subjects in the realm, will grant blessings. / In this way the subjects will be pleased, and the earth will come under his control.

5.5.s: purohitaṃ mantriṇaṃ ca senādhyakṣaṃ tathaiva ca | aśvādhyakṣaṃ gajādhyakṣaṃ koṣṭhāgārapatiṃ tathā ||
5.5.d: पुरोहितं मन्त्रिणं च सेनाध्यक्षं तथैव च । अश्वाध्यक्षं गजाध्यक्षं कोष्ठागारपतिं तथा ॥
5.5.m: The purohita, the minister, and likewise the commander of the army, / the master of the horse, the master of the elephants, and the master of the storehouse,

5.5.s: bhāṇḍāgārapatiṃ vaidyaṃ daivajñaṃ ca yathākramam | yathārheṇa ca yogena sarvān saṃpūjayen nṛpaḥ ||
5.5.d: भाण्डागारपतिं वैद्यं दैवज्ञं च यथाक्रमम् । यथार्हेण च योगेन सर्वान् संपूजयेन् नृपः ॥
5.5.m: the master of the treasury, the physician, and the astrologer in due order: / the king should honor all of them according to their worth with fitting gifts.

5.5.s: rājyaṃ purohite nyasya śeṣāṇāṃ ca yathākramam | sthānāntarāṇi cānyāni dattvā sukham avāpnuyāt ||
5.5.d: राज्यं पुरोहिते न्यस्य शेषाणां च यथाक्रमम् । स्थानान्तराणि चान्यानि दत्त्वा सुखम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
5.5.m: Having entrusted the kingdom to the purohita and assigned the other offices / to the rest in due order, he will obtain happiness.

5.5.s: dūrvāsiddhārthakān sarpiḥ śamīr vrīhiyavau tathā śuklāni caiva puṣpāṇi mūrdhni dadyāt purohitaḥ ||
5.5.d: दूर्वासिद्धार्थकान् सर्पिः शमीर् व्रीहियवौ तथा शुक्लानि चैव पुष्पाणि मूर्ध्नि दद्यात् पुरोहितः ॥
5.5.m: The purohita should place dūrvā grass, white mustard seeds, ghee, / śamī leaves, rice and barley, and white flowers upon [the king's] head.

5.5.s: atharvavihito hy eṣa vidhiḥ puṣyābhiṣecane | rājā snāto mahīṃ bhuṅkte śakralokaṃ sa gacchati || iti puṣyābhiṣekaḥ ||
5.5.d: अथर्वविहितो ह्य् एष विधिः पुष्याभिषेचने । राजा स्नातो महीं भुङ्क्ते शक्रलोकं स गच्छति ॥ इति पुष्याभिषेकः ॥
5.5.m: For this is the rule prescribed in the Atharvan regarding the consecration during Puṣya; / the king, bathed, enjoys the earth and goes to the realm of Śakra.

6.1.m: Om. Now then we will explain the ordinance of Piṣṭarātrī.

6.1.s: ahatavāsāḥ purastāt talpasya gomayena sthaṇḍilam upalipya
6.1.d: अहतवासाः पुरस्तात् तल्पस्य गोमयेन स्थण्डिलम् उपलिप्य
6.1.m: Wearing unwashed clothes, having smeared a mound with cow dung in front of the bed,
[and] having covered the lion-throne with an unwashed cloth,

6.1.s: yāṃ devāḥ prati nandantīti rātrim āvāhayet ||
6.1.d: यां देवाः प्रति नन्दन्तीति रात्रिम् आवाहयेत् ॥
6.1.m: he should invoke Night with: "She whom the gods greet with joy..."

6.1.s: saṃvatsarasya pratimām iti piṣṭamayīṃ pratikṛtiṃ kṛtvodanmukhīm upaveśayet ||
6.1.d: संवत्सरस्य प्रतिमाम् इति पिष्टमयीं प्रतिकृतिं कृत्वोदन्मुखीम् उपवेशयेत् ॥
6.1.m: Having made an effigy consisting of flour with: "Image of the year...", he should seat it facing north.

6.1.s: chattraṃ hiraṇmayaṃ dadyād āsanaṃ ca hiraṇmayam | dadyāc chubhrāṇi vāsāṃsi śubhraṃ caivānulepanam ||
6.1.d: छत्त्रं हिरण्मयं दद्याद् आसनं च हिरण्मयम् । दद्याच् छुभ्राणि वासांसि शुभ्रं चैवानुलेपनम् ॥
6.1.m: He should present a golden parasol and a golden seat; / he should present white garments and white ointment,

6.1.s: śubhram annam atathā dadyāt prabhūtāṃś caiva modakān | dhūpaṃ ca vividhaṃ nityaṃ pradīpāṃś ca prakalpayet ||
6.1.d: शुभ्रम् अन्नम् अतथा दद्यात् प्रभूतांश् चैव मोदकान् । धूपं च विविधं नित्यं प्रदीपांश् च प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
6.1.m: he should present white food and abundant sweet dumplings, / and he should regularly provide various kinds of incense and lamps.

6.1.s: ā mā puṣṭe ca poṣe cety etābhir upasthāya ||
6.1.d: आ मा पुष्टे च पोषे चेत्य् एताभिर् उपस्थाय ॥
6.1.m: Having worshipped with these verses: "Into me, in nourishment and thriving...",
having consecrated mustard seeds with demon-destroying mantras,

6.1.s: āvatas ta iti japan samantāt talpasyāvakīrya
6.1.d: आवतस् त इति जपन् समन्तात् तल्पस्यावकीर्य
6.1.m: whispering: "From near and far to you...", having scattered them all around the bed,

6.1.s: ayaṃ pratisara iti pratisaram ābadhya śarkarān pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
6.1.d: अयं प्रतिसर इति प्रतिसरम् आबध्य शर्करान् प्रतिदिशं क्षिपेत् ॥
6.1.m: having tied on the protective amulet with: "This amulet...", he should throw sugar crystals in each direction.
He should give the remains of the incense to the king.

6.1.s: paścāt sarveṣu koneṣu dvimukhīm ekamukhīṃ vā | sarvato vijayāṃ rakṣām ekāṃ vā teṣu caturmukhīm ||
