6.1.d: पश्चात् सर्वेषु कोनेषु द्विमुखीम् एकमुखीं वा । सर्वतो विजयां रक्षाम् एकां वा तेषु चतुर्मुखीम् ॥
6.1.m: Afterwards, in all corners, [an effigy] having two faces or one face; / [he should place] a Vijayā defense on all sides, or one four-faced [effigy] among them,
or one-faced everywhere, with the recitation of the Apratiratha hymn, according to some;
and the throwing of sugar crystals everywhere.

6.2.m: Taking the flour-night [effigy], he should cast it away at the door of the residence.

6.2.s: vanaspatir aso madhya iti guggulukuṣṭhadhūpaṃ dadyād
6.2.d: वनस्पतिर् असो मध्य इति गुग्गुलुकुष्ठधूपं दद्याद्
6.2.m: He should offer incense of bdellium and costus with: "Lord of the forest...";

6.2.s: yas te gandha iti bhūtim abhimantrya
6.2.d: यस् ते गन्ध इति भूतिम् अभिमन्त्र्य
6.2.m: having consecrated the sacred ashes with: "What fragrance of yours...";
having made a defense for the king with: "Triple lifetime...";

6.2.s: asapatnam iti śarkarān abhimantryāṅguṣṭhād abhipradakṣiṇaṃ pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
6.2.d: असपत्नम् इति शर्करान् अभिमन्त्र्याङ्गुष्ठाद् अभिप्रदक्षिणं प्रतिदिशं क्षिपेत् ॥
6.2.m: having consecrated the sugar crystals with: "Free from rivals...", he should throw them from the thumb clockwise in each direction.

6.2.s: śāntā dyaur iti japitvā rājānaṃ vāsagṛhaṃ nayet ||
6.2.d: शान्ता द्यौर् इति जपित्वा राजानं वासगृहं नयेत् ॥
6.2.m: Having whispered: "Calm is the sky...", he should lead the king to his bedchamber.
Having made a defense with the sacred ashes, having gone out,

6.2.s: evamevam ahar ahaḥ kuryād iti || piṣṭarātryāḥ kalpaḥ samāptaḥ ||
6.2.d: एवमेवम् अहर् अहः कुर्याद् इति ॥ पिष्टरात्र्याः कल्पः समाप्तः ॥
6.2.m: he should do this each day. Thus ends the ordinance of Piṣṭarātrī.

7.1.s: oṃ na suṣvāpa purā śakro dānavānāṃ purodhasā | prayuktair auṣadhair yogair mantrāṇāṃ japahomataḥ ||
7.1.d: ओं न सुष्वाप पुरा शक्रो दानवानां पुरोधसा । प्रयुक्तैर् औषधैर् योगैर् मन्त्राणां जपहोमतः ॥
7.1.m: Om. In ancient times Śakra could not sleep, because of the herbs and devices / employed by the purohita of the Dānavas through the chanting and fire-offering of mantras.

7.1.s: praṇipatya bṛhaspatim atharvāṇaṃ puraṃdaraḥ | dānavaiḥ paribhūto 'haṃ trāhi mām ity uvāca ha ||
7.1.d: प्रणिपत्य बृहस्पतिम् अथर्वाणं पुरंदरः । दानवैः परिभूतो ऽहं त्राहि माम् इत्य् उवाच ह ॥
7.1.m: Bowing down before Bṛhaspati, the Atharvan, Puraṃdara / said: "I am overcome by the Dānavas; protect me!"

7.1.s: tato 'sāv evam uktas tu prabhūtabalavardhanam | ārogyadaṃ bhūtikaraṃ kṣudropadravanāśanam ||
7.1.d: ततो ऽसाव् एवम् उक्तस् तु प्रभूतबलवर्धनम् । आरोग्यदं भूतिकरं क्षुद्रोपद्रवनाशनम् ॥
7.1.m: Then, thus addressed, he [said] that which promotes abundant strength, / gives health, creates prosperity, and destroys minor afflictions:

7.1.s: ārātrikaṃ hi kartavyaṃ tasya trātum idaṃ tadā | kṛtvā piṣṭamayaṃ dīpaṃ suvartisnehasaṃyutam ||
7.1.d: आरात्रिकं हि कर्तव्यं तस्य त्रातुम् इदं तदा । कृत्वा पिष्टमयं दीपं सुवर्तिस्नेहसंयुतम् ॥
7.1.m: "An evening wave-offering must indeed be performed then to protect him." / Having made a lamp consisting of flour, furnished with a fine wick and oil,

7.1.s: ati nihaḥ prānyān iti dvābhyām enaṃ pradīpayet | pātre sapuṣpe saṃsthāpya sarṣapāṃś ca sahākṣataiḥ ||
7.1.d: अति निहः प्रान्यान् इति द्वाभ्याम् एनं प्रदीपयेत् । पात्रे सपुष्पे संस्थाप्य सर्षपांश् च सहाक्षतैः ॥
7.1.m: he should light it with the two [verses]: "Surpassing all..."; / having placed it in a dish with flowers, mustard seeds along with unbroken grain,

7.1.s: priyaṅguṃ śatapuṣpāṃ ca dūrvāṃ caiva śatāvarīm | sapāpahāriṇīṃ bhūtiṃ tatraiva ca baliṃ nyaset ||
7.1.d: प्रियङ्गुं शतपुष्पां च दूर्वां चैव शतावरीम् । सपापहारिणीं भूतिं तत्रैव च बलिं न्यसेत् ॥
7.1.m: priyaṅgu, śatapuṣpā, dūrvā, and śatāvarī, / [and] sin-removing sacred ashes, he should place the offering right there.

7.1.s: apsarobhiḥ parivṛto gurur gatvā puraṃdaram | prāptasattvaṃ sumanasam āsane prānmukhaṃ sthitam ||
7.1.d: अप्सरोभिः परिवृतो गुरुर् गत्वा पुरंदरम् । प्राप्तसत्त्वं सुमनसम् आसने प्रान्मुखं स्थितम् ॥
7.1.m: Surrounded by Apsarases, the Guru, having gone to Puraṃdara / who had regained his strength, was cheerful, and was seated facing east upon a seat,

7.1.s: preto yantv ekaśataṃ ca dīpaṃ samabhimantrayet | triḥ paribhrāmayed rājño mantreṇātha sumaṅgalam ||
7.1.d: प्रेतो यन्त्व् एकशतं च दीपं समभिमन्त्रयेत् । त्रिः परिभ्रामयेद् राज्ञो मन्त्रेणाथ सुमङ्गलम् ॥
7.1.m: should consecrate the lamp with: "Let the departed go..." and the one hundred and one [mantras]; / he should then wave the highly auspicious [lamp] around the king three times with the mantra.

7.1.s: śāmyanty asya tato rogā grahā vighnavināyakāḥ | svasty astu nrparāṣṭrāya svasti gobrāhmaṇāya ca ||
7.1.d: शाम्यन्त्य् अस्य ततो रोगा ग्रहा विघ्नविनायकाः । स्वस्त्य् अस्तु न्र्पराष्ट्राय स्वस्ति गोब्राह्मणाय च ॥
7.1.m: His diseases, planets, and obstructive Vināyakas then become calm. / May there be welfare for the king and the realm, and welfare for cow and Brahmin!

7.1.s: tatas tu śaṅkhadhvaninā dīpaṃ gṛhītvā satoyadhārāṃ prayato 'pi nirharet | purohito jyotiṣiko 'pi vā svayaṃ hitaiṣinī dhātry atharvo pakāritā ||
7.1.d: ततस् तु शङ्खध्वनिना दीपं गृहीत्वा सतोयधारां प्रयतो ऽपि निर्हरेत् । पुरोहितो ज्योतिषिको ऽपि वा स्वयं हितैषिनी धात्र्य् अथर्वो पकारिता ॥
7.1.m: Then, to the sound of a conch, one should take the lamp and, keeping pure, carry it out along with a stream of water; either the royal domestic priest, the astrologer, or even herself, the well-wishing nurse instructed in the Atharvan rites.

7.1.s: ācāmyātha ha rājānam ācamyādau purohitaḥ | brāhmaṇāya yathāśakti rukmaṃ prātaḥ pradāpayet ||
7.1.d: आचाम्याथ ह राजानम् आचम्यादौ पुरोहितः । ब्राह्मणाय यथाशक्ति रुक्मं प्रातः प्रदापयेत् ॥
7.1.m: Then, having sipped water, the royal domestic priest should first have the king sip water, and should make him give gold to a Brahmin in the morning according to his means.

7.1.s: mūlakarmādikaṃ tasya pañcaguhyakakāritam | bhayaṃ rājño na bhavati tejo vīryaṃ ca vardhate ||
7.1.d: मूलकर्मादिकं तस्य पञ्चगुह्यककारितम् । भयं राज्ञो न भवति तेजो वीर्यं च वर्धते ॥
7.1.m: Sorcery and the like wrought against him by the five Guhyakas causes no fear to the king, and his luster and vigor increase.

7.1.s: evaṃ vidhānam akhilaṃ vihitaṃ yathāvad etat samastaśubhadaṃ gaditaṃ nrpāṇām | naivāpadaḥ samupayānti nṛpaṃ kadā cid ārātrikaṃ pratiniśaṃ kriyate tu yasya || ity ārātrikaṃ samāptam ||
7.1.d: एवं विधानम् अखिलं विहितं यथावद् एतत् समस्तशुभदं गदितं न्र्पाणाम् । नैवापदः समुपयान्ति नृपं कदा चिद् आरात्रिकं प्रतिनिशं क्रियते तु यस्य ॥ इत्य् आरात्रिकं समाप्तम् ॥
7.1.m: Thus the entire rule has been duly laid down, declared as bestowing all auspiciousness upon kings. / Misfortunes never approach a king for whom the waving of lights is performed night after night. // Thus ends the waving of lights.

8.1.m: Om. Now we shall explain the gazing into ghee.

8.1.s: prātaḥprātaḥ śaṅkhadundubhinādena brahmaghoṣeṇa vā prabodhito rājā śayanagṛhād utthāyāparājitāṃ diśam abhiniṣkramyopādhyāyaṃ pratīkṣeta ||
8.1.d: प्रातःप्रातः शङ्खदुन्दुभिनादेन ब्रह्मघोषेण वा प्रबोधितो राजा शयनगृहाद् उत्थायापराजितां दिशम् अभिनिष्क्रम्योपाध्यायं प्रतीक्षेत ॥
8.1.m: Every morning, awakened by the sound of conches and kettledrums or by the recitation of the Veda, the king, having risen from his bedchamber and gone out towards the invincible direction [the northeast], should await his preceptor.

8.1.s: atha purohitaḥ snātānuliptaḥ śuciḥ śuklavāsāḥ krtamaṅgalaviracitoṣṇīṣī śāntigṛhaṃ praviśya devānāṃ namaskāraṃ kṛtvā svastivācanam anujñāpya vinītavad upaviśet ||
8.1.d: अथ पुरोहितः स्नातानुलिप्तः शुचिः शुक्लवासाः क्र्तमङ्गलविरचितोष्णीषी शान्तिगृहं प्रविश्य देवानां नमस्कारं कृत्वा स्वस्तिवाचनम् अनुज्ञाप्य विनीतवद् उपविशेत् ॥
8.1.m: Then the royal domestic priest, bathed, anointed, pure, clad in white garments, wearing a turban arranged for auspiciousness, having entered the propitiation chamber and made obeisance to the gods, having requested the recitation of benedictions, should sit down modestly.

8.1.s: yamasya lokād yathā kalāṃ yo na jīvo 'sīti svastyayanaṃ kṛtvollikhyābhyukṣya paristīrya śantātīyena tilān ghṛtāktān juhuyāt ||
8.1.d: यमस्य लोकाद् यथा कलां यो न जीवो ऽसीति स्वस्त्ययनं कृत्वोल्लिख्याभ्युक्ष्य परिस्तीर्य शन्तातीयेन तिलान् घृताक्तान् जुहुयात् ॥
8.1.m: Having performed the recitation for well-being with [the mantras] "From the realm of Yama...", "As a sixteenth part...", and "Who [is alive]...", "You are the living one...", having drawn the lines, sprinkled water, and spread the sacred grass around, he should sacrifice sesame seeds smeared with ghee with the Śantātīya hymn.

8.1.s: tān hutvā sauvarṇarājatam audumbaraṃ vā pātraṃ ghṛtapūrṇaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ ghṛtasya jūtiḥ sahasraśṛṅgo yamasya lokād uru viṣṇo vi kramasvety abhimantryājyaṃ teja iti tadālabhate ||
8.1.d: तान् हुत्वा सौवर्णराजतम् औदुम्बरं वा पात्रं घृतपूर्णं सहिरण्यं घृतस्य जूतिः सहस्रशृङ्गो यमस्य लोकाद् उरु विष्णो वि क्रमस्वेत्य् अभिमन्त्र्याज्यं तेज इति तदालभते ॥
8.1.m: Having sacrificed them, he consecrates a golden, silver, or udumbara-wood vessel full of ghee and containing gold with [the mantras] "The impulse of ghee...", "The thousand-horned...", "From the realm of Yama...", and "Stride widely, O Viṣṇu!", and touches it with [the verse] "Ghee is luster...".

8.1.s: ājyaṃ tejaḥ samuddiṣṭam ājyaṃ pāpaharaṃ param | ājyena devās trpyanti ājye lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ ||
8.1.d: आज्यं तेजः समुद्दिष्टम् आज्यं पापहरं परम् । आज्येन देवास् त्र्प्यन्ति आज्ये लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ॥
8.1.m: "Ghee has been declared to be luster; ghee is the supreme remover of sin. / By ghee the gods are gratified; in ghee the worlds are established.

8.1.s: bhaumāntarikṣadivyaṃ vā yat te kalmaṣam āgatam | sarvaṃ tad ājyasaṃsparśāt praṇāśam upagacchatv iti ||
8.1.d: भौमान्तरिक्षदिव्यं वा यत् ते कल्मषम् आगतम् । सर्वं तद् आज्यसंस्पर्शात् प्रणाशम् उपगच्छत्व् इति ॥
8.1.m: Whatever defilement has come to you, whether earthly, atmospheric, or celestial, / let all of that go to destruction through contact with ghee!"

8.1.s: tasmin ghṛtapātrasthaṃ hi sarvam ātmānaṃ ca paśyet ||
8.1.d: तस्मिन् घृतपात्रस्थं हि सर्वम् आत्मानं च पश्येत् ॥
8.1.m: Indeed, in that vessel of ghee, he should look upon all things and himself.
Having touched his head and heart with curds, he should mutter [the verses]:
with the two [verses] beginning with "Flying up high...".

8.1.s: sūryasyāvṛtam iti pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya śeṣaṃ kārayed ity
8.1.d: सूर्यस्यावृतम् इति प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्य शेषं कारयेद् इत्य्
8.1.m: Having turned around clockwise with [the mantra] "With the revolution of the sun...", he should have the remainder performed.

8.2.s: ayaṃ ghṛtāvekṣaṇasya prokto vidhir atharvaṇā | upāsyo nityakālaṃ tu rājñā vijayakāṅkṣiṇā ||
8.2.d: अयं घृतावेक्षणस्य प्रोक्तो विधिर् अथर्वणा । उपास्यो नित्यकालं तु राज्ञा विजयकाङ्क्षिणा ॥
8.2.m: "This procedure of gazing into ghee has been taught by the Atharvan; / it must be constantly observed by a king desiring victory.

8.2.s: etat samāharet sarvaṃ prayatas tu samāhitaḥ | rājā vijayate rāṣṭraṃ naśyante tasya śatravaḥ ||
8.2.d: एतत् समाहरेत् सर्वं प्रयतस् तु समाहितः । राजा विजयते राष्ट्रं नश्यन्ते तस्य शत्रवः ॥
8.2.m: Purified and attentive, he should assemble all this; / the king is victorious over the realm, and his enemies perish.

8.2.s: dvijottamāya kapilāṃ rājā dadyāt tu gāṃ śubhām | āśīrvādaṃ tatas tena śrutvā tanmukhaniḥsṛtam ||
8.2.d: द्विजोत्तमाय कपिलां राजा दद्यात् तु गां शुभाम् । आशीर्वादं ततस् तेन श्रुत्वा तन्मुखनिःसृतम् ॥
8.2.m: The king should bestow an auspicious brown cow upon the best of the twice-born; / then, having heard the blessing issuing from his mouth,

8.2.s: guruṇā vācito yasmād dīrgham āyur avāpnuyāt | putrān pautrāṃś ca maitrāṃś ca labhate nātrasaṃśayaḥ ||
8.2.d: गुरुणा वाचितो यस्माद् दीर्घम् आयुर् अवाप्नुयात् । पुत्रान् पौत्रांश् च मैत्रांश् च लभते नात्रसंशयः ॥
8.2.m: because he has been blessed by his guru, he will attain long life; / he obtains sons, grandsons, and allies: of this there is no doubt.

8.2.s: āyuṣyam atha varcasyaṃ saubhāgyaṃ śatrutāpanam | duḥsvapnanāśanaṃ puṇyaṃ ghṛtāsyāvekṣaṇaṃ smṛtam iti || iti ghṛtāvekṣaṇaṃ samāptam || śrīsāmba | yamasya lokād adhy ābabhūvitha iti ṛcaḥ, yathā kalāṃ yathā śapham iti ṛcaḥ, ghṛtasya jūtir iti ṛcaḥ ghṛtāvekṣaṇamadhye paippalādā mantrāḥ ||
8.2.d: आयुष्यम् अथ वर्चस्यं सौभाग्यं शत्रुतापनम् । दुःस्वप्ननाशनं पुण्यं घृतास्यावेक्षणं स्मृतम् इति ॥ इति घृतावेक्षणं समाप्तम् ॥ श्रीसाम्ब । यमस्य लोकाद् अध्य् आबभूविथ इति ऋचः, यथा कलां यथा शफम् इति ऋचः, घृतस्य जूतिर् इति ऋचः घृतावेक्षणमध्ये पैप्पलादा मन्त्राः ॥
8.2.m: Conferring long life, luster, good fortune, distressing enemies, / destroying bad dreams, and meritorious is the gazing into ghee traditionally declared." Thus ends the gazing into ghee. Homage to Sāmba. "From Yama's realm you originated" are 6 verses; "As a sixteenth part, as a hoof" are 6 verses; "The impulse of ghee" are 4 verses: these are Paippalāda mantras in the gazing into ghee.

9.1.s: om atha tiladhenuṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvapāpapraṇāśanīm | tilāḥ śvetās tilāḥ kṛṣṇās tilā gomūtravarṇakāḥ ||
9.1.d: ओम् अथ तिलधेनुं प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वपापप्रणाशनीम् । तिलाः श्वेतास् तिलाः कृष्णास् तिला गोमूत्रवर्णकाः ॥
9.1.m: Om. Now I shall proclaim the sesame cow that destroys all sins. / Sesame seeds are white, sesame seeds are black, and sesame seeds have the color of cow's urine.

9.1.s: tilānāṃ tu vicitrāṇāṃ dhenuṃ vatsaṃ ca kārayet | droṇasya vatsakaṃ kuryāc caturdroṇā tu gauḥ smṛtā ||
9.1.d: तिलानां तु विचित्राणां धेनुं वत्सं च कारयेत् । द्रोणस्य वत्सकं कुर्याच् चतुर्द्रोणा तु गौः स्मृता ॥
9.1.m: One should fashion a cow and a calf out of variegated sesame seeds: / one should make the calf with one droṇa, but the cow is traditionally remembered as made of four droṇas.

9.1.s: suvāsāyāṃ śucau bhūmau dhūpapuṣpair alaṃkrtā | kṛṣṇājine tu kartavyā bahūnāṃ vāpi kārayet ||
9.1.d: सुवासायां शुचौ भूमौ धूपपुष्पैर् अलंक्र्ता । कृष्णाजिने तु कर्तव्या बहूनां वापि कारयेत् ॥
9.1.m: Adorned with incense and flowers upon clean, well-perfumed ground, / she is to be made upon a black antelope skin; or one may make it with many [droṇas].

9.1.s: karṇau ratnamayau kuryāc cakṣuṣī dīpakau tathā | ghrāṇe tu sarvagndhāṃs tu jihvāyāṃ śāradaṃ ghṛtam ||
9.1.d: कर्णौ रत्नमयौ कुर्याच् चक्षुषी दीपकौ तथा । घ्राणे तु सर्वग्न्धांस् तु जिह्वायां शारदं घृतम् ॥
9.1.m: One should make the two ears of jewels, and likewise the two eyes of lamps; / all fragrant spices in the snout, and autumn ghee upon the tongue.

9.1.s: danteṣu mauktikaṃ dadyāl lalāṭe tāmrabhājanam | ūdhasi tu madhūśīram apāne ca ghṛtaṃ madhu ||
9.1.d: दन्तेषु मौक्तिकं दद्याल् ललाटे ताम्रभाजनम् । ऊधसि तु मधूशीरम् अपाने च घृतं मधु ॥
9.1.m: One should place pearls upon the teeth, a copper vessel on the forehead, / honey and uśīra-grass in the udder, and ghee and honey in the anus.

9.2.s: hṛdaye candanaṃ dadyāj jaṅghayor ikṣukāṇḍakam | suvarṇaśṛṅgī raupyakhurī raupyalāṅgūladakṣiṇā ||
9.2.d: हृदये चन्दनं दद्याज् जङ्घयोर् इक्षुकाण्डकम् । सुवर्णशृङ्गी रौप्यखुरी रौप्यलाङ्गूलदक्षिणा ॥
9.2.m: One should apply sandalwood paste to the heart, sugar-cane stalks for the shanks; / with golden horns, silver hooves, and a silver tail as the sacrificial fee,

9.2.s: vastrachannā tu dātavyā kāṃsyapātraṃ tu dohanī |
9.2.d: वस्त्रछन्ना तु दातव्या कांस्यपात्रं तु दोहनी ।
9.2.m: covered with a garment, she should be given, with a bell-metal vessel as the milking pail.
Having consecrated her with [the mantra] "And Prajāpati...", he should give her to a Brahmin.

9.2.s: dhenuṃ vatsaṃ ca yo dadyād vinātharvābhimantritām | vinānena vidhānena devatvaṃ nopajāyate ||
9.2.d: धेनुं वत्सं च यो दद्याद् विनाथर्वाभिमन्त्रिताम् । विनानेन विधानेन देवत्वं नोपजायते ॥
9.2.m: "He who would give a cow and a calf without being consecrated with the Atharvan, / without this rite, godhood does not arise [for him].

9.2.s: viśvarūpāḥ sthitāḥ sarvā dhenavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ | dhenutvaṃ na sa prayāti vinā sūktābhimantritām | niṣphalaṃ naśyate sarvaṃ vinābhimantritaṃ satām ||
9.2.d: विश्वरूपाः स्थिताः सर्वा धेनवः परिकीर्तिताः । धेनुत्वं न स प्रयाति विना सूक्ताभिमन्त्रिताम् । निष्फलं नश्यते सर्वं विनाभिमन्त्रितं सताम् ॥
9.2.m: All cows are proclaimed to stand as having universal forms; / it does not attain cownood without being consecrated with a hymn; / everything perishes without fruit for the good without being consecrated.

9.2.s: bālatve yac ca kaumāre yat pāpaṃ yauvane kṛtam | vayaḥpariṇatau yac ca yac ca janmāntareṣu ca ||
9.2.d: बालत्वे यच् च कौमारे यत् पापं यौवने कृतम् । वयःपरिणतौ यच् च यच् च जन्मान्तरेषु च ॥
9.2.m: Whatever sin was committed in childhood, in boyhood, or in youth, / and whatever in mature age, and whatever in other births,

9.2.s: yan niśāyāṃ tathā prātar yan madhyāhnāparāhṇayoḥ | saṃdhyayor yat kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ karmaṇā manasā girā ||
9.2.d: यन् निशायां तथा प्रातर् यन् मध्याह्नापराह्णयोः । संध्ययोर् यत् कृतं पापं कर्मणा मनसा गिरा ॥
9.2.m: whatever at night, likewise in the morning, whatever at midday and afternoon, / whatever sin was committed at the two twilights by deed, mind, or speech—

9.3.s: prasūyamānāṃ yo dhenuṃ dadyād brāhmaṇapuṃgave | kṛṣṇājinaṃ guḍadhenuṃ ghṛtadhenuṃ tathaiva ca ||
9.3.d: प्रसूयमानां यो धेनुं दद्याद् ब्राह्मणपुंगवे । कृष्णाजिनं गुडधेनुं घृतधेनुं तथैव च ॥
9.3.m: he who would give a cow in the act of calving to an eminent Brahmin, / or likewise a black antelope skin, a jaggery cow, or a ghee cow,

9.3.s: suvarṇaratnadhenuṃ ca jaladhenuṃ tathā parām | kṣīradhenuṃ madhudhenuṃ śarkarālavaṇaṃ tathā ||
9.3.d: सुवर्णरत्नधेनुं च जलधेनुं तथा पराम् । क्षीरधेनुं मधुधेनुं शर्करालवणं तथा ॥
9.3.m: and a golden-and-jeweled cow, and likewise another water cow, / a milk cow, a honey cow, likewise sugar and salt,

9.3.s: rasādidhenūḥ sarvānyā anena vidhinā smṛtāḥ | yat tu bālye kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yauvane caiva yat kṛtam ||
9.3.d: रसादिधेनूः सर्वान्या अनेन विधिना स्मृताः । यत् तु बाल्ये कृतं पापं यौवने चैव यत् कृतम् ॥
9.3.m: all other cows made of liquids and the like are traditionally declared according to this rule. / The sin that was committed in childhood, and that which was committed in youth,

9.3.s: mānakūṭaṃ tulākūṭaṃ kanyānṛtagavānṛtam | udake ṣṭhīvitaṃ caiva musalaṃ cāpi laṅghitam ||
9.3.d: मानकूटं तुलाकूटं कन्यानृतगवानृतम् । उदके ष्ठीवितं चैव मुसलं चापि लङ्घितम् ॥
9.3.m: falsehood in measures, falsehood in scales, falsehood concerning maidens, and falsehood concerning cattle, / spitting into water, and stepping over a pestle,

9.3.s: vṛṣalīgamanaṃ caiva gurudārāniṣevaṇam | surāpānasya yat pāpaṃ tiladhenuḥ praśāmyati ||
9.3.d: वृषलीगमनं चैव गुरुदारानिषेवणम् । सुरापानस्य यत् पापं तिलधेनुः प्रशाम्यति ॥
9.3.m: consorting with an outcaste woman, serving the wife of a guru, / and whatever sin there is of drinking liquor: the sesame cow pacifies it.

9.4.s: yā sa yamapure ghore nadī vaitaraṇī smṛtā | yatra lohamukhāḥ kākāḥ śvānaś caiva bhayāvahāḥ ||
9.4.d: या स यमपुरे घोरे नदी वैतरणी स्मृता । यत्र लोहमुखाः काकाः श्वानश् चैव भयावहाः ॥
9.4.m: That which is known as the dread river Vaitaraṇī in the city of Yama, / where there are iron-beaked crows and terrifying dogs,

9.4.s: vālukāntāḥ sthalāś caiva pacyante yatra duṣkṛtaḥ | asipattravanaṃ yatra śālūkāḥ śālmalī tathā ||
9.4.d: वालुकान्ताः स्थलाश् चैव पच्यन्ते यत्र दुष्कृतः । असिपत्त्रवनं यत्र शालूकाः शाल्मली तथा ॥
9.4.m: and grounds bordered by burning sand where evil-doers are tormented, / where is the forest of sword-like leaves, leeches, and the śālmalī tree—

9.4.s: tān sukhena vyatikramya dharmarājāśramaṃ vrajet | svāgataṃ te mahābhāga svasti te 'stu mahāmate ||
9.4.d: तान् सुखेन व्यतिक्रम्य धर्मराजाश्रमं व्रजेत् । स्वागतं ते महाभाग स्वस्ति ते ऽस्तु महामते ॥
9.4.m: passing beyond these with ease, he goes to the hermitage of the King of Dharma: / 'Welcome to you, highly fortunate one! May there be well-being to you, of great intellect!

9.4.s: vimānam etad yogyaṃ te maṇiratnavibhūṣitam | atrāruhya naraśreṣṭha gaccha tvaṃ paramāṃ gatim ||
9.4.d: विमानम् एतद् योग्यं ते मणिरत्नविभूषितम् । अत्रारुह्य नरश्रेष्ठ गच्छ त्वं परमां गतिम् ॥
9.4.m: Here is an aerial chariot worthy of you, adorned with gems and jewels; / mounting this, best of men, go to the supreme state!'

9.4.s: mā ca cārabhaṭe dadyān mā ca dadyāt purohite | mā ca kāṇe virūpe ca kuṣṭhivyaṅge tathaiva ca ||
9.4.d: मा च चारभटे दद्यान् मा च दद्यात् पुरोहिते । मा च काणे विरूपे च कुष्ठिव्यङ्गे तथैव च ॥
9.4.m: One should not give it to a spy or a soldier, nor should one give it to the royal domestic priest; / nor to one who is one-eyed, deformed, leprous, or mutilated in limb.

9.4.s: vedāntagāya dātavyā vedāntagasutāya vā | ekaikasmai ca dātavyā māghamāse tu pūrṇimām ||
9.4.d: वेदान्तगाय दातव्या वेदान्तगसुताय वा । एकैकस्मै च दातव्या माघमासे तु पूर्णिमाम् ॥
9.4.m: It should be given to one who has mastered the Vedānta, or to the son of one who has mastered the Vedānta; / and it should be given to an individual [worthy Brahmin] on the full moon day in the month of Māgha."

9.4.s: ya imāṃ paṭhate nityaṃ yaś cemāṃ śṛṇuyād api | devalokam atikramya sūryalokaṃ sa gacchati || sūryalokaṃ sa gacchatīti || iti tiladhenuvidhiḥ samāptaḥ ||
9.4.d: य इमां पठते नित्यं यश् चेमां शृणुयाद् अपि । देवलोकम् अतिक्रम्य सूर्यलोकं स गच्छति ॥ सूर्यलोकं स गच्छतीति ॥ इति तिलधेनुविधिः समाप्तः ॥
9.4.m: Whoever constantly recites this, and whoever listens to it, surpassing the world of the gods, goes to the world of the sun; "he goes to the world of the sun." Thus ends the rite of the sesame cow.

10.1.s: om atha rohiṇyāṃ sakalāyām upoṣito brahmā sarvabījarasaratnagandhāvakīrṇaṃ tīrthodakapūrṇakalaśam ādāyātisṛṣṭo apām ity abhiṣekamantrair yathoktair dātāram abhiṣiñcati ||
10.1.d: ओम् अथ रोहिण्यां सकलायाम् उपोषितो ब्रह्मा सर्वबीजरसरत्नगन्धावकीर्णं तीर्थोदकपूर्णकलशम् आदायातिसृष्टो अपाम् इत्य् अभिषेकमन्त्रैर् यथोक्तैर् दातारम् अभिषिञ्चति ॥
10.1.m: Om. Now, when the lunar mansion Rohiṇī is whole, the Brahman priest, having fasted, takes a jar filled with sacred water and strewn with all kinds of seeds, liquids, jewels, and perfumes, and consecrates the donor with the consecration verses as prescribed, beginning with "Dismissed of the waters..."

10.1.s: vratena tvaṃ vratapata iti vratam upaiti
10.1.d: व्रतेन त्वं व्रतपत इति व्रतम् उपैति
10.1.m: He undertakes the observance with: "By the vow, you, O Lord of vows..."

10.1.s: yācitāradātārāv ayācitāśināv adhahśāyinau bhavato
10.1.d: याचितारदाताराव् अयाचिताशिनाव् अधह्शायिनौ भवतो
10.1.m: The requester and the donor both eat unbegged food and sleep on the ground.

10.1.s: vratopacāram
10.1.d: व्रतोपचारम्

10.1.s: yathāśaktyaikarātraṃ pañcarātraṃ dvādaśarātraṃ vā vrataṃ caritvā
10.1.d: यथाशक्त्यैकरात्रं पञ्चरात्रं द्वादशरात्रं वा व्रतं चरित्वा
10.1.m: Having observed the vow according to ability for one night, five nights, or twelve nights,

10.1.s: śvo bhūte tantram ājyabhāgāntaṃ kṛtvānvārabhyātha juhuyāt ||
10.1.d: श्वो भूते तन्त्रम् आज्यभागान्तं कृत्वान्वारभ्याथ जुहुयात् ॥
10.1.m: on the following day, having performed the ritual framework up to the ghee portions and having maintained continuous contact, he should then make oblations.

10.1.s: kāmasūktaṃ kālasūktaṃ puruṣasūktaṃ mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ saṃkhyāpūrvikābhiḥ sarva ṛtvijo juhvaty
10.1.d: कामसूक्तं कालसूक्तं पुरुषसूक्तं महाव्याहृतिभिः संख्यापूर्विकाभिः सर्व ऋत्विजो जुह्वत्य्
10.1.m: All the officiating priests make oblations of the Kāmasūkta, the Kālasūkta, and the Puruṣasūkta, preceded by counting with the great sacred utterances.

10.1.s: atha suvarṇamayīṃ bhūmiṃ bhūmeḥ pratikṛtiṃ gocarmamātrāṃ kṛtvā
10.1.d: अथ सुवर्णमयीं भूमिं भूमेः प्रतिकृतिं गोचर्ममात्रां कृत्वा
10.1.m: Then, having fashioned an effigy of the earth made of gold to the size of a cow-hide,

10.1.s: maṇḍapavedyāṃ samānīya vedyuttarato yasyāṃ vedim ity upasthāpya
10.1.d: मण्डपवेद्यां समानीय वेद्युत्तरतो यस्यां वेदिम् इत्य् उपस्थाप्य
10.1.m: having brought it onto the pavilion altar, placing it to the north of the altar with the verse: "Upon which the altar...",

10.1.s: girayas te parvatā iti parvatān avasthāpya
10.1.d: गिरयस् ते पर्वता इति पर्वतान् अवस्थाप्य
10.1.m: establishing mountains with the verse: "May your mountains and hills...",

10.1.s: hiraṇyarajatamaṇimuktāpravālādibhir upaśobhayed yad adaḥ saṃprayatīr iti
10.1.d: हिरण्यरजतमणिमुक्ताप्रवालादिभिर् उपशोभयेद् यद् अदः संप्रयतीर् इति
10.1.m: he should embellish it with gold, silver, gems, pearls, corals, and other treasures with the verse: "When those [waters] set forth yonder..."

10.1.s: sā mandasāneti nadīḥ kalpayitvā rasaiś ca paripūrayed
10.1.d: सा मन्दसानेति नदीः कल्पयित्वा रसैश् च परिपूरयेद्
10.1.m: Having fashioned rivers with the verse: "May she, rejoicing...", he should fill them with liquids;

10.1.s: apām agram asi samudraṃ vo 'bhyavasṛjāmīti samudrān
10.1.d: अपाम् अग्रम् असि समुद्रं वो ऽभ्यवसृजामीति समुद्रान्
10.1.m: the oceans with the verses: "You are the forefront of the waters..." and "I release you into the ocean...";

10.1.s: vanaspatiḥ saha devair na āgann iti bṛhaspatineti vanaspatīn anyāṃś ca
10.1.d: वनस्पतिः सह देवैर् न आगन्न् इति बृहस्पतिनेति वनस्पतीन् अन्यांश् च
10.1.m: and forest trees and others with the verses: "May the lord of the forest come to us with the gods..." and "With Bṛhaspati...".

10.1.s: yajñe tvā manasā saṃkalpayen manasā saṃkalpayatītha bhavatīha bhavatīha bhavati
10.1.d: यज्ञे त्वा मनसा संकल्पयेन् मनसा संकल्पयतीथ भवतीह भवतीह भवति
10.1.m: One should fashion it with the mind in the sacrifice; one fashions it with the mind: "Be here, be here, be here."

10.1.s: nidhiṃ bibhratī bahudheti namaskārayitvā
10.1.d: निधिं बिभ्रती बहुधेति नमस्कारयित्वा
10.1.m: Having made [the donor] bow with the verse: "Bearing treasure in many ways...",

10.1.s: satyaṃ bṛhad ity anuvāko ye devā divy ekādaśa stheti puṇyāhaṃ vācayet
10.1.d: सत्यं बृहद् इत्य् अनुवाको ये देवा दिव्य् एकादश स्थेति पुण्याहं वाचयेत्
10.1.m: he should have an auspicious day proclaimed with the section beginning "Great truth..." and "Whatever gods are eleven in heaven...".

10.1.s: saṃsthāpayen
10.1.d: संस्थापयेन्

10.1.s: nava divo devajanenety abhimantrya brāhmaṇebhyo dadyād
10.1.d: नव दिवो देवजनेनेत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यो दद्याद्
10.1.m: Having consecrated it with the verse: "Nine [skies] with the divine race...", he should give it to the Brahmins.

10.1.s: dātur esāsmai rohiṇī kāmaṃ nikāmaṃ vā dugdha iti
10.1.d: दातुर् एसास्मै रोहिणी कामं निकामं वा दुग्ध इति
10.1.m: "May this Rohiṇī milk desire or full satisfaction for the donor."

10.1.s: yathā rohanti bījāni phālakṛṣṭe mahītale evaṃ kāmāḥ prarohante pretyeha manasaḥ sadā
10.1.d: यथा रोहन्ति बीजानि फालकृष्टे महीतले एवं कामाः प्ररोहन्ते प्रेत्येह मनसः सदा
10.1.m: Just as seeds sprout on the surface of the earth plowed by the share, / so desires of the mind always sprout here and after death.

10.1.s: sarveṣām eva dānānāṃ yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtam | tattat prāpnoti viprebhyo dattvā bhūmiṃ yathāvidhi || dattvā bhūmiṃ yathāvidhīti || iti bhūmidānaṃ samāptam ||
10.1.d: सर्वेषाम् एव दानानां यत् फलं समुदाहृतम् । तत्तत् प्राप्नोति विप्रेभ्यो दत्त्वा भूमिं यथाविधि ॥ दत्त्वा भूमिं यथाविधीति ॥ इति भूमिदानं समाप्तम् ॥
10.1.m: Whatever fruit is proclaimed for all gifts whatsoever, / that very fruit he obtains by giving land to Brahmins according to rule; "by giving land to Brahmins according to rule." Thus ends the gift of land.

11.1.m: Om. Now, therefore, we will explain the rule of the man-balance.

11.1.s: tad udagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre śraddhāpreritau grahaṇakāle vā
11.1.d: तद् उदगयन आपूर्यमाणपक्षे पुण्ये नक्षत्रे श्रद्धाप्रेरितौ ग्रहणकाले वा
11.1.m: During the sun's northern course, in the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious lunar mansion, impelled by faith, or at the time of an eclipse,
the officiating priest and the sacrificer, having their hair and beards trimmed and having shaved their body hair and nails,
having arranged the ritual requisites and having performed the preliminary framework up to the ghee portions,
having offered oblations with the great sacred utterances, the Sāvitrī, the propitiation, and "The Brahman born first...",

11.1.s: agne gobhir agne 'bhyāvartinn agneḥ prajātam iti saṃpātān udapātrānīyābhiṣekakalaśeṣu ninayed
11.1.d: अग्ने गोभिर् अग्ने ऽभ्यावर्तिन्न् अग्नेः प्रजातम् इति संपातान् उदपात्रानीयाभिषेककलशेषु निनयेद्
11.1.m: he should bring the residual drops to the water-vessels with "O Agni, with cows...", "O Agni, turning back...", and "Born of Agni...", and pour them into the consecration jars.
Then he should consecrate him with: "Indra by the pressing-stones..."

11.1.s: idam āpo yathendro bāhubhyām ity abhiṣecayitvā
11.1.d: इदम् आपो यथेन्द्रो बाहुभ्याम् इत्य् अभिषेचयित्वा
11.1.m: Having consecrated him with "These waters..." and "As Indra with his two arms...",

11.1.s: yathoktam añjanābhyañjanānulepanaṃ kārayitvā vāso gandhasrajaś cābadhnīyāt
11.1.d: यथोक्तम् अञ्जनाभ्यञ्जनानुलेपनं कारयित्वा वासो गन्धस्रजश् चाबध्नीयात्
11.1.m: having caused eye-salve, inunction, and ointment to be applied as prescribed, he should bind a garment, perfumes, and garlands [on him].

11.1.s: tulāṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca pavitrair abhyukṣya puruṣasaṃmito 'rtha iti saptabhis tadārohayed
11.1.d: तुलां हिरण्यं च पवित्रैर् अभ्युक्ष्य पुरुषसंमितो ऽर्थ इति सप्तभिस् तदारोहयेद्
11.1.m: Having sprinkled the balance and the gold with strainers, he should cause him to mount it with the seven verses beginning: "The wealth equal to a man..."
He should cause him to dismount with the four verses beginning: "Unshaken is heaven..."

11.1.s: sūryasyāvṛtam iti pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya brāhmaṇebhyo nivedayitvātmālaṃkārān kartre dadyāt
11.1.d: सूर्यस्यावृतम् इति प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यो निवेदयित्वात्मालंकारान् कर्त्रे दद्यात्
11.1.m: Having turned clockwise with the verse: "With the turning of the sun...", and having presented [the gifts] to the Brahmins, he should give his personal ornaments to the officiant,
a sacrificial fee of a thousand [cows], and an excellent village.
He should satisfy the twice-born with food.

11.1.s: atha cen niḥsvapakṣeṇa yathā saṃpadyate dhanam | dhātubhiḥ saha taulyam atu vāsobhiś ca rasais tathā | vrīhyādisaptadhānyair vā yathāsaṃpadyate gṛhe ||
11.1.d: अथ चेन् निःस्वपक्षेण यथा संपद्यते धनम् । धातुभिः सह तौल्यम् अतु वासोभिश् च रसैस् तथा । व्रीह्यादिसप्तधान्यैर् वा यथासंपद्यते गृहे ॥
11.1.m: Now, if according to the condition of one of meager means, according to the wealth available: / weighing along with base metals, or with garments and liquids, / or with the seven grains such as rice, according as it is found in his house.

11.2.s: sakhaḍgaḥ saśirastrāṇaḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ | tapanīyam agare kṛtvā paścāt tolyo narādhipaḥ ||
11.2.d: सखड्गः सशिरस्त्राणः सर्वाभरणभूषितः । तपनीयम् अगरे कृत्वा पश्चात् तोल्यो नराधिपः ॥
11.2.m: With sword, with helmet, adorned with all ornaments, / having placed refined gold in front, the ruler of men is then to be weighed.

11.2.s: indreṇedaṃ purā dattam adhirājyāptaye varam | sarvapāpapraṇāśāya sarvapuṇyavivṛddhaye ||
11.2.d: इन्द्रेणेदं पुरा दत्तम् अधिराज्याप्तये वरम् । सर्वपापप्रणाशाय सर्वपुण्यविवृद्धये ॥
11.2.m: This excellent gift was formerly given by Indra to obtain supreme sovereignty, / for the destruction of all sins, and for the increase of all merit.

11.2.s: mahādānātidānānām idaṃ dānam anuttamam | akṣayyaphaladaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dātṝṇāṃ śreyavardhanam ||
11.2.d: महादानातिदानानाम् इदं दानम् अनुत्तमम् । अक्षय्यफलदं श्रेष्ठं दातॄणां श्रेयवर्धनम् ॥
11.2.m: Among the great gifts and supreme gifts, this gift is unsurpassed; / it grants inexhaustible fruit, is the best, and increases the welfare of donors.

11.2.s: yat pāpaṃ sve kule jātais triḥ sapta puruṣaiḥ kṛtam | tat sarvaṃ naśyate kṣipram agnau tūlaṃ yathā tathā ||
11.2.d: यत् पापं स्वे कुले जातैस् त्रिः सप्त पुरुषैः कृतम् । तत् सर्वं नश्यते क्षिप्रम् अग्नौ तूलं यथा तथा ॥
11.2.m: Whatever sin has been committed by twenty-one generations of men born in one's family, / all that is destroyed quickly, just like cotton in fire.

11.2.s: anāmayaṃ sthānam avāpya daivair alaṅghanīyaṃ sukṛtair hiraṇmayaiḥ | suvarṇatejāḥ pravimuktapāpo divīndravad rājati sūryaloke || divīndravad rājati sūryaleketi || iti tulāpuruṣavidhiḥ samāptaḥ ||
11.2.d: अनामयं स्थानम् अवाप्य दैवैर् अलङ्घनीयं सुकृतैर् हिरण्मयैः । सुवर्णतेजाः प्रविमुक्तपापो दिवीन्द्रवद् राजति सूर्यलोके ॥ दिवीन्द्रवद् राजति सूर्यलेकेति ॥ इति तुलापुरुषविधिः समाप्तः ॥
11.2.m: Attaining a healthy state, unsurpassable by gods through golden good deeds, / of golden splendor, freed from sin, he shines in the world of the sun like Indra in heaven; "he shines in the world of the sun like Indra in heaven." Thus ends the rule of the man-balance.

12.1.s: om atha yaḥ kāmayeta sarveṣāṃ nṛṇām uttamaḥ syām iti sa bhāskarāyāpūpaṃ dadyāt
12.1.d: ओम् अथ यः कामयेत सर्वेषां नृणाम् उत्तमः स्याम् इति स भास्करायापूपं दद्यात्
12.1.m: Om. Now, whoever should desire, "May I be the highest of all men," he should offer a cake to the Sun.
Having baked [a cake] circular in shape using flour of either barley or wheat,
and having placed a piece of gold with raw sugar and ghee on top, he should worship it with red flowers.
Having consecrated it with the verse beginning "The conqueror...", he should present it to a Brahmin.

12.1.s: anena vidhinā yas tu pūpaṃ dadyād dvijātaye | prayacchet satataṃ prājñas tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu ||
12.1.d: अनेन विधिना यस् तु पूपं दद्याद् द्विजातये । प्रयच्छेत् सततं प्राज्ञस् तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ॥
12.1.m: He who according to this rule gives a cake to a twice-born man, / who, wise, gives it continually—hear the fruit of his merit!

12.1.s: ārogyavān varcasvī ca prajāvān paśumāṃs tathā | dhanavān annavān śrīmāṃs tathā sarvajanapriyaḥ ||
12.1.d: आरोग्यवान् वर्चस्वी च प्रजावान् पशुमांस् तथा । धनवान् अन्नवान् श्रीमांस् तथा सर्वजनप्रियः ॥
12.1.m: Possessed of health, radiant, rich in offspring, and rich in cattle, / wealthy, supplied with food, prosperous, and dear to all people,

12.1.s: apamṛtyuśataṃ sāgraṃ nāśayaty avicārataḥ | pradattaṃ sūryalokaṃ ca prāpayet paramaṃ padam || prāpayet paramaṃ padam iti || ity ādityamaṇḍakaḥ samāptaḥ ||
12.1.d: अपमृत्युशतं साग्रं नाशयत्य् अविचारतः । प्रदत्तं सूर्यलोकं च प्रापयेत् परमं पदम् ॥ प्रापयेत् परमं पदम् इति ॥ इत्य् आदित्यमण्डकः समाप्तः ॥
12.1.m: undoubtedly, that which is given destroys a full hundred untimely deaths, / and brings him to the world of the sun, the supreme abode; "and brings him to the world of the sun, the supreme abode." Thus ends the Sun-Cake.

13.1.m: Om. Now we will set forth the rule of the golden embryo, which removes all sins.

13.1.s: udagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre śraddhāpreritau grahaṇakāle vā
13.1.d: उदगयन आपूर्यमाणपक्षे पुण्ये नक्षत्रे श्रद्धाप्रेरितौ ग्रहणकाले वा
13.1.m: During the sun's northern course, in the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious lunar mansion, impelled by faith, or at the time of an eclipse,

13.1.s: atha ṛtvik prag astaṃgamanād aśvatthād araṇī ādhāyāgne jāyasveti dvābhyāṃ mathyamānam anumantrayate
13.1.d: अथ ऋत्विक् प्रग् अस्तंगमनाद् अश्वत्थाद् अरणी आधायाग्ने जायस्वेति द्वाभ्यां मथ्यमानम् अनुमन्त्रयते
13.1.m: Then, before sunset, the officiating priest, having taken two kindling sticks from an aśvattha tree, recites over [the fire] being churned with the two [stanzas beginning] "Be born, O Agni".
With the third [stanza] [he recites over it] when born; with the fourth he adds fuel [to it].

13.1.s: śucau deśe paridhāpya yathoktam añjanābhyañjanānulepanaṃ kārayitvā
13.1.d: शुचौ देशे परिधाप्य यथोक्तम् अञ्जनाभ्यञ्जनानुलेपनं कारयित्वा
13.1.m: Having dressed [the patron] in a pure place, and having caused him to undergo eye-salving, inunction, and anointing as prescribed,

13.1.s: agneḥ prajātaṃ pari yad dhiraṇyaṃ yad ābadhnann iti hiraṇyasrajam āgrathya rakṣantu tveti rakṣāṃ kṛtvā
13.1.d: अग्नेः प्रजातं परि यद् धिरण्यं यद् आबध्नन्न् इति हिरण्यस्रजम् आग्रथ्य रक्षन्तु त्वेति रक्षां कृत्वा
13.1.m: having woven a golden garland with [the verses] "Produced from Agni," "The gold which around," and "That which they bound on," and having made an amulet of protection with "May they protect thee,"
having spread darbha grass, the two should lie on the ground.

13.1.s: śvo bhūte 'bhijinmuhūrte hiraṇmayaṃ maṇḍalākṛti nābhimātraṃ pātram ādhāya sāpidhānam
13.1.d: श्वो भूते ऽभिजिन्मुहूर्ते हिरण्मयं मण्डलाकृति नाभिमात्रं पात्रम् आधाय सापिधानम्
13.1.m: On the next day, at the Abhijit hour, having set down a golden, circular vessel as high as the navel, along with a lid,
and the large ladle, the small ladle, the clarified-butter pot, the water vessel, and ornaments,

13.1.s: parisamuhya paryukṣya paristīrya barhir udapātram upasādya paricaraṇenājyaṃ paricarya nityān purastāddhomān hutvājyabhāgau cātha juhoti
13.1.d: परिसमुह्य पर्युक्ष्य परिस्तीर्य बर्हिर् उदपात्रम् उपसाद्य परिचरणेनाज्यं परिचर्य नित्यान् पुरस्ताद्धोमान् हुत्वाज्यभागौ चाथ जुहोति
13.1.m: having swept around, sprinkled around, strewn sacrificial grass, placed the water vessel near, attended the clarified butter with attending rites, and having offered the regular preliminary oblations and the two portions of clarified butter, he then makes oblations:

13.2.s: hiraṇyagarbhāya svāhā || agnaye svāhā || brahmaṇe svāhā || prajāpataye svāheti hutvā
13.2.d: हिरण्यगर्भाय स्वाहा ॥ अग्नये स्वाहा ॥ ब्रह्मणे स्वाहा ॥ प्रजापतये स्वाहेति हुत्वा
13.2.m: Having offered with: "To Hiraṇyagarbha, svāhā! To Agni, svāhā! To Brahman, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā!"—
having caused [him] to make obeisance with those very [formulas],
having worshipped with those very [formulas], and [consecrating] the large ladle, the small ladle, the clarified-butter pot, the water vessel, and the ornaments;
having bathed the king in the golden [vessel] with the [verses] containing the word "gold" (hiraṇyavatī),
and having poured the five products of the cow and water into it using golden jars,

13.2.s: hiraṇyagarbhasūktenāṃhomucena śantātīyena pañcabhiś ca nāmabhiḥ saṃpātān ānīya
13.2.d: हिरण्यगर्भसूक्तेनांहोमुचेन शन्तातीयेन पञ्चभिश् च नामभिः संपातान् आनीय
13.2.m: having brought the remnant drops [of the oblation] with the Hiraṇyagarbha hymn, the Aṃhomuc [hymn], the Śantātīya [hymn], and with the five names,
in the same manner, he should ask permission of the seated and unseated officiating priests:

13.2.s: rājā hiraṇyagarbhatvam abhīpsaty asmin bhavanto 'numanyantām iti
13.2.d: राजा हिरण्यगर्भत्वम् अभीप्सत्य् अस्मिन् भवन्तो ऽनुमन्यन्ताम् इति
13.2.m: "The king desires the condition of Hiraṇyagarbha. May your honors assent to this."

13.3.s: ud ehi vājinn iti dvābhyāṃ praveśayet
13.3.d: उद् एहि वाजिन्न् इति द्वाभ्यां प्रवेशयेत्
13.3.m: he should cause him to enter with the two [verses] "Rise up, O courser!"

13.3.s: trayastriṃśad devatā ity abhisaṃdhāya tam anuśāsti
13.3.d: त्रयस्त्रिंशद् देवता इत्य् अभिसंधाय तम् अनुशास्ति
13.3.m: Bearing in mind the thirty-three deities, he instructs him:

13.3.s: vācaṃ niyamya pratisaṃhṛtya cendriyāṇi viṣayebhyo manasā bhagavantaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ hiraṇyagarbhaṃ parameṣṭhinaṃ pauruṣaṃ dhyāyasveti
13.3.d: वाचं नियम्य प्रतिसंहृत्य चेन्द्रियाणि विषयेभ्यो मनसा भगवन्तं हिरण्मयं हिरण्यगर्भं परमेष्ठिनं पौरुषं ध्यायस्वेति
13.3.m: "Restraining your speech and withdrawing your senses from their objects, meditate in your mind upon the blessed, golden Hiraṇyagarbha, the supreme, the Cosmic Person."
"So be it," [the king] agrees to that.
He remains inside for the duration of seventeen moments.
He should declare: "[It is] the procedure of Prajāpati."
In the same manner, having obtained permission from the seated and unseated [priests], he should raise [the king] up.
He should press down upon him when he has arisen with a golden wheel.
He should lift [him] out with "May thy breath not [fail thee]."

13.3.s: uddhṛtaṃ hiraṇyanāmno pravimucya yas tvā mṛtyur ity apāsyet
13.3.d: उद्धृतं हिरण्यनाम्नो प्रविमुच्य यस् त्वा मृत्युर् इत्य् अपास्येत्
13.3.m: Having untied the two golden names from him who has been lifted out, he should throw [them] away with "Whatever death [threatens] thee."

13.3.s: saṃpaśyamānā ity avekṣito brāhmaṇān praṇipatya namaskārya namo hiraṇyagarbhāyety
13.3.d: संपश्यमाना इत्य् अवेक्षितो ब्राह्मणान् प्रणिपत्य नमस्कार्य नमो हिरण्यगर्भायेत्य्
13.3.m: Having been looked at with "Beholding," having bowed down before the brahmins, and having made obeisance with "Homage to Hiraṇyagarbha,"

13.3.s: atha ha vai hiraṇyagarbhasyeti priyatamāya tata uktam
13.3.d: अथ ह वै हिरण्यगर्भस्येति प्रियतमाय तत उक्तम्
13.3.m: then [the formula] "Now indeed of Hiraṇyagarbha" is recited for the dearest one.
The brahmins should say: "Arise, thou art favored by Hiraṇyagarbha!"
Having made an offering with the Apratiratha [hymn], he should conclude [the rite].

13.3.s: apsu te rājan varuṇeti varuṇam abhiṣṭūya snātvā pavitraiḥ pratyetyādityam upatiṣṭhante
13.3.d: अप्सु ते राजन् वरुणेति वरुणम् अभिष्टूय स्नात्वा पवित्रैः प्रत्येत्यादित्यम् उपतिष्ठन्ते
13.3.m: Having praised Varuṇa with "In the waters is thy [home], O King Varuṇa," having bathed, and having returned with purification [implements], they attend upon the sun:

13.4.s: hiraṇyaṃ tava yad garbho hiraṇyasyāpi garbhajaḥ | hiraṇyagarbhas tasmāt tvaṃ pāhi māṃ mahato mahān iti
13.4.d: हिरण्यं तव यद् गर्भो हिरण्यस्यापि गर्भजः । हिरण्यगर्भस् तस्मात् त्वं पाहि मां महतो महान् इति
13.4.m: "Since gold is thy womb, and thou art also born from the womb of gold, / therefore, thou art Hiraṇyagarbha; protect me, O great one among the great!"
Turning clockwise with "Following the turning of the sun,"
and approaching the house with "I approach the houses,"

13.4.s: tvam agne pramatir ity agnim upasthāpyāthotsṛjed
13.4.d: त्वम् अग्ने प्रमतिर् इत्य् अग्निम् उपस्थाप्याथोत्सृजेद्
13.4.m: having worshipped the fire with "Thou, O Agni, art the wise guardian," he should then dismiss [it].

13.4.s: atha dvijebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ daśa sahasrāṇ dadyāt
13.4.d: अथ द्विजेभ्यो दक्षिणां दश सहस्राण् दद्यात्
13.4.m: Then he should give a sacrificial fee to the twice-born: ten thousand [cows],
And the large ladle, the small ladle, the clarified-butter pot, the water vessel, and ornaments—everything else [goes] to the assembled priests,

13.4.s: yāvad vā tuṣyeraṃś tāvad vā deyam || rājā dadyād
13.4.d: यावद् वा तुष्येरंश् तावद् वा देयम् ॥ राजा दद्याद्
13.4.m: or as much as would satisfy [them] should be given. The king should give [it].
He should serve the brahmins with food according to their desire.

13.5.s: vedānāṃ pāragā yasya caturṇāṃ brahmavittamāḥ | tuṣṭā yasyāśiṣo brūyus tasya yajñaphalaṃ bhavet ||
13.5.d: वेदानां पारगा यस्य चतुर्णां ब्रह्मवित्तमाः । तुष्टा यस्याशिषो ब्रूयुस् तस्य यज्ञफलं भवेत् ॥
13.5.m: "He whose blessings are spoken with satisfaction by the foremost knowers of Brahman / who have reached the further shore of the four Vedas, obtains the fruit of the sacrifice.

13.5.s: brāhmaṇānāṃ prasādena sūryo divi virājati | indro 'py eṣāṃ prasādena devān ativirājati ||
13.5.d: ब्राह्मणानां प्रसादेन सूर्यो दिवि विराजति । इन्द्रो ऽप्य् एषां प्रसादेन देवान् अतिविराजति ॥
13.5.m: By the favor of the brahmins the sun shines in heaven; / Indra too, by their favor, outshines the gods.

13.5.s: hiraṇyadānasya phalam amṛtatvam iti śrutiḥ | śrūyate hy asya dātā yaḥ so 'mṛtatvaṃ samaśnute ||
13.5.d: हिरण्यदानस्य फलम् अमृतत्वम् इति श्रुतिः । श्रूयते ह्य् अस्य दाता यः सो ऽमृतत्वं समश्नुते ॥
13.5.m: The fruit of the gift of gold is immortality: so runs the sacred tradition. / For it is heard that he who is the giver of this attains immortality.

13.5.s: rājekṣuvākuprabhrtayaḥ purā rājarṣayo 'malāḥ | dattvā hiraṇyaṃ viprebhyo jyotir bhūtvā divi sthitāḥ ||
13.5.d: राजेक्षुवाकुप्रभ्र्तयः पुरा राजर्षयो ऽमलाः । दत्त्वा हिरण्यं विप्रेभ्यो ज्योतिर् भूत्वा दिवि स्थिताः ॥
13.5.m: The spotless royal sages of old, beginning with King Ikṣvāku, / having given gold to the inspired poets, became luminous and dwelt in heaven.

13.5.s: ya evaṃ saṃskṛto rājā vidhinā brahmavādinā | prajānām iha sāmrājyaṃ jyaiṣṭhyaṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ ca gacchati ||
13.5.d: य एवं संस्कृतो राजा विधिना ब्रह्मवादिना । प्रजानाम् इह साम्राज्यं ज्यैष्ठ्यं श्रैष्ठ्यं च गच्छति ॥
13.5.m: The king who is consecrated in this manner by the ordinance declared by the knower of Brahman / attains empire over his subjects in this world, along with pre-eminence and supremacy.

13.5.s: amuṣmin brahmaṇā sārdham ānandam anubhūya vai | jyotirmayaṃ satyalokaṃ nacaivāvartate punaḥ ||
13.5.d: अमुष्मिन् ब्रह्मणा सार्धम् आनन्दम् अनुभूय वै । ज्योतिर्मयं सत्यलोकं नचैवावर्तते पुनः ॥
13.5.m: Having indeed experienced bliss in the other world together with Brahman, / in the luminous realm of truth (Satyaloka), he never returns again."

14.1.m: Oṃ. Now I shall declare the sequence of gifts of an elephant chariot.

14.1.s: jātarūpamayaṃ krtvā ekacakraṃ suśobhanam | hastibhiḥ saptabhir yuktam arcayitvā yathāvidhi ||
14.1.d: जातरूपमयं क्र्त्वा एकचक्रं सुशोभनम् । हस्तिभिः सप्तभिर् युक्तम् अर्चयित्वा यथाविधि ॥
14.1.m: Having made [a chariot] of gold, with a single wheel, very splendid, / yoked with seven elephants, and having worshipped it according to rule,

14.1.s: atha vā caturbhir yuktaṃ haimaṃ rājatam eva vā | aspṛṣṭaṃ dārujaṃ vāpi sarvasaṃbhārapūritam ||
14.1.d: अथ वा चतुर्भिर् युक्तं हैमं राजतम् एव वा । अस्पृष्टं दारुजं वापि सर्वसंभारपूरितम् ॥
14.1.m: or else yoked with four, made of gold or silver, / or made of untouched wood, filled with all provisions,

14.1.s: hastiyugmena saṃyuktaṃ saurabheyayutena vā | bhuṅkte saptaiva janmāni saptadvīpāṃ vasuṃdharām ||
14.1.d: हस्तियुग्मेन संयुक्तं सौरभेययुतेन वा । भुङ्क्ते सप्तैव जन्मानि सप्तद्वीपां वसुंधराम् ॥
14.1.m: yoked with a pair of elephants or with a pair of cattle, / he enjoys the earth with its seven continents for seven births.

14.1.s: hastena yukte candramasi paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vā puṇye vā ṛkṣe śuciḥ śucau deśe tantram ity uktam ||
14.1.d: हस्तेन युक्ते चन्द्रमसि पौर्णमास्याम् अमावास्यायां वा पुण्ये वा ऋक्षे शुचिः शुचौ देशे तन्त्रम् इत्य् उक्तम् ॥
14.1.m: When the moon is in conjunction with Hasta, on a full-moon day or a new-moon day, or on an auspicious lunar mansion, being pure in a pure place—such is the procedure stated.
Having laid down the sacrificial fuel eastward and maintained touch [with the priest], he should then offer:

14.1.s: savitre svāhā || pataṃgāya svāhā || pāvakāya svāhā || sahasraraśmaye svāhā || mārtaṇḍāya svāhā || viṣṇave svāhā || prajāpataye svāhā || parameṣṭhine svāhā iti hutvā |
14.1.d: सवित्रे स्वाहा ॥ पतंगाय स्वाहा ॥ पावकाय स्वाहा ॥ सहस्ररश्मये स्वाहा ॥ मार्तण्डाय स्वाहा ॥ विष्णवे स्वाहा ॥ प्रजापतये स्वाहा ॥ परमेष्ठिने स्वाहा इति हुत्वा ।
14.1.m: Having offered with: "To Savitṛ, svāhā! To Pataṅga, svāhā! To Pāvaka, svāhā! To the thousand-rayed one, svāhā! To Mārtaṇḍa, svāhā! To Viṣṇu, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To Parameṣṭhin, svāhā!"—

14.1.s: kanakāś ca tilā gāvo dāsī gṛhamahīrathāḥ | kanyā hastī ca vidyā ca mahādāni vai daśa ||
14.1.d: कनकाश् च तिला गावो दासी गृहमहीरथाः । कन्या हस्ती च विद्या च महादानि वै दश ॥
14.1.m: "Gold, sesame seeds, cattle, a maidservant, a house, land, chariots, / a maiden, an elephant, and knowledge are indeed the ten great gifts.

14.1.s: tasmāt sarveṣu dāneṣu anuktavidhikeṣu ca | agniṃ brūma iti sūktam ājyatantreṇa homayet ||
14.1.d: तस्मात् सर्वेषु दानेषु अनुक्तविधिकेषु च । अग्निं ब्रूम इति सूक्तम् आज्यतन्त्रेण होमयेत् ॥
14.1.m: Therefore, in all gifts and in those whose procedures are not specified, / one should offer with the hymn 'We speak to Agni' according to the ritual of clarified butter.

14.1.s: aśvadātā vrajet svargam aśvārūḍhaś ca mānavaḥ | pūjyate devagandharvair apsarokiṃnarais tathā ||
14.1.d: अश्वदाता व्रजेत् स्वर्गम् अश्वारूढश् च मानवः । पूज्यते देवगन्धर्वैर् अप्सरोकिंनरैस् तथा ॥
14.1.m: The giver of a horse goes to heaven; and mounted on a horse, that man / is worshipped by gods, gandharvas, apsarases, and kiṃnaras."

14.1.s: hastivarcasaṃ prathatām iti kalaśe saṃpātān ānīya yugaṃ yoktraṃ ratham iti sarvaṃ saṃprokṣya ||
14.1.d: हस्तिवर्चसं प्रथताम् इति कलशे संपातान् आनीय युगं योक्त्रं रथम् इति सर्वं संप्रोक्ष्य ॥
14.1.m: Having brought the sacrificial residues into a water-pot with [the verse] 'May the splendour of elephants spread…' and sprinkled the yoke, the trace, and the chariot—everything;
He should harness [the animal] with [the words], 'I harness you with unwearied mind…'

14.1.s: aśrāntasya tvā manasā yunajmi prathamasya ca | utkūlam udvaho bhavo uduhya prati dhāvatāt ||
14.1.d: अश्रान्तस्य त्वा मनसा युनज्मि प्रथमस्य च । उत्कूलम् उद्वहो भवो उदुह्य प्रति धावतात् ॥
14.1.m: 'I harness you with unwearied mind, and [with the mind] of the foremost; / be a bearer of burdens uphill, having carried [them] up run back!'

14.1.s: śyāvair yuktaḥ śitipadbhir hiraṇyayo yasya rathaḥ pathibhir vartate sukhaiḥ | sa no hastena savitā hiraṇyabhug ghiraṇyapāṇiḥ savitā no 'bhirakṣatu ||
14.1.d: श्यावैर् युक्तः शितिपद्भिर् हिरण्ययो यस्य रथः पथिभिर् वर्तते सुखैः । स नो हस्तेन सविता हिरण्यभुग् घिरण्यपाणिः सविता नो ऽभिरक्षतु ॥
14.1.m: 'He whose golden chariot, harnessed with dark, white-footed [steeds], travels along easy paths; / may that Savitṛ, the enjoyer of gold, the golden-handed Savitṛ protect us!'

14.1.s: bṛhaddhastirathaṃ yuktaṃ hastena tu dadan naraḥ | savituḥ sthānam āpnoti divyāṃ kāmajavāṃ sabhām ||
14.1.d: बृहद्धस्तिरथं युक्तं हस्तेन तु ददन् नरः । सवितुः स्थानम् आप्नोति दिव्यां कामजवां सभाम् ॥
14.1.m: A man who gives an elephant-chariot harnessed with a great elephant with his own hand / attains the abode of Savitṛ, the divine assembly that moves at will.

15.1.m: Om. Now, the rules for the gift of a horse-chariot.

15.1.s: goṣṭha udakānte śucau vā deśe prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāyānvārabhyātha juhuyāt ||
15.1.d: गोष्ठ उदकान्ते शुचौ वा देशे प्राञ्चम् इध्मम् उपसमाधायान्वारभ्याथ जुहुयात् ॥
15.1.m: In a cowpen, at the water's edge, or in a pure place, having set up eastward-pointing sacrificial fuel and made contact [with the sacrificer], he should then offer oblation.

15.1.s: vataraṃhā bhava vājin yujyamāna ity etenāśveṣu saṃpātān ānīyāśrāntasya tveti samānam
15.1.d: वतरंहा भव वाजिन् युज्यमान इत्य् एतेनाश्वेषु संपातान् आनीयाश्रान्तस्य त्वेति समानम्
15.1.m: Having brought the sacrificial residues onto the horses with [the verse] 'Be swift as the wind, O steed, when harnessed…', [the rest is] the same as [described with] 'With unwearied mind…'

15.1.s: tvam indras tvaṃ mahendra iti savitre arghaṃ dattvā
15.1.d: त्वम् इन्द्रस् त्वं महेन्द्र इति सवित्रे अर्घं दत्त्वा
15.1.m: Having offered a guest-offering to Savitṛ with [the words] 'You are Indra, you are Mahendra…';
Touching himself with [the words] 'May they purify me…', he should whisper [the formula];

15.1.s: rakṣantu tvāgnaya iti yajamānam abhimantrya samṛddhihomānte
15.1.d: रक्षन्तु त्वाग्नय इति यजमानम् अभिमन्त्र्य समृद्धिहोमान्ते
15.1.m: Having consecrated the sacrificer with [the verse] 'May the fires protect you…', at the end of the prosperity oblations,

15.1.s: varāṃ dhenuṃ kartre dadyād aśvarathaṃ grāmavaraṃ ceti
15.1.d: वरां धेनुं कर्त्रे दद्याद् अश्वरथं ग्रामवरं चेति
15.1.m: He should give an excellent cow to the celebrant, [and] a horse-chariot and a prime village.

15.1.s: ya evaṃ vidhinā dadyād viduṣe aśvarathaṃ sudhīḥ | jyaiṣṭhyaṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ ca sāmrājyaṃ prajānām iha gacchati ||
15.1.d: य एवं विधिना दद्याद् विदुषे अश्वरथं सुधीः । ज्यैष्ठ्यं श्रैष्ठ्यं च साम्राज्यं प्रजानाम् इह गच्छति ॥
15.1.m: A wise man who, according to these rules, gives a horse-chariot to a learned man / attains primacy, pre-eminence, and sovereignty over the subjects in this world.

15.1.s: saptānāṃ lokānām ante jyotirlokam anāmayam | gatvā sa paramānandaṃ bhuṅkte yāvad vibhāvasuḥ ||
15.1.d: सप्तानां लोकानाम् अन्ते ज्योतिर्लोकम् अनामयम् । गत्वा स परमानन्दं भुङ्क्ते यावद् विभावसुः ॥
15.1.m: At the end of the seven worlds, having gone to the world of light free from disease, / he enjoys supreme bliss as long as the sun [shines].

16.1.m: Om. Now therefore, the rules for [the gift of] a thousand cows.

16.1.s: goṣṭha udakānte śucau vā deśe prāñcam idhmam upasamādhāyānvālabhyātha juhuyāt ||
16.1.d: गोष्ठ उदकान्ते शुचौ वा देशे प्राञ्चम् इध्मम् उपसमाधायान्वालभ्याथ जुहुयात् ॥
16.1.m: In a cowpen, at the water's edge, or in a pure place, having set up eastward-pointing sacrificial fuel and made contact [with the sacrificer], he should then offer oblation.
He should offer clarified butter with the hymn 'Hither the cows…'

16.1.s: mahāvrīhīṇām aindraṃ caruṃ saumyaṃ ca sahasratamyāḥ payasi śrapayitvā gāva eva surabhava ity etena juhuyāt ||
16.1.d: महाव्रीहीणाम् ऐन्द्रं चरुं सौम्यं च सहस्रतम्याः पयसि श्रपयित्वा गाव एव सुरभव इत्य् एतेन जुहुयात् ॥
16.1.m: Having cooked an oblation of large rice for Indra and one for Soma in the milk of the thousandth [cow], he should offer it with [the verse] 'Fragrant indeed are the cows…'
[He should bring] sacred water from five rivers.

16.1.s: paścād agnes tīrthodakena pūrṇaṃ kalaśam avasthāpya hiraṇyavarṇā ity abhimantrya saṃ vo goṣṭheneti daśa gāḥ snāpayet ||
16.1.d: पश्चाद् अग्नेस् तीर्थोदकेन पूर्णं कलशम् अवस्थाप्य हिरण्यवर्णा इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य सं वो गोष्ठेनेति दश गाः स्नापयेत् ॥
16.1.m: Behind the fire, having placed a jar full of sacred water and consecrated it with [the hymn] 'Golden-coloured…', he should bathe ten cows with [the verse] 'Together with your cowpen…'

16.1.s: tvaramānanayāḥ samabhyukṣya sahasratamyāḥ sānodanekemam indra vardhaya kṣatriyaṃ ma iti rājānam abhiṣicya ||
16.1.d: त्वरमाननयाः समभ्युक्ष्य सहस्रतम्याः सानोदनेकेमम् इन्द्र वर्धय क्षत्रियं म इति राजानम् अभिषिच्य ॥
16.1.m: Having sprinkled the swiftly moving [cows] with the rinse-water of the thousandth [cow], having consecrated the king with [the hymn] 'Increase this kṣatriya for me, O Indra…';

16.1.s: imā āpa iti ṣaḍbhir yothoktam añjanābhyañjanānulepanaṃ kṛtvā ||
16.1.d: इमा आप इति षड्भिर् योथोक्तम् अञ्जनाभ्यञ्जनानुलेपनं कृत्वा ॥
16.1.m: Having performed the application of collyrium, anointing, and unction as prescribed, with the six [verses beginning with] 'These waters…';

16.1.s: ā gāvo mām upatiṣṭhantām ity upatiṣṭhet ||
16.1.d: आ गावो माम् उपतिष्ठन्ताम् इत्य् उपतिष्ठेत् ॥
16.1.m: He should attend [upon them] with [the words], 'May the cows approach me…'

16.1.s: prajāvatīḥ sūyavasād iti ca sarvāḥ pāyayet ||
16.1.d: प्रजावतीः सूयवसाद् इति च सर्वाः पाययेत् ॥
16.1.m: And he should make them all drink with [the verse] 'Possessed of offspring, [grazing] on rich pasture…'

16.1.s: priyam aśanaṃ dattvāddhi tṛṇam aghnya iti sahasratamīm ālabhya japet ||
16.1.d: प्रियम् अशनं दत्त्वाद्धि तृणम् अघ्न्य इति सहस्रतमीम् आलभ्य जपेत् ॥
16.1.m: Having given preferred fodder, he should whisper, touching the thousandth cow, 'Eat grass, O inviolable one…'

16.1.s: mayā gāvo gopatinā sacadhvam iti mantrānetnārghaṃ dattvā ||
16.1.d: मया गावो गोपतिना सचध्वम् इति मन्त्रानेत्नार्घं दत्त्वा ॥
16.1.m: Having offered a guest-offering with the mantras [beginning with] 'Accompany me as your herdsman, O cows…';

16.1.s: sahasratamyāḥ pucham aupasaṃgṛhya bhūmiṣ ṭvā pratigṛhṇātv iti japan ||
16.1.d: सहस्रतम्याः पुछम् औपसंगृह्य भूमिष् ट्वा प्रतिगृह्णात्व् इति जपन् ॥
16.1.m: Taking hold of the tail of the thousandth [cow] while whispering, 'May the earth receive you…';

16.1.s: sarvāḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya namaskṛtya svastivācya brāhmaṇebhyo nivedya daśa gā dakṣiṇāṃ kartre dadyāt sahasratamīṃ vastrayugmam aca ||
16.1.d: सर्वाः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य नमस्कृत्य स्वस्तिवाच्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यो निवेद्य दश गा दक्षिणां कर्त्रे दद्यात् सहस्रतमीं वस्त्रयुग्मम् अच ॥
16.1.m: Having circumambulated them all clockwise, saluted them, caused the blessing to be recited, and presented them to the brahmins, he should give ten cows as a sacrificial fee to the celebrant, and the thousandth [cow] and a pair of garments.

16.2.s: saptājanmānugaṃ pāpaṃ puruṣaiḥ saptabhiḥ krtam | tatkṣaṇād vidhinānena nāśayed goprado naraḥ ||
16.2.d: सप्ताजन्मानुगं पापं पुरुषैः सप्तभिः क्र्तम् । तत्क्षणाद् विधिनानेन नाशयेद् गोप्रदो नरः ॥
16.2.m: The sin pursuing seven lifetimes, committed by seven generations of men, / a man giving a cow destroys instantly through this rite.

16.2.s: sarveṣām eva dānānāṃ phalaṃ yat parikīrtitam | tad avāpnoti virebhyo gosahasraprado naraḥ ||
16.2.d: सर्वेषाम् एव दानानां फलं यत् परिकीर्तितम् । तद् अवाप्नोति विरेभ्यो गोसहस्रप्रदो नरः ॥
16.2.m: Whatever fruit is proclaimed for all gifts, / that a man who gives a thousand cows obtains from the heroes.

16.2.s: aśvamedhaṃ vṛṣotsargaṃ gosahasraṃ ca yaḥ sutaḥ | dadyān madīya ity āhuḥ pitaras tarpayanti hi ||
16.2.d: अश्वमेधं वृषोत्सर्गं गोसहस्रं च यः सुतः । दद्यान् मदीय इत्य् आहुः पितरस् तर्पयन्ति हि ॥
16.2.m: 'A son who performs a horse sacrifice, the release of a bull, and [the gift of] a thousand cows, / is mine,' so say the ancestors; for they gladden [them].

16.2.s: tasmād anena vidhinā gosahasraṃ daden naraḥ | sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā yāti tat paramaṃ padam iti ||
16.2.d: तस्माद् अनेन विधिना गोसहस्रं ददेन् नरः । सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा याति तत् परमं पदम् इति ॥
16.2.m: Therefore, by this rite, a man should give a thousand cows; / purified of all sins, he goes to that supreme abode.

17.1.s: om atha pratisaṃvatsaraṃ rājakarmāṇi krameṇa vakṣyāmaḥ ||
17.1.d: ओम् अथ प्रतिसंवत्सरं राजकर्माणि क्रमेण वक्ष्यामः ॥
17.1.m: Om. Now, we shall explain in order the duties of the king year by year.
Now, on the third day of the bright fortnight in the month of Aśvayuja;

17.1.s: rakṣantu tvāgnaya iti catasṛbhī rakṣām aśvānāṃ baddhvā hastyaśvānāṃ nīrājanaṃ kuryāt ||
17.1.d: रक्षन्तु त्वाग्नय इति चतसृभी रक्षाम् अश्वानां बद्ध्वा हस्त्यश्वानां नीराजनं कुर्यात् ॥
17.1.m: Having tied an amulet on the horses with the four [verses beginning with] 'May the fires protect you…', he should perform the waving of lights for the elephants and horses.

17.1.s: aśvo 'si kṣiprajanmāsi … pradadyāt sa viśuddhātmā saptadvīpāṃ vasuṃdharām ||
17.1.d: अश्वो ऽसि क्षिप्रजन्मासि … प्रदद्यात् स विशुद्धात्मा सप्तद्वीपां वसुंधराम् ॥
17.1.m: 'You are a horse, you are swift-born…' [...] Purified of self, he should grant the earth of seven continents.

17.1.s: hastena yukte candramasi paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyāṃ vā puṇye nakṣatre śucau deśe || tantram ity uktam ||
17.1.d: हस्तेन युक्ते चन्द्रमसि पौर्णमास्याम् अमावास्यायां वा पुण्ये नक्षत्रे शुचौ देशे ॥ तन्त्रम् इत्य् उक्तम् ॥
17.1.m: When the moon is conjoined with Hasta, on a full moon or a new moon, under an auspicious lunar mansion, in a pure place—the sacrificial procedure has been explained.
Having set up eastward-pointing sacrificial fuel and made contact [with the sacrificer], he should then offer oblation:

17.1.s: savitre svāhā || pataṃgāya svāhā || pāvakāya svāhā || sahasraraśmaye svāhā || mārtaṇḍāya svāhā || viṣṇave svāhā || prajāpataye svāhā || parameṣṭhine svāheti hutvā kanakānāṃ baddhvā hastyaśvānāṃ pūrvavan nīrājanaṃ kuryāt ||
17.1.d: सवित्रे स्वाहा ॥ पतंगाय स्वाहा ॥ पावकाय स्वाहा ॥ सहस्ररश्मये स्वाहा ॥ मार्तण्डाय स्वाहा ॥ विष्णवे स्वाहा ॥ प्रजापतये स्वाहा ॥ परमेष्ठिने स्वाहेति हुत्वा कनकानां बद्ध्वा हस्त्यश्वानां पूर्ववन् नीराजनं कुर्यात् ॥
17.1.m: Having offered with 'To Savitṛ, svāhā! To Pataṅga, svāhā! To Pāvaka, svāhā! To Sahasraraśmi, svāhā! To Mārtaṇḍa, svāhā! To Viṣṇu, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To Parameṣṭhin, svāhā!', and having tied [amulets] of gold, he should perform the waving of lights for the elephants and horses as before.

17.2.s: atha navamyām aparāhṇe vāhanāni snāpayitvā ahatavāsā brahmā dvādaśamitāṃ vediṃ kṛtvā || tantram ity uktam ||
17.2.d: अथ नवम्याम् अपराह्णे वाहनानि स्नापयित्वा अहतवासा ब्रह्मा द्वादशमितां वेदिं कृत्वा ॥ तन्त्रम् इत्य् उक्तम् ॥
17.2.m: Then, on the ninth [lunar day] in the afternoon, having bathed the mounts, the brahman priest, wearing unwashed garments, having constructed an altar measuring twelve [cubits]—the sacrificial procedure has been explained.
Having sprinkled the mount three times with [the rite of] non-defilement of the propitiatory act, he should go around it.

17.2.s: niḥsālām iti sūktaṃ japan pratyetyābhiṣiñcayed enam ||
17.2.d: निःसालाम् इति सूक्तं जपन् प्रत्येत्याभिषिञ्चयेद् एनम् ॥
17.2.m: Whispering the hymn 'Out of the house…', having returned, he should consecrate it.
Having adorned the horse, provided it with a dappled neck, and caused it to stand near, he should give curds.

17.2.s: evam eva maiśradhānyāny udapātrāṇy antarāsu dikṣu ||
17.2.d: एवम् एव मैश्रधान्यान्य् उदपात्राण्य् अन्तरासु दिक्षु ॥
17.2.m: In the same manner, [he places] water-vessels with mixed grains in the intermediate directions.

17.2.s: tatraiva devatā yajet || agniṃ vāyuṃ varuṇam aśvināv iti ||
17.2.d: तत्रैव देवता यजेत् ॥ अग्निं वायुं वरुणम् अश्विनाव् इति ॥
17.2.m: Right there he should worship the deities: Agni, Vāyu, Varuṇa, and the Aśvins.
Having cooked a pot-offering in milk;

17.2.s: samās tvāgne tvaṃ no agne mā no vidann abhayair aparājitair āyuṣyaiḥ svastyayanair apratiratheneti ca hutvā saṃsthāpya ||
17.2.d: समास् त्वाग्ने त्वं नो अग्ने मा नो विदन्न् अभयैर् अपराजितैर् आयुष्यैः स्वस्त्ययनैर् अप्रतिरथेनेति च हुत्वा संस्थाप्य ॥
17.2.m: Having offered with [the hymns] 'Years for you, O Agni…', 'You to us, O Agni…', 'May they not find us…', with the fear-dispelling, undefeated, longevity-bestowing, prosperity-bringing, and irresistible [hymns], and having concluded;

17.2.s: agner ado 'sīty ahatavāsobhiḥ prachādya rasaiḥ kumbhān audumbarān pūrayitvā pratidiśam avasthāpya mamāgne varco abhayaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī ud uttamaṃ varuṇāśvinā brahmaṇā yātam iti juhuyāt ||
17.2.d: अग्नेर् अदो ऽसीत्य् अहतवासोभिः प्रछाद्य रसैः कुम्भान् औदुम्बरान् पूरयित्वा प्रतिदिशम् अवस्थाप्य ममाग्ने वर्चो अभयं द्यावापृथिवी उद् उत्तमं वरुणाश्विना ब्रह्मणा यातम् इति जुहुयात् ॥
17.2.m: Having covered them with unwashed garments with 'You are the food of Agni…', having filled jars of udumbara wood with juices and stationed them in each direction, he should offer oblation with 'My splendour, O Agni…', 'Freedom from fear, O Heaven and Earth…', 'Up to the highest, O Varuṇa…', [and] 'Come with sacred prayer, O Aśvins…'

17.2.s: paurṇamāsī prathameti ca juhuyād dundubhim āhanyād ity uktam ||
17.2.d: पौर्णमासी प्रथमेति च जुहुयाद् दुन्दुभिम् आहन्याद् इत्य् उक्तम् ॥
17.2.m: He should also offer oblation with 'The full moon is first…', and beat the war drum, as has been stated.

17.2.s: upa śvāsaya pṛthivīm iti tatraivānumantraṇaṃ ca ||
17.2.d: उप श्वासय पृथिवीम् इति तत्रैवानुमन्त्रणं च ॥
17.2.m: And right there [takes place] the recitation over [it] with 'Cause the earth to resound…'
And all musical instruments and mounts [are included].
[With the words] 'Delight the people…' he should establish the fifth [rite/image].

17.2.s: na taṃ yakṣmā aitu deva iti guggulakṣṭhadūpaṃ dadyāt ||
17.2.d: न तं यक्ष्मा ऐतु देव इति गुग्गुलक्ष्ठदूपं दद्यात् ॥
17.2.m: With the verses, "Let not consumption reach him, O god" and "Let the gods come," he should offer incense of bdellium and costus.

17.2.s: yas te gandhas tryāyuṣam iti bhūtiṃ prayacchet ||
17.2.d: यस् ते गन्धस् त्र्यायुषम् इति भूतिं प्रयच्छेत् ॥
17.2.m: With "Whatever fragrance of yours" and "Triple life-span," he should bestow ash [for protection].

17.2.s: dūṣyā dūṣir asīti pratisaram ābadhya ye purastād iti pratidiśaṃ kṣipet ||
17.2.d: दूष्या दूषिर् असीति प्रतिसरम् आबध्य ये पुरस्ताद् इति प्रतिदिशं क्षिपेत् ॥
17.2.m: Having tied on an amulet-cord with "You are an expeller, an expelling cord," he should cast [water] in each direction with "Those who in the east..."

17.2.s: bahir niḥsṛtyottareṇa gatvā bāhyenopaniṣkramya suhṛde kuryāc chraddadhate kuryād vāhanānām abhayaṃ karma ||
17.2.d: बहिर् निःसृत्योत्तरेण गत्वा बाह्येनोपनिष्क्रम्य सुहृदे कुर्याच् छ्रद्दधते कुर्याद् वाहनानाम् अभयं कर्म ॥
17.2.m: Having gone out, proceeded to the north, and stepped outside, he should perform for a friend, for one of faith, the security rite for the draft animals.

18.1.s: athāśvayuje māse paurṇamāsyām aparāhṇe hastinīrājanaṃ kuryāt ||
18.1.d: अथाश्वयुजे मासे पौर्णमास्याम् अपराह्णे हस्तिनीराजनं कुर्यात् ॥
18.1.m: Now, in the month of Aśvayuj, on the full-moon day in the afternoon, he should perform the waving of lights over the elephants.

18.1.s: prāgudakpravaṇe deśe yatra vā mano ramate ||
18.1.d: प्रागुदक्प्रवणे देशे यत्र वा मनो रमते ॥
18.1.m: In a place sloping towards the east or the north, or wherever the mind takes delight.

18.1.s: girayas te parvatā ity etayā hastaśatam ardhaṃ vā maṇḍalaṃ parigṛhya yābhir yajñam iti saṃprokṣet ||
18.1.d: गिरयस् ते पर्वता इत्य् एतया हस्तशतम् अर्धं वा मण्डलं परिगृह्य याभिर् यज्ञम् इति संप्रोक्षेत् ॥
18.1.m: Having demarcated a circular area of a hundred cubits or half [that] with the verse, "May your mountains and hills be snowy," he should consecrate it with "With which [they consecrate] the sacrifice."

18.1.s: daśahastasamutsedhaṃ pañcahastaṃ tu vistṛtam | śāntavrkṣamayaṃ kuryāt toraṇaṃ puṣṭivardhanama ||
18.1.d: दशहस्तसमुत्सेधं पञ्चहस्तं तु विस्तृतम् । शान्तव्र्क्षमयं कुर्यात् तोरणं पुष्टिवर्धनम ॥
18.1.m: "He should construct an archway made of propitious wood, ten cubits in height and five cubits in width, which promotes prosperity.

18.1.s: śuklaiḥ śuklāmbaradhvajair mālyaiś ca paribhūṣitam | kārayeta bile śubhre rasaiś ca paripūrite ||
18.1.d: शुक्लैः शुक्लाम्बरध्वजैर् माल्यैश् च परिभूषितम् । कारयेत बिले शुभ्रे रसैश् च परिपूरिते ॥
18.1.m: Decorated with white garlands and white flags, he should have it set in two clean post-holes filled with savors:

18.1.s: rasais tvām abhiṣiñcāmi bhūme mahyaṃ śivā bhava | asapatnā sapatnaghnī mama yajñavivardhanī ||
18.1.d: रसैस् त्वाम् अभिषिञ्चामि भूमे मह्यं शिवा भव । असपत्ना सपत्नघ्नी मम यज्ञविवर्धनी ॥
18.1.m: 'With savors I anoint you, O earth; be auspicious to me, free of rivals, slaying rivals, and furthering my sacrifice.'

18.1.s: imau stambhau ghṛtānvaktāv ubhau mā yaśasāvatāt | yo mā kaś cabhidāsati tam imau stambhau nirdahatām iti ||
18.1.d: इमौ स्तम्भौ घृतान्वक्ताव् उभौ मा यशसावतात् । यो मा कश् चभिदासति तम् इमौ स्तम्भौ निर्दहताम् इति ॥
18.1.m: "With the words: 'May both of these posts, smeared with ghee, protect me with renown; whoever attacks me, may these two posts consume him.'"

18.1.s: uc chrayasva imā yā brahmaṇaspata ity etābhyāṃ suvarṇamālā patākaiḥ stambhau saṃyojya ||
18.1.d: उच् छ्रयस्व इमा या ब्रह्मणस्पत इत्य् एताभ्यां सुवर्णमाला पताकैः स्तम्भौ संयोज्य ॥
18.1.m: Having joined the two posts with golden garlands and banners with these two verses, "Erect yourself" and "These [prayers] of Bṛhaspati,"

18.1.s: tasyādhastāc caturhastāṃ vediṃ kṛtvā darbhapavitrapāṇir baliṃ puṣpāṇi ca dattvā ||
18.1.d: तस्याधस्ताच् चतुर्हस्तां वेदिं कृत्वा दर्भपवित्रपाणिर् बलिं पुष्पाणि च दत्त्वा ॥
18.1.m: and having made an altar of four cubits beneath it, having a darbha-grass strainer in hand, and having presented an oblation and flowers;
having strewed around the fire with honey, parched grain, svastika-cakes, wheat porridge, curds, spiced rice-gruel, sweet cakes, milk rice, ghee, and diverse drinks, edibles, and fruits;

18.1.s: āpo asmān mātaraḥ sūdayantv iti caturaudumbarān kumbhān hradodakena pūrayitvā ||
18.1.d: आपो अस्मान् मातरः सूदयन्त्व् इति चतुरौदुम्बरान् कुम्भान् ह्रदोदकेन पूरयित्वा ॥
18.1.m: having filled four udumbara jars with lake-water with the verse, "May the waters, our mothers, cleanse us";

18.1.s: pratidiśam avasthāpya dadhyād raudrāgneyaṃ vāyavyaṃ vāruṇā mantrāḥ ||
18.1.d: प्रतिदिशम् अवस्थाप्य दध्याद् रौद्राग्नेयं वायव्यं वारुणा मन्त्राः ॥
18.1.m: and having placed them in each direction, he should place [them]; the mantras belong to Rudra, Agni, Vāyu, and Varuṇa.

18.1.s: rakṣoghnaṃ krtyādūśaṇaṃ yaśasyavarcasyāni ca hutvauṣadhīḥ samādāya dvihastaṃ maṇḍalam ity uktam ||
18.1.d: रक्षोघ्नं क्र्त्यादूशणं यशस्यवर्चस्यानि च हुत्वौषधीः समादाय द्विहस्तं मण्डलम् इत्य् उक्तम् ॥
18.1.m: Having offered [hymns that are] demon-slaying, witchcraft-destroying, renown-bestowing, and splendor-bestowing, and having gathered herbs, it is stated that the circular area is two cubits.

18.1.s: bṛhatkaṇṭārīkaṇṭakā lāghukaṇṭārikā smṛtāḥ | suvarṇapuṣpī śvetagiri karṇikā hy udisatrā ||
18.1.d: बृहत्कण्टारीकण्टका लाघुकण्टारिका स्मृताः । सुवर्णपुष्पी श्वेतगिरि कर्णिका ह्य् उदिसत्रा ॥
18.1.m: "The great kaṇṭārī, the thorned one, the small kaṇṭārikā are remembered, golden-flowered, white hill-ear-flower, and udisatrā,

18.1.s: siṃhī vyāghrī ca hariṇī hy amṛtā cāparājitā | pṛśniparṇī ca dūrvā ca padmam utpalamālinī ||
18.1.d: सिंही व्याघ्री च हरिणी ह्य् अमृता चापराजिता । पृश्निपर्णी च दूर्वा च पद्मम् उत्पलमालिनी ॥
18.1.m: siṃhī, vyāghrī, hariṇī, amṛtā, aparājitā, pṛśniparṇī, dūrvā grass, lotus, and water-lily."

18.2.m: Having set down a bamboo hoop, he should lay it down.
Having spread out the skin of a leopard, a tiger, or an ox;

18.2.s: tato yā syād adhidevatā tasyai baliṃ dattvā piṇḍāni ca dadyāt ||
18.2.d: ततो या स्याद् अधिदेवता तस्यै बलिं दत्त्वा पिण्डानि च दद्यात् ॥
18.2.m: then, having given an oblation to whichever tutelary deity it may be, he should also present balls of rice.

18.3.s: yasyāṃ diśi sa ripur bhavati tāṃ diśaṃ gatvā hastinam ānayed dhiraṇyena rajatena vajramaṇimuktādibhiḥ śaṅkhena candanena bhadradāruṇayā kuṣṭhena naladena rocanenāñjanena manahśilayā padmakumudotpalair ||
18.3.d: यस्यां दिशि स रिपुर् भवति तां दिशं गत्वा हस्तिनम् आनयेद् धिरण्येन रजतेन वज्रमणिमुक्तादिभिः शङ्खेन चन्दनेन भद्रदारुणया कुष्ठेन नलदेन रोचनेनाञ्जनेन मनह्शिलया पद्मकुमुदोत्पलैर् ॥
18.3.m: Having gone in whichever direction that enemy is, he should lead the elephant [forward] with gold, silver, diamond, pearls, and the like, with conch shell, sandalwood, cedar, costus, spikenard, yellow orpiment, collyrium, realgar, and with red and blue water-lilies.

18.3.s: mamāgne varca iti sūktaṃ dakṣinottaramakhaṃ pratijapet ||
18.3.d: ममाग्ने वर्च इति सूक्तं दक्षिनोत्तरमखं प्रतिजपेत् ॥
18.3.m: He should softly recite the hymn, "My splendor, O Agni," facing south-north towards the rite.
With the remainder, he should anoint its limbs.

18.3.s: hastināṃ rakṣaṇe daṇḍaḥ kartavyo vaiṇavo navaḥ | ṣoḍaśāratnimātras tu cāruparvamanaoramaḥ ||
18.3.d: हस्तिनां रक्षणे दण्डः कर्तव्यो वैणवो नवः । षोडशारत्निमात्रस् तु चारुपर्वमनओरमः ॥
18.3.m: "For protecting the elephants, a new bamboo staff should be made; it should measure sixteen cubits, pleasing and with lovely joints.

18.3.s: dantāgreṣu tṛṇāni kṛtvā yathā havyaṃ vahasi grasati ||
18.3.d: दन्ताग्रेषु तृणानि कृत्वा यथा हव्यं वहसि ग्रसति ॥
18.3.m: Having placed grasses at the tips of the tusks, with the verse, "As you carry the oblation," [the elephant] chews [them].
With the verse, "The well-born Jātavedas," he should kindle the fire.

18.3.s: sujātaṃ jātavedasam iti vācayed yathā havyam iti nīrājayitvā ||
18.3.d: सुजातं जातवेदसम् इति वाचयेद् यथा हव्यम् इति नीराजयित्वा ॥
18.3.m: He should cause [the priest] to recite "The well-born Jātavedas"; having waved lights with "As you [carry] the oblation,"
he should make [the elephant] enter the stable with "Bearing a treasure."

18.3.s: anapekṣamānāḥ svāni sthānāni vrajanti dīrghāyuṣo balavantaś ca bhavanti ||
18.3.d: अनपेक्षमानाः स्वानि स्थानानि व्रजन्ति दीर्घायुषो बलवन्तश् च भवन्ति ॥
18.3.m: Without looking back, they go to their stalls; they become long-lived and strong.
A thousand cows and an excellent village are the sacrificial fee for the officiant.

19.1.s: saṃbhṛteṣu saṃbhāreṣu brahmā rājā ca ubhau snātau ahatavasanau surabhisujātānulepanau karmaṇyau vratavantau upavasataḥ
19.1.d: संभृतेषु संभारेषु ब्रह्मा राजा च उभौ स्नातौ अहतवसनौ सुरभिसुजातानुलेपनौ कर्मण्यौ व्रतवन्तौ उपवसतः

19.1.s: vratavantau śvo bhūte śamnodevyāḥ pādair ardharcābhyām ṛcā ṣakṛtvodakaṃ pari vācam ācānto
19.1.d: व्रतवन्तौ श्वो भूते शम्नोदेव्याः पादैर् अर्धर्चाभ्याम् ऋचा षकृत्वोदकं परि वाचम् आचान्तो
19.1.m: 1.4. Having offered into the fire on the third [lunar day] with the hymn, "Great is Indra who by his might," with "To Indra, svāhā!" and so forth, and having worshipped the world guardians, touching the king, he should offer oblations as at the beginning, with: "Hitherward Indra," "Indra the good protector," "Increase this kṣatriya of mine, O Indra," and "Living for a hundred autumns."

19.1.s: arvāñcam indraṃ trātāram indram indraḥ sutrāmā imam indra vardhaya kṣatriyaṃ me hantāya vṛṣa indrasya indro jayāti iti ca hutvā rāṣṭrasaṃvargaiś cā
19.1.d: अर्वाञ्चम् इन्द्रं त्रातारम् इन्द्रम् इन्द्रः सुत्रामा इमम् इन्द्र वर्धय क्षत्रियं मे हन्ताय वृष इन्द्रस्य इन्द्रो जयाति इति च हुत्वा राष्ट्रसंवर्गैश् चा

19.1.s: atha indram utthāpayanti ā tvā ahārṣam antar dhruvādyaur viśas tvā sarvā vāñchantu iti sarvato 'pramattā dhārayerann
19.1.d: अथ इन्द्रम् उत्थापयन्ति आ त्वा अहार्षम् अन्तर् ध्रुवाद्यौर् विशस् त्वा सर्वा वाञ्छन्तु इति सर्वतो ऽप्रमत्ता धारयेरन्न्

19.1.s: adbhutaṃ hi savanānayet samutthitaṃ bhavati || yadi prācyām agnibhayam || yadi dakṣiṇasyāṃ yamabhayam || yadi pratīcyāṃ varuṇabhayam || yadi udīcyāṃ kṣudbhayam || yadi antardeśebhyobhayato vidyād
19.1.d: अद्भुतं हि सवनानयेत् समुत्थितं भवति ॥ यदि प्राच्याम् अग्निभयम् ॥ यदि दक्षिणस्यां यमभयम् ॥ यदि प्रतीच्यां वरुणभयम् ॥ यदि उदीच्यां क्षुद्भयम् ॥ यदि अन्तर्देशेभ्योभयतो विद्याद्

19.1.s: agnir mā pātu agniṃ te vasumantam ṛcchantv iti || yathāsvaliṅgaṃ dvābhyāṃ-dvābhyāṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ pratidiśam upasthāpayet ||
19.1.d: अग्निर् मा पातु अग्निं ते वसुमन्तम् ऋच्छन्त्व् इति ॥ यथास्वलिङ्गं द्वाभ्यां-द्वाभ्यां प्रदक्षिणं प्रतिदिशम् उपस्थापयेत् ॥

19.1.s: gṛdhraś ced asmin nipatati mṛtyor bhayaṃ bhavati || yad vā kṛṣṇaśakunir antarikṣrṇa patati iti japed yas tvā gṛdhraḥ kapota iti antato japet
19.1.d: गृध्रश् चेद् अस्मिन् निपतति मृत्योर् भयं भवति ॥ यद् वा कृष्णशकुनिर् अन्तरिक्ष्र्ण पतति इति जपेद् यस् त्वा गृध्रः कपोत इति अन्ततो जपेत्

19.1.s: śirobhaṅge tu rājānaṃ madhyabhaṅge tu mantriṇam | ādibhaṅge janapadaṃ mūlabhaṅge tu nāgarān ||
19.1.d: शिरोभङ्गे तु राजानं मध्यभङ्गे तु मन्त्रिणम् । आदिभङ्गे जनपदं मूलभङ्गे तु नागरान् ॥

19.1.s: indrāṭako yadā bhidyād rājakośo vilupyate | rajjuchede parijāte nṛpatis tu vinaśyati ||
19.1.d: इन्द्राटको यदा भिद्याद् राजकोशो विलुप्यते । रज्जुछेदे परिजाते नृपतिस् तु विनश्यति ॥

19.2.s: sāvitryā abhimantritaṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam āvartayed rājānam abhibhūr yajña iti etais tribhiḥ sūktair anvārabdhe rājani pūrṇahomaṃ juhuyāt ||
19.2.d: सावित्र्या अभिमन्त्रितं कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम् आवर्तयेद् राजानम् अभिभूर् यज्ञ इति एतैस् त्रिभिः सूक्तैर् अन्वारब्धे राजनि पूर्णहोमं जुहुयात् ॥

19.3.s: indradevatāḥ syur ye rājño bhṛtyāḥ syuḥ sarve dīkṣitā brahmacāriṇaḥ syur
19.3.d: इन्द्रदेवताः स्युर् ये राज्ञो भृत्याः स्युः सर्वे दीक्षिता ब्रह्मचारिणः स्युर्

19.3.s: indraṃ copasadya yajeran || trirātraṃ saptarātraṃ vā
19.3.d: इन्द्रं चोपसद्य यजेरन् ॥ त्रिरात्रं सप्तरात्रं वा

19.3.s: trir ayanam ahnām upatiṣṭhante havisā ca yajante ||
19.3.d: त्रिर् अयनम् अह्नाम् उपतिष्ठन्ते हविसा च यजन्ते ॥

19.3.s: āvṛta indram aham iti indra kṣatram iti haviṣo hutvā
19.3.d: आवृत इन्द्रम् अहम् इति इन्द्र क्षत्रम् इति हविषो हुत्वा

19.3.m: Now on the first lunar day of summer, having bathed with [the formula] "āyuṣyam" ("life-giving"), having plunged with the water hymns, having turned clockwise, and having touched water, [the rite] has been explained.

19.3.s: apāṃ sūktair āplutya pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya apa upaspṛśya anapekṣamāṇāḥ pratyetya brāhmaṇān bhaktyā yad īpsitaṃ varapradānaiḥ paritoṣayet ||
19.3.d: अपां सूक्तैर् आप्लुत्य प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्य अप उपस्पृश्य अनपेक्षमाणाः प्रत्येत्य ब्राह्मणान् भक्त्या यद् ईप्सितं वरप्रदानैः परितोषयेत् ॥

19.3.s: śvaḥśvo 'sya rāṣṭraṃ jyāyo bhavati eko 'syāṃ pṛthivyāṃ rājā bhavati na purā jarasaḥ pramīyate ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃvidvān indramaheṇa carati iti brāhmaṇam ||
19.3.d: श्वःश्वो ऽस्य राष्ट्रं ज्यायो भवति एको ऽस्यां पृथिव्यां राजा भवति न पुरा जरसः प्रमीयते य एवं वेद यश् चैवंविद्वान् इन्द्रमहेण चरति इति ब्राह्मणम् ॥
19.3.m: Now we shall explain the ritual ordinance for the king's great festival of Indra.

20.1.m: Now therefore we shall explain the ritual manual of the Rogue.
He should perform it regularly every four months, in the bright fortnights of Phālguna, Āṣāḍha, and Kārttika.

20.1.s: śvo bhūte ṣaṣṭhyām upavāsaṃ kṛtvā prāgudīcīṃ diśaṃ niṣkramya śucau deśe manohare noṣare maṇḍalaṃ trayodaśaratniṃ kṛtvā madhye maṇḍapasya sarvavānaspatyāṃ mālāṃ kṛtvā ghaṇṭāpatākāsrajaḥ pratisaraṃ ca mālāpṛṣṭhe kṛtvā madhye darpaṇāṃś copakalpayitvā tatra yaṃ vahanti hayāḥ śvetā ity āvāhayet ||
20.1.d: श्वो भूते षष्ठ्याम् उपवासं कृत्वा प्रागुदीचीं दिशं निष्क्रम्य शुचौ देशे मनोहरे नोषरे मण्डलं त्रयोदशरत्निं कृत्वा मध्ये मण्डपस्य सर्ववानस्पत्यां मालां कृत्वा घण्टापताकास्रजः प्रतिसरं च मालापृष्ठे कृत्वा मध्ये दर्पणांश् चोपकल्पयित्वा तत्र यं वहन्ति हयाः श्वेता इत्य् आवाहयेत् ॥
20.1.m:
On the next day, having fasted on the sixth lunar day, having gone out to the north-east direction, having made a circle of thirteen cubits in a clean, charming place that is not saline, having placed a garland made of all kinds of forest-trees in the middle of the pavilion, having placed bells, banners, garlands, and an amulet-cord behind the garland, and having arranged mirrors in the middle, he should invite [the deity] there with the verse: "Whom white horses bear..."

"Whom white horses bear, ever-yoked, swift as thought— / that Dhūrta clad in white armor do I invoke.

20.2.s: yaṃ vahanti hayāḥ śvetā nityayuktā manojavāḥ | tam ahaṃ śvetasaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
20.2.d: यं वहन्ति हयाः श्वेता नित्ययुक्ता मनोजवाः । तम् अहं श्वेतसंनाहं धूर्तम् आवाहयाम्य् अहम् ॥

20.2.s: yaṃ vahanti gajāḥ siṃhā vyāghrāś cāpi viṣāṇinaḥ | tam ahaṃ siṃhasaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
20.2.d: यं वहन्ति गजाः सिंहा व्याघ्राश् चापि विषाणिनः । तम् अहं सिंहसंनाहं धूर्तम् आवाहयाम्य् अहम् ॥
20.2.m: Whom elephants, lions, tigers, and horned beasts bear— / that Dhūrta clad in lion-armor do I invoke.

20.2.s: yaṃ vahanti mayūrāś ca citrapakṣā vihaṃgamāḥ | tam ahaṃ citrasaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
20.2.d: यं वहन्ति मयूराश् च चित्रपक्षा विहंगमाः । तम् अहं चित्रसंनाहं धूर्तम् आवाहयाम्य् अहम् ॥
20.2.m: Whom peacocks and birds with multicolored wings bear— / that Dhūrta clad in multicolored armor do I invoke.

20.2.s: yaṃ vahanti sarvavārṇāḥ sadāyuktā manojavāḥ | tam ahaṃ sarvasaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
20.2.d: यं वहन्ति सर्ववार्णाः सदायुक्ता मनोजवाः । तम् अहं सर्वसंनाहं धूर्तम् आवाहयाम्य् अहम् ॥
20.2.m: Whom [steeds] of all colors bear, ever-yoked, swift as thought— / that Dhūrta clad in all kinds of armor do I invoke.

20.2.s: yasyāmoghā sadā śaktir nityaṃ ghaṇtāpatākinī | tam ahaṃ śaktisaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
20.2.d: यस्यामोघा सदा शक्तिर् नित्यं घण्तापताकिनी । तम् अहं शक्तिसंनाहं धूर्तम् आवाहयाम्य् अहम् ॥
20.2.m: Whose spear is ever unfailing, constantly adorned with bells and banners— / that Dhūrta equipped with a spear do I invoke.

20.2.s: yaś ca mātṛgaṇair nityaṃ sadā parivṛto yuvā | tam ahaṃ mātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
20.2.d: यश् च मातृगणैर् नित्यं सदा परिवृतो युवा । तम् अहं मातृभिः सार्धं धूर्तम् आवाहयाम्य् अहम् ॥
20.2.m: And who is ever surrounded by the troops of Mothers, ever youthful— / that Dhūrta along with the Mothers do I invoke.

20.2.s: yaś ca kanyāsahasreṇa sadā parivṛto mahān | tam ahaṃ siṃhasaṃnāhaṃ dhūrtam āvāhayāmy aham ||
20.2.d: यश् च कन्यासहस्रेण सदा परिवृतो महान् । तम् अहं सिंहसंनाहं धूर्तम् आवाहयाम्य् अहम् ॥
20.2.m: And who is ever surrounded by a thousand maidens, the great one— / that [Dhūrta] clad in lion-armor do I invoke.

20.2.s: āyātu devaḥ sagaṇaḥ sasainyaḥ savāhanaḥ sānucaraḥ pratītaḥ | ṣaḍānano 'ṣṭādaśalocanaś ca suvarṇavarṇo laghupūrṇabhāsaḥ ||
20.2.d: आयातु देवः सगणः ससैन्यः सवाहनः सानुचरः प्रतीतः । षडाननो ऽष्टादशलोचनश् च सुवर्णवर्णो लघुपूर्णभासः ॥
20.2.m: May the god arrive with his host, with his army, with his mount, with his attendants, well-pleased, / six-faced and eighteen-eyed, golden-hued, of light and full brilliance.

20.2.s: āyātu devo mama kārttikeyo brahmaṇyapitraiḥ saha mātṛbhiś ca | bhrātrā viśākhena ca viśvarūpa imaṃ baliṃ sānucara juṣasva ||
20.2.d: आयातु देवो मम कार्त्तिकेयो ब्रह्मण्यपित्रैः सह मातृभिश् च । भ्रात्रा विशाखेन च विश्वरूप इमं बलिं सानुचर जुषस्व ॥
20.2.m: May my god Kārttikeya come, together with the Fathers devoted to Brahmā and with the Mothers, / and with his brother Viśākha, all-formed! Accept this offering along with your attendants!"
With the words "Seat yourself," he should have him sit down.
